title: Consulting Senior Associate - Technical Risk & Safety (Entry-level)
description:
As a Junior Consultant, you will support technical safety and risk projects by performing robust analysis, modelling, and calculations under the guidance of senior team members. This role offers exposure to diverse industries and projects, providing a strong foundation in safety engineering and risk management.

Why This Role Matter:
Shape Safer Operations Across Asia Pacific with ERM
Take on a role that shapes how industries operate safely and responsibly in a rapidly evolving region. You will influence critical decisions for global leaders, delivering expertise in process safety, HAZOP validation, SIL, and advanced risk modeling. Your work will go beyond compliance, creating strategies that protect lives, assets, and the environment while enabling sustainable growth. At ERM, every project is an opportunity to set new standards for safety and resilient to build a safer future for Asia Pacific.

What You Impact Is

You will help deliver high-quality work that drives impactful programs for our clients, while building strong relationships and contributing fresh ideas to evolve our services. Through collaboration and continuous learning, you will strengthen our culture and create opportunities that support long-term success for both clients and the firm.

Key Responsibilities

  • Assist in technical safety and risk projects involving risk analysis, modelling, and calculations.
  • Perform technically sound analysis based on defensible data and reasoned arguments.
  • Support development of Quantitative Risk Analysis (QRA) models using Excel spreadsheets.
  • Assist in fire and explosion modelling, gas and smoke dispersion modelling using CFD or empirical tools.
  • Conduct risk calculations (e.g., probability of events occurring) and non-flammable hazard analysis.
  • Contribute to Escape, Temporary Refuge, Evacuation and Rescue Analysis (ETRERA) for offshore facilities.
  • Participate in safety workshops (HAZID, HAZOP, ALARP) as a scribe and assist in client reporting.
  • Prepare sections of safety cases and high-quality reports with clear diagrams and explained calculations.
  • Support proposal preparation and attend client meetings as required
  • Ensure adherence to Health and Safety protocols in all project activities.

Qualifications & Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Master’s degree or professional registration is a plus).
  • 1–5 years in safety and risk analysis projects.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision and manage multiple tasks.
  • Commitment to safety and willingness to travel for project needs.

APAC Ready to Lead Way

At ERM, your work creates impact that matters, helping global organizations tackle the most pressing sustainability challenges while shaping a better future for communities and the environment. Our vision is to empower you to grow, lead, and innovate alongside world-class clients on transformative projects. We prioritize wellbeing, continuous learning, and an inclusive culture where collaboration, expertise, and purpose drive meaningful impact. At ERM, diverse perspectives are celebrated, and innovation thrives. If you’re ready to make sustainability your mission and build a career that creates lasting change, your journey starts here

You can apply for this role through Careers or through the internal careers portal if you are a current employee.

title: Network Engineer
description:
Position Title: Network Engineer Job Description

Summary: As a Network Engineer at iLearn Schools, you'll lead the design, support, and management of our network infrastructure across all sites and Internet connectivity. Your role is crucial in ensuring stable, cost-efficient, scalable, and secure solutions that align with ESL's architecture standards.

Compensation: Base $100,000-$130,000, Advanced Degree-Masters $3,000; PHD $5,000. Comprehensive Benefits: Health (Medical, Vision, Dental), Short Term Disability, AAE, & Pension

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and analytical skills.
  • Ability to work independently and manage priorities effectively.
  • Demonstrate the ability to effectively communicate orally and in writing, using proper grammar and vocabulary
  • Demonstrate working knowledge of the use of various technological software and equipment for tasks such as, but not limited to, word processing, data management, information retrieval, visual presentations, and telecommunications.
  • Understand the requirement to maintain confidentiality concerning charter school-related matters.
  • Ability to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with others contacted in the course of work; faculty etc.
  • Prior to employment, the following must be addressed:
  • Required to complete a criminal history background check to prove that the individual has not been convicted of a crime or a disorderly person's offense.
  • Provide evidence that health is adequate to fulfill the job functions and responsibilities with reasonable accommodation pursuant to 42 U.S.C. 12101 and in accordance with N.J.A.C. 6A:32-6.2.
  • Pass the state required Mantoux Intradermal Tuberculin Test as required by N.J.A.C. 6A:32-6.3.

Requirements/Environmental Conditions:

The physical demands and work environment factors described below are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Requires prolonged sitting or standing
  • Occasionally requires physical exertion to manually move, lift, carry, pull, or push objects or materials.
  • Requires the ability to work in noisy and crowded environments.
  • Occasionally requires stooping, bending, or reaching.
  • Requires some traveling.

Key Responsibilities: (The following description is illustrative of tasks and responsibilities. It is not meant to be all inclusive of every task or responsibility.)

  • Architect and maintain network infrastructure for stability, scalability, and security.
  • Plan and execute upgrades and routine maintenance for high availability and performance.
  • Lead hardware and software selection, implementation, and support.
  • Participate in iLearn Schools's Change Management System for system changes.
  • Collaborate with Information Security on DMZ networks and firewall configurations.
  • Ensure redundancy and backup processes for critical systems.
  • Manage yearly budgets for Network Services.
  • Provide technical consultation and support for corporate projects.
  • Maintain strong client relationships and ensure third-party vendors meet SLAs.

Required Skills & Experience:

  • CCNP-level Cisco certifications or 7+ years of large enterprise network management.
  • Strong routing and switching experience including L2/L3 protocols
  • Thorough understanding of OSI model and network technologies.
  • In-depth knowledge of Cisco, Meraki, and Palo Alto Networks devices.
  • Experience with Cisco Wireless LAN controllers and network security best practices.
  • Experience with Zoom(Zoom Room, VoIP and Zoom Meetings)
  • Customer service experience in a high-pressure environment.

title: RECREATION THERAPIST
description:
PRIMARY PURPOSE: Plan, schedule and implement activities for the treatment cottages consistent with the overall hospital mission. Develop and implement Recreation Therapy interventions for Hillside youth related to goals/ problem areas in the clinical record. Collaborate with multi- disciplinary treatment team to provide holistic approach to care.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

A. Provide Recreation Therapy services to Hillside clients that are therapeutic, safe, age-appropriate, creative, and culturally appropriate. Primary services will be delivered via groups addressing physical fitness, art, Leisure Education, social/life skills, DBT skills, Social Emotional Learning, and other areas deemed therapeutically relevant by RT clinical team.

B. Directly responsible for facilitation of RT services during school day, evening, and weekend hours. Assigned responsibilities for schedule modification necessary to accommodate campus needs.

C. Transport and supervise children involved in off-campus activities as necessary.

D. Coordinate the acquisition/inventory/maintenance of supplies and equipment as well as facilitate the use of Kids Club and movie/ game check out per department guidelines.

E. Responsible for the active direct supervision of all children assigned to his/her supervision as to their designated duties and responsibilities. Provide direction for developing and understanding an appreciation of the philosophy, function, and operation of the treatment program, as well as the structure and philosophy of service and treatment of Hillside.

F. Serve as a coach/ liaison for activity/ program planning for assigned cottages by collaborating with Cottage Supervisors, Lead Behavior Specialists, and direct care staff to develop opportunities that enhance cottage schedule.

G. Communicates and proactively seeks pertinent information on client behaviors, progress, and general concerns via Hillside email, participation in clinical rounds (2x per month for assigned cottages), and participation in scheduled staff meetings.

H. Participates in coordination and implementation of volunteer and on- campus special events as assigned by RT Director.

I. Perform all assigned duties in a safe manner by following Hillside policies and procedures. Ensure proper ESI techniques are adhered to when involved in physical interventions. Report all accidents/incidents in an expeditious manner. If involved in a work-related accident, follow the State of Georgia Worker’s Compensation Laws and Responsibilities and abide by the treating physician’s directions.

J. Responsible for completing a variety of paperwork on a daily basis. This paperwork includes, but is not limited to: progress notes, attendance records, special procedure observation forms, incident reports, Emergency Safety Intervention records or reports, treatment received, monthly summaries, documentation of school behaviors on child’s daily tracking sheet/progress notes, completion of crossover report and any area of concern in accordance with record documentation policies. Emphasis is placed on the neatness, correctness and timeliness of the paperwork. Required to understand and maintain the confidential nature of all children and facility related activities with emphasis on the sensitivity of the child’s records.

K. Ensure Hillside’s Accessibility Plan is adhered to by assuring the removal of barriers to the greatest extent possible that may hinder those served, staff and/or other stakeholders.

L. Perform other duties as deemed necessary by Management.

GENERAL COMPETENCIES:

Customer Focus

A. Promote positive image of Hillside with all contacts (customers)

B. Exhibit high quality of work

C. Contribute to development of a culture of care

Teamwork

A. Take the initiative to act on own

B. Demonstrate cooperation

C. Be a productive member of the staff

Communication

A. Communicate Effectively, clearly, and appropriately

B. Make use of supervision

C. Use excellent Judgment

CORE COMPETENCIES:

A. Plans therapeutically- driven experiential tasks that support Hillside’s mission and clinical foundation.

B. Facilitation of RT treatment services that support child/ adolescent growth and development as well as individualized clinical needs.

C. Completion of high- quality clinical documentation compliant with departmental guidelines.

D. Represents RT department as an engaged, professional, member of the multidisciplinary treatment team.

JOB SPECIFIC COMPETENCIES:

A. Creates activity plans that are diverse, address Social Emotional/ clinical/ departmental objectives, and have clear therapeutic goals.

B. Implement program services using a variety of activities, facilitation techniques, and methods of processing while providing strong leadership and coaching.

C. Ability to conduct formal and informal assessments and use findings to develop interventions and provide feedback via clinical summaries.

D. Serve as a liaison between department and treatment team for assigned cottages by attending team meetings for assigned cottages and providing/ receiving pertinent information to implement in program services.

title: Job Developer (CalWORKs)
description:
Job Description / Essential Elements

Job Developer (CalWORKs)

Rancho Santiago Community College District

Salary Range: Grade 12: $34.57 - $44.17

Job Type: Part Time

Job Number: CL26-01458

Location: 1530 W. 17th Street, Santa Ana, CA

Division: SAC Student Services

Closing: 9/18/2026 5:00 PM Pacific

POSITION DETAILS

About Rancho Santiago Community College District

https://rsccd.edu/Pages/default.aspx is one of the most established districts in the state and has been in operation for nearly 50 years. Located in the heart of Orange County, it is one of the largest of California's 72 community college districts, based on the number of credit and non-credit students. RSCCD encompasses 25 percent of Orange County's total area and serves a population of more than 700,000 residents in the communities of Anaheim Hills, Orange, Santa Ana, Villa Park, and portions of Anaheim, Costa Mesa, Irvine, Fountain Valley, Garden Grove, Tustin, and Yorba Linda. The district includes Santiago Canyon College and Santa Ana College, as well as the Centennial and Orange Continuing Education Centers, the Digital Media Center, the Joint Powers Fire Training Center, the Orange County Sheriff's Regional Training Academy, the College and Workforce Preparation Center, and the District Operations Center. RSCCD's three (3) auxiliary Foundations are actively involved in supporting both community and campus programs.

RSCCD's student population is a direct reflection of the diverse communities in the surrounding neighborhoods. As a whole, the district has the honor of serving approximately 55,537 students: 51% Hispanic/Latinx, 20% White, 9% Asian & Filipino, and 2% are African American. RSCCD is a proud Hispanic Serving Institution (HSI) and serves predominately historically underrepresented students. There is a commitment to foster student centered values among our employees to provide equitable student learning, academic excellence, and workforce development. By delivering high-quality educational programs and student support services, the district ensures that students have the appropriate resources to achieve their goals.

At RSCCD, our mission is to integrate diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility, and justice into all aspects of student academics and employee relations. Thus, creating transformational experiences that prepares students and employees to engage in the world with a renewed sense-of-self. Through this commitment, Rancho Santiago Community College District strives to cultivate a learning environment that prioritizes respect, to ensure that RSCCD stakeholders feel valued and supported throughout their academic and professional careers.

About the Position

The ideal candidate will demonstrate cultural competency in serving diverse community college populations, including faculty, management, and students from varied ethnic, racial, cultural, and socioeconomic backgrounds. This includes those with differing abilities, AB 540 students, DACA recipients, Foreign Residents, VACA participants, and Continuing Education students. They will support RSCCD's mission to promote self-awareness, knowledge, and communication skills, enabling all members of the college community to participate creatively and confidently in an ever-changing world.

Candidates will contribute to an inclusive and collaborative workplace culture that supports the diverse needs of faculty, management, staff, and students. They will effectively provide services and support to individuals with differing academic preparation levels and unique learning or workplace needs, ensuring equitable access and opportunities for success. Candidates should demonstrate cultural competency, sensitivity, equity-mindedness, and a commitment to anti-racism in all interactions and contributions. Through their role, they will empower students to achieve their educational and career goals while promoting a positive and inclusive environment where faculty and management can thrive, fostering creativity, confidence, and lifelong learning throughout the college community.

Class Summary

Under general direction, initiates contacts with private industry and the public sector for on-the-job training and to develop jobs for students who have completed vocational programs; provides information and training in job search skills for students in the California Works program; collects follow-up data on placement of students; performs related duties as required.

Representative Duties

Initiates contacts with employers by phone and in person to identify and develop work opportunities for students; provides occupational information to students; identifies and analyzes job duties to match the students capabilities and training; assists in preparation of students resumes and applications as appropriate; present workshops, attend job fairs, assist students in filling out applications and writing resumes; screens and refers qualified applicants for employment vacancies; assists students with interviewing and job search skills; completes activity logs of all employer and student contacts; may direct daily job club activities; assists in maintaining placement files for students and collects follow-up data on all placements.

Organizational Relationships

This classification reports to the designated manager/administrator and may lead and coordinate the work of clerical employees and student workers.

QUALIFICATIONS

Training and Experience

Any combination of training and/or experience equivalent to an Associate degree with course work in counseling, psychology, business and one year experience in employment interviewing and job placement or a related field.

Knowledge and Abilities

Good Knowledge of: the Internet and job databases such as JOBTRAK; local labor market information; job search skills; job development techniques; record keeping; various alternative programs (i.e., work study, work experience, internships).

Ability to: establish and maintain effective relationships with students and those contacted in the course of work; communicate effectively, both orally and in writing; be sensitive to students with special needs; work without close supervision; follow-up on leads on own initiative.

License or certification: valid California Motor Vehicle Operator's license.

Additional Qualifications

Candidate must demonstrate clear evidence of sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, ability, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, staff, and the community.

APPLICATION PROCESS

To ensure full consideration, all applicants must submit a complete Rancho Santiago Community College District online application that includes the items listed below by the position's closing date. Recruitment will review all applications for completeness, and only complete application packets will be forwarded to the screening committee for further review.

A Complete Application Packet Must Include the Following:

- RSCCD Online Application

- Resume - details all relevant education, training, and other work experience

- Academic Transcripts (Unofficial copies of undergraduate, graduate, and post-graduate transcripts).

Foreign Degrees

Transcripts from countries other than the United States must be evaluated by an agency that is approved by or a member of the National Association of Credentials Evaluation Service (http://www.naces.org/members.html) or the Association of International Credential Evaluators, Inc. (https://aice-eval.org/endorsed-members/), or Commission on Teacher Credentialing (https://www.ctc.ca.gov/credentials/leaflets/foreign-transcript-evaluation-(cl-635)).

Application Screening

Job announcements will include screening criteria to be used during screening and interviews. This may include, but is not limited to:

- Education experience (breadth and depth)

- Work experience (breadth and depth)

- Demonstrated ability to work cooperatively with others

- Bilingual ability (if needed)

- Demonstrated experience and sensitivity to diversity, equity, and inclusion.

- Professional growth activities

- Specialized skills training

- Leadership skills

- Written and/or oral communication skills

- Presentation

- Problem Solving.

Based on the information presented in the application materials, a limited number of candidates with qualifications most pertinent to the position will be invited to participate in the selection process, which may include a written test and an oral interview. Meeting the position's minimum requirements does not guarantee advancement in the selection process. Candidate qualifications will be assessed to determine those who meet and exceed requirements and are deemed the most competitive in the applicant pool.

Interview

Applicants selected for an interview may be required to take additional tests or assessments and will be notified of such prior to the date of the interview. During the oral session, those selected for interviews will, in addition to the above, also be evaluated on the following factors:

- Oral communication skills

- Presentation

- Problem-solving skills

A predetermined set of questions will be asked of all applicants interviewed. Applicants are requested to provide thorough yet concise information on their related experience to ensure the correct evaluation of their qualifications. Evaluation criteria will be applied consistently to all applicants.

Disability Accommodations

Individuals who require reasonable accommodations in the Application or Interviewing Process in accordance with ADA should notify the Recruitment Office in the Human Resources Division at least two days prior to the closing date, by calling (714) 480-7455.

Conditions of Employment

The selected candidate is required to complete the following before employment as part of the onboarding process:

- Present original documents for proof of eligibility to work in the United States.

- Provide a certificate of Tuberculosis Exam.

- Fingerprints (by a Live Scan Agency at the candidate's expense, and clearance must be received before the first day of employment)

EEO STATEMENT

The Rancho Santiago Community College District (RSCCD) is an equal opportunity employer. The policy of the District is to encourage applications from persons who are economically disadvantaged and individuals belonging to significantly underrepresented groups within the District's workforce, including ethnic and racial minorities, women, and persons with disabilities. No person shall be denied employment because of ethnicity or race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, veteran or military status, or political or organizational affiliation.

RSCCD will consider qualified applicants with a criminal history pursuant to the California Fair Chance Act. You do not need to disclose your criminal history or participate in a background check until a conditional employment offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if RSCCD is concerned about a conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.

title: Software Engineer, Program Analysis, Mobile Threat Analysis Platform
description:
Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

Our team builds security and privacy analysis infrastructure for Google Play and Android to detect malicious and abusive apps. Together with partner teams across Android, Ads, Chrome, Search and Cloud, we help Google protect users with safe experiences on our app platform and ecosystem.

This is a unique opportunity to be part of the team, which is responsible for building detection technologies to protect Android users from malware and abuse.

Android is Google’s mobile operating system powering more than 3 billion devices worldwide. Android is about bringing computing to everyone in the world. We believe computing is a super power for good, enabling access to information, economic opportunity, productivity, connectivity between friends and family and more. We think everyone in the world should have access to the best computing has to offer. We provide the platform for original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and developers to build compelling computing devices (smartphones, tablets, TVs, wearables, etc) that run the best apps/services for everyone in the world.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $147000 - $210000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.
  • Build automated runtime analysis platform at Google scale using cloud virtualization infrastructure.
  • Build full-stack solutions including app instrumentation, networking, app crawling, anti-cloaking, leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) where applicable, to build exceptional dynamic analysis-based detection and reverse-engineering solutions.
  • Work broadly with security, privacy and abuse engineering and product teams to land impact protecting Android and Play users against malware and all kinds of mobile threats.
  • Design and build Google-scale automations to scan Android apps with dynamic analysis.
  • Collaborate with other teams in the organization and Google to deliver impact.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 2 years of experience with software development in C++ or Python.
  • Experience with program analysis.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science or a related technical field.
  • 2 years of experience with performance, large scale systems data analysis, visualization tools, or debugging.
  • 2 years of experience with data structures and algorithms in either an academic or industry setting.
  • Experience with security or privacy.
  • Experience with static or dynamic analysis.
  • Experience with Android security or privacy.

title: Workforce Development Coordinator
description:
Education & Workforce Development Coordinator (Family Shelter & Housing Program)

Some people just need a place to sleep. Others need a path—one step at a time—back to safety, stability, and independence.

As our Education & Workforce Development Coordinator, you’ll design and deliver empowering learning programs for adults and teenagers living in a family residential shelter and for families transitioning into permanent housing. You’ll help residents build the practical skills, confidence, and community connections they need to secure lasting stability—through a trauma-informed, age-appropriate approach that meets people where they are.

If you’re passionate about education as a tool for resilience, and you thrive in environments where relationships matter as much as outcomes, we want to hear from you.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop and implement learning tracks for adults and teens, tailored to age-specific needs and developmental stages.
  • Create trauma-informed personal development curricula covering:
    • Personal care, household management, communication, and community navigation
    • Financial literacy and budgeting
    • Employment readiness and job search strategies
    • Housing readiness, apartment hunting, and maintaining tenancy
    • Parenting skills and self-advocacy
  • Lead weekly life skills classes for shelter residents and participants in our housing program.
  • Facilitate teen-focused sessions that support academic success, career exploration, healthy relationships, and future planning.
  • Conduct initial and ongoing life skills assessments, then build individualized plans based on goals and needs.
  • Work closely with case managers to align your programming with each family’s housing and service plan.
  • Provide follow-up support as families transition to permanent housing—monitor progress, adjust programming, and maintain documentation.
  • Build and strengthen community partnerships with employers, training programs, and educational institutions.
  • Coordinate guest speakers, field trips, workshops, and resource connections (GED, job training, mental health services, and more).
  • Maintain accurate records and help track program effectiveness through reports and documentation.

Who You Are

You bring:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Human Services, Education, or a related field (required)
  • 2+ years of experience working with homeless populations or in residential settings
  • Experience designing and facilitating educational programming for adults and/or youth
  • A solid understanding of trauma-informed care and the barriers families face (housing discrimination, employment hurdles, system navigation)
  • Strong group facilitation and communication skills, with the ability to connect with diverse individuals—including those facing mental health challenges, disabilities, or other barriers
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and database management
  • A valid driver’s license and reliable transportation

Bonus points if you have:

  • A Master’s degree
  • Experience with family homelessness or emergency shelter programs
  • Background in adult education or youth development
  • Certifications related to life skills, financial counseling, or job readiness
  • Experience building community-based programming and resources

The Impact

In this role, your work will directly contribute to:

  • Stronger housing readiness and long-term stability
  • Increased employment preparedness and self-advocacy
  • Improved family confidence, goal-setting, and daily-life independence
  • Better alignment between education programming and housing case plans

Working Conditions

  • Primarily based in the family shelter facility, with outreach and programming in community settings
  • Some evening hours required
  • Fast-paced environment with real-world challenges, including family crises and mental health situations
  • Close collaboration with shelter staff, case managers, housing specialists, and community partners

Ready to Help People Build a Future?

If you’re energized by meaningful work that blends education, empowerment, and practical support—apply today and help families move from crisis to stability, one skill at a time.

title: Instructional Technology Facilitator (Secondary)
description:
General Definition of Work:

The Instructional Technology Facilitator (ITF) champions the integration of technology in educational settings, aligning efforts with the ISTE Standards, North Carolina Digital Learning and Media Inventory (NCDLMI), and current educational best practices. This role involves leading, supporting, and pioneering the adoption of digital tools and learning models to enhance instruction and student achievement in a school setting.

Essential Functions

  • Leadership and Vision: Collaborate with administrative and teaching staff to cultivate and implement a strategic vision for digital learning, ensuring alignment with ISTE Standards and the North Carolina Digital Learning Plan. Spearhead initiatives that integrate computational thinking and digital citizenship across the curriculum
  • Professional Development: Design and facilitate professional learning opportunities that empower educators to integrate technology into their instructional practices effectively, focusing on improving student engagement and learning Provide ongoing coaching and support for educators to support the sustainability of technology integration and practices through professional learning communities (PLC) or one on one coaching. Coaching should be in alignment and supportive of the district’s strategic plan and the school’s improvement plan.
  • Curriculum Support and Development: Aid in the development, evaluation, and enhancement of technology-enriched learning experiences that comply with state standards, stimulate creativity, promote problem-solving skills, and advance digital literacy among Support and monitor the implementation of core instructional practices including but not limited to the CCS Instructional Frameworks, Science of Reading, Mathematical Practice and Concepts, etc.
  • Digital Learning Environment Management: Oversee the selection and utilization of educational technology tools and resources, advocating for equitable access to technology and digital content for all students and fostering an inclusive learning environment.
  • Data-Driven Practice: Employ data from the NCDLMI and other relevant sources to guide instructional technology initiatives, evaluate the impact of technology integration, and support evidence-based decision-making at the school level. Collaborate with educators to leverage data to inform instructional decisions, personalize learning experiences, and monitor student progress towards mastery of state standards and learning objectives. Manage, analyze, and utilize student data in order to assist school teams in making core instructional decisions.
  • Community and Global Collaboration: Encourage and facilitate collaboration among students, educators, and the global community through digital platforms, nurturing global awareness and cultural understanding.
  • Digital Citizenship Advocacy: Model and advocate for responsible and ethical use of technology, educating students and staff on digital citizenship principles to ensure a respectful and secure online learning environment that aligns with district and state privacy policies.


Qualification Requirements

  • Education and Experience: Bachelor’s Degree in Education, Instructional Technology, or related field, with preferred experience in educational technology.
  • Certifcations and Skills: Profciency in contemporary educational technologies and digital platforms, with a thorough understanding of the ISTE Standards, North Carolina Digital Learning Plan, and Exceptional interpersonal, communication, and presentation abilities, with a knack for collaborative work.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and coach adult learners, fostering professional growth and promoting an engaging learning.
  • Physical Requirements: Capable of managing digital learning spaces and occasionally handling tech equipment up to 10 pounds.
  • Special Requirements: Must possess or be eligible for relevant professional certifcations, such as the North Carolina Teaching Endorsement in K-12 Computer Education or Instructional Technology Specialist-Computers.

Physical Requirements:
• This work requires the occasional exertion of up to 10 pounds of force.
• Work regularly requires speaking or hearing, using hands to finger, handle or feel and repetitive motions, frequently requires sitting and occasionally requires standing, walking, stooping, kneeling, crouching or crawling, reaching with hands and arms, pushing or pulling and lifting.
• Work has standard vision requirements.
• Vocal communication is required for expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word.
• Hearing is required to perceive information at normal spoken word levels.
• Work requires preparing and analyzing written or computer data, operating machines, operating motor vehicles or equipment and observing general surroundings and activities.
• Work occasionally requires exposure to outdoor weather conditions.
• Work is generally in a moderately noisy location (e.g. business office, light traffic).

Special Requirements
• Must hold or have the ability to attain a North Carolina Teaching Endorsement in K-12 Computer Education or Instructional Technology Specialist-Computers.

title: Data Integration Engineer
description:
EAST CENTRAL INDEPENDENT SCHOOL DISTRICT

Job Announcement

Data Integration Engineer

The position of Data Integration Engineer will be available immediately at East Central ISD. All individuals (district employees included) who are interested in this position must apply online through Frontline via the district website. The deadline for submitting an application is until the position is filled.

PRIMARY PURPOSE: The Data Integration Engineer will serve as the point-of-contact and provider of district-level technology support for data imports, management, and exports using SQL Server, MS Access, Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, and various file transfer protocols. The Data Integration Engineer will provide database services to the district staff using student and staff databases from various applications providing the proper conversion techniques in a timely manner. The position is the Clever district administrator, providing support for the data in the Clever portal and its supported/related applications. The Data Integration Engineer is the champion of securing district data.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES/DUTIES:

  1. Create, maintain and optimize Microsoft Access databases.
  2. Maintain, update, and administer access for database servers, applications, and data, including imports and exports.
  3. Maintain, update, and administer access for Microsoft, Cerberus, WinSCP, and other FTP servers, FTP applications, and data, including data transfers in and out of the District.
  4. Provide timely data services to the Curriculum Department in a manner that meets all TEA and assessment deadlines with time to spare.
  5. Design and implement processes and procedures to reduce and eliminate database outages and downtime.
  6. Implement data backup and recovery procedures to prevent the loss of data from all types of failure.
  7. To document, plan and test disaster recovery (DR) procedures.
  8. Design, implement, and maintain database security strategies that provide the appropriate level of security for users and applications.
  9. Develop and maintain an annual calendar of submissions to facilitate advanced planning.
  10. Document all filters, queries, and conversions developed. Store copies of documentation and converters in multiple locations.
  11. Assist the district and campus assessment staff in extracting data from the district's applications in a timely manner for adjusting instruction.
  12. Be on call for all district staff needing database services using the priorities given by the Director of Technology.
  13. Support technicians with the data components of their duties.
  14. Assist, monitor, and train data staff with user creation, update, deletion, and management services to the district staff.
  15. Monitor and maintain the district's user databases, including integration/synchronization with active directory, google, and more in collaboration with the Server and Network team members.
  16. Provide support with applications in Eduphoria, including managing permissions, issues with uploads, troubleshooting, etc.
  17. Maintain skill and knowledge levels on the latest releases of all of the district's databases, plus related servers, software, and applications.
  18. Attend and study materials and resources provided by the district in a timely manner and pass the related certification examinations to keep certifications updated to the latest versions as directed by the Technology Director.
  19. Create and continuously update a plan for training related to current and future data needs.
  20. Collaborate with vendors in a timely and transparent manner as approved by the Director of Technology.
  21. Document database activities, configurations, and procedures regularly with copies in multiple locations and in a manner that can be used easily by other staff.
  22. To organize, review and negotiate data sharing and privacy agreements (DPA/DSA's) with partners and vendors.
  23. Assist other technicians as needed or when caught up on work orders, including serving as a mentor and assisting with managing the IT shop.
  24. Maintain confidentiality of student and staff information.
  25. Complete work as indicated by the Director of Technology or the ticket priority, in that order.
  26. Other duties as assigned.

NOTE: Not all applicants will be interviewed. Each applicant's resume, application and other available information will be considered in the screening process. Only those persons currently meeting all of the minimum requirements will be considered.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Education/Certification:

Bachelor's Degree or higher required

Clever Administrator Certification

Extensive training in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office with emphasis on MS Access, MS Excel, and Google Sheets.

Special Knowledge/Skills:

Experience using Microsoft Access with advanced queries required

Experience building and maintaining Microsoft Access applications with Switchboard required

Experience using Microsoft Access with online and offline ODBC database required

Experience with batch files, PowerShell, Google Meet, Jabber, and advanced data query functionality in Google Sheets preferred

Advanced knowledge of computer technology used in school settings, including data gathering, export, and analysis required

Superior organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills

EQUIPMENT USED: Personal computer equipment, service tools, technology websites, motor vehicles, and phone

WORKING CONDITIONS: Mental Demands/Physical Demands/Environmental Factors: Maintain emotional control under stress; work with frequent interruptions. Frequent standing, stooping, bending, kneeling, pushing, and pulling, carrying and running. Frequent light lifting and carrying (less than 15 pounds); occasional heavy lifting (45 pounds or over) and lifting and moving equipment. Work inside and outside (exposure to sun, heat, and inclement weather); exposure to noise; exposure to biological hazards. Frequent use of small hand tools and electronic test equipment; Frequent district-wide travel. Regular occasions of prolonged and irregular hours. Normal classroom/office environments, and work around electrical energy.

WORK LOCATION/FLEXIBILITY: While priority will be given to standard, onsite work arrangements, the district may consider remote/hybrid work arrangements for Texas residents living beyond a reasonable commute distance. All candidates must still meet all job responsibilities, service expectations, security requirements, and availability for on-site meetings, project work, training, and other district needs.

title: Werkvoorbereider E Property Management
description:
32-40 uur | Standplaats Vianen | Werkzaam op locatie Rijswijk | Hanab Installation Technology

Jij bent de spin in het web tussen voorbereiding en realisatie

Als Werkvoorbereider E Projecten ben jij degene die ervoor zorgt dat een project niet alleen op papier klopt, maar ook op de bouwplaats soepel verloopt. Je vertaalt een opdracht naar een concreet, uitvoerbaar plan: van werktekeningen en materiaallijsten tot planning en contractbewaking. Zonder jouw voorbereidend werk staat de uitvoering stil. Met jouw werk loopt alles op rolletjes.

Je gaat werken aan toonaangevende projecten waar jij het verschil in gaat maken, onder andere binnen commerciële vastgoedomgevingen en de zorgsector: projecten waar techniek, precisie en samenwerking er echt toe doen.

Wat ga je concreet doen?

Geen dag is hetzelfde, maar dit zijn de bouwstenen van jouw werk:

  • Voorbereiden en instrueren: je stelt heldere werkinstructies op zodat de uitvoerende collega's precies weten wat er moet gebeuren.
  • Materiaal en logistiek: je trekt de benodigde materialen uit, plant en bestelt materiaal en diensten van onderaannemers, en houdt zicht op levertijden en prijzen.
  • Tekeningen en techniek: je controleert (sparings)tekeningen, verzorgt werktekeningen en zorgt voor een volledige, eenduidige opdrachtbeschrijving.
  • Contractbeheer: je bewaakt lopende (onderhouds)contracten en verzorgt de calculaties bij wijzigingen.
  • Formaliteiten die ertoe doen: je maakt garantiedocumenten op en verstuurt deze naar de fabrikant, en regelt vergunningen en andere vereiste documenten.
  • Meedenken over het grotere geheel: je signaleert kansen voor extra werkzaamheden en denkt actief mee over totaaloplossingen voor de klant.

Je bent hét aanspreekpunt voor de contractbeheerder, onderaannemers, leveranciers en het projectteam. Jij bewaakt de voortgang en zorgt dat kwaliteit en planning hand in hand gaan.

Hoe ziet je werkweek eruit?

Ongeveer 80% van je tijd werk je vanaf kantoor aan de voorbereiding, planning en administratie. De overige 20% ben je op de bouw of het project zelf, om met eigen ogen te zien hoe jouw voorbereiding tot leven komt en om kort te schakelen met de mensen op locatie.

Het team

Je komt terecht in een gezellig, multicultureel en inclusief team, waar collega's elkaar makkelijk weten te vinden en waar ruimte is voor eigen inbreng. De lijnen zijn kort en de deuren staan letterlijk open, ook die van het management.

Wat breng jij mee?

  • MBO/HBO werk- en denkniveau in elektrotechniek of een vergelijkbare richting.
  • Bij voorkeur minimaal 3 jaar relevante werkervaring als werkvoorbereider binnen de installatiebranche.
  • Kennis van contractbeheer en het vermogen om processen efficiënt te begeleiden.
  • Je schakelt moeiteloos tussen verschillende niveaus en weet een team op een prettige manier aan te sturen.
  • Goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal, in woord en geschrift.

Wat biedt Hanab jou?

  • Een informele, collegiale werksfeer binnen een platte organisatie.
  • Volop ruimte voor persoonlijke ontwikkeling en doorgroeimogelijkheden.
  • Salaris tussen €3.152 en €5.652 bruto per maand, afhankelijk van ervaring.
  • Telefoon, laptop en gereedschap van de zaak.
  • Uitstekende secundaire voorwaarden: een goede pensioenregeling, 25 vakantiedagen, 13 ADV-dagen en een leasefietsregeling.
  • Aandacht voor gezondheid en welzijn: gratis deelname aan sportevenementen zoals Limburgs Mooiste, padeltoernooien en hardloopwedstrijden.

Laten we kennismaken!

Herken jij jezelf in deze rol en wil je onderdeel worden van een team waar jouw voorbereidend werk het verschil maakt op de bouwplaats? Solliciteer direct.

Heb je inhoudelijke vragen? Bel of WhatsApp met Peter via +31651671451

Let op: wanneer bureaus ongevraagd een kandidaat voorstellen, kunnen hier geen rechten aan worden ontleend. Hanab behoudt zich het recht voor om zelf een keuze te maken en de verdere selectieprocedure te volgen. Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

  • Evaluate, onboard, and manage cybersecurity vendors and third-party service providers to ensure compliance with district security standards and service level agreements.
  • Maintain comprehensive documentation regarding security incidents, policies, and disaster recovery procedures.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS AND ABILITIES

BASIC REQUIREMENTS

Approximately 80% of the role is dedicated to the administration, reporting, compliance, coordination, and writing support associated with government grants from city, county, state, and federal sources. This may include drafting or contributing to grant applications, proposals, reports, and other funder materials in partnership with the Director of Government Funding & Partnerships and other internal stakeholders. The remaining time (less than 20%) provides administrative and project support to External Affairs staff and leadership in advancing broader fundraising and engagement priorities.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities:

Grant Administration & Reporting

• Maintain a comprehensive calendar of public grant application and reporting deadlines
• Oversee entry of deadlines, files, and reporting metrics of all government, federal, and state grants into Salesforce and other platforms as needed.
• Maintain accurate records of government grant portal credentials for application and reporting purposes
• Collaborate with the Evaluation and Quality Improvement (EQI) team to gather quantitative data and complete funder reports
• Create and maintain reporting infrastructure with program leadership and staff to gather qualitative data for reporting.
• Work with the Finance team to secure financial data and prepare financial reports
• Facilitate and submit required reports and documentation in partnership with program, evaluation, and finance staff.
• Support Compliance Officer with tasks related to program audits and accreditation.
• Maintain a library of agency documents and data necessary for desk audits.
• Create and maintain an organized library of agency documents and program Memoranda of Understanding that can be tailored to specific schools and/or districts.
• Monitor progress of funding proposals post-submission to ensure compliance with all required procedures and deadlines.

Grant Prospecting and Writing

• Research and identify public funding opportunities at the city, county, state, and federal levels.
• Draft and contribute to government grant applications, proposals, reports, and other funder materials in coordination with the Director of Government Funding & Partnerships and program, evaluation, and finance staff.

Team & Administrative Support
• Provide administrative support to the External Affairs team staff and leadership as needed.
• Maintain accurate and timely public funding opportunity, award, deadline, and reporting information in Salesforce and other relevant systems.
• Perform other duties as assigned.

title: Partner Solutions Architect , ANZ-PS
description:
As a Partner Solutions Architect at Amazon Web Services (AWS), you’ll build technical relationships with partners of all sizes. You'll operate as their trusted advisor, ensuring a great partner experience with AWS and most importantly, for our customers.

You’ll manage the overall technical relationship between AWS and our partners, helping them to support our customers by making recommendations on security, cost, performance, reliability, and operational efficiency to accelerate our customer’s challenging, mission-critical projects. Internally, you are the voice of the partner, sharing their needs and wants to inform the roadmap of AWS features and partner program improvements. In this role, your creative thinking will link technology to solutions. You will help partners deliver on our shared goal to transform the experience of citizens who interact with all levels of Government, Education and Health.

You will participate in the creation and sharing of best practices, technical content, and new reference architectures (e.g. white papers, code samples, blog posts). You'll evangelise and educate partners about AWS technology (e.g. through workshops, user groups, meet-ups, public speaking, online videos, or conferences).

If you can educate AWS customers and partners about the art of the possible, while challenging the impossible, come build the future with us. As a public sector Solutions Architect within AWS, you can help shape and deliver on a strategy to build mind share and broad use of AWS cloud services across our partners and within strategic customers.

A day in the life
Solutions Architects are part of the sales organisation. They meet with partners to understand their business and technical challenges, crafting solutions that leverage AWS products and services. To position the best solutions with partners, a portion of their time is dedicated to learning and experimentation with the latest technologies.

About the team
Solutions Architects are technical “thought leaders” who evangelise emerging technologies on a conceptual and practical level. Our SAs play a critical role in the adoption and advancement of cloud computing capabilities within the public sector. They think outside the box to provide solutions that are cost-effective, time-saving, and secure. As an SA, you’ll solve problems at both the mission and technical levels by working backwards from partner requirements.

title: Technology Specialist
description:
The Orleans Southwest Supervisory Union is seeking a dynamic Technology Specialist. The successful candidate will have the following. The position is full-time, year-round, and comes with excellent benefits and generous paid time off. 

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:
-Can troubleshoot & resolve basic tech issues.

-Knowledge and experience with the use and support of software applications, especially Google Suite for Education.

title: Licensed Bus Operator
description:
Under the direction of the Supervisor, Transportation, the Licensed Bus Operator provides best-in-class safe, professional, and efficient transportation service to internal and external guests aboard passenger buses. Delivers exceptional quality service in alignment with brand standards/expectations for all guests– requiring a high level of professionalism, anticipatory service, and enthusiasm focusing on guest comfort. Contributes by creating a positive and productive working environment for patrons and employees. Maintains a positive attitude and public image while delivering authentic greetings, and cordial farewells, centered on a sense of personal service.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Is responsible for operating passenger vehicles abiding by all federal and state passenger carrier regulations. Expertly operates vehicles with extreme care and attention to detail ensuring safe passenger transportation. Exhibits exceptional display of enthusiasm for service and desire to deliver passengers to and from assigned destinations based on specific time schedules. Consistently maintains traffic and weather condition awareness to avoid seen and unseen road hazards. Responsible for identifying any in-operation mechanical malfunctions to ensure the safe transportation of guests. Operates ADA-accessible lift when needed. Professionally relays operational updates via radio communication, including but not limited to road hazards, unsafe traffic and environment conditions, location, load status, and estimated arrival and departure times.
2. Strictly adheres to all Federal Department of Transportation and California State rules and regulations that govern passenger carriers. Exercises maximum regard for all transported guests safety and welfare during vehicle operation. Completes federally mandated pre-and post-trip inspections to ensure vehicle compliance established by the Department of Transportation. Up to date with the ever-changing vehicle out-of-service criteria, set forth by North American Standard Out-Of-Service Criteria. Reports any condition of concern to leadership regarding vehicle issues/defects that may affect driver and passenger/guest safety. In the event of an accident, Drivers are responsible for safely removing passengers onboard the bus. Abides by all rules and regulations stated in California commercial driver handbook. Responsible for reporting all accidents, vehicle damage, and passenger safety situations and concerns to appropriate parties.
3. Handles all guest interactions with the highest level of hospitality and professionalism, accommodating special requests whenever possible; assists guests in all inquiries in connection with resort and casino services, hours of operations, key resort and casino personnel, and in-house events.
4. Maintains a neat and clean working environment by sweeping out vehicles, cleaning up spills, disposing of trash, and cleaning windows/mirrors for visibility.
5. Performs other duties as assigned to support the efficient operation of the department.

EDUCATIONAL, EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • High School Diploma or GED required.

  • Minimum three (3) years of commercial driving experience required.

  • Minimum five (5) years equivalent combination of route delivery driver, including but not limited to, postal driving, medical transport, and delivery of goods and services required.

  • Related, relevant, and/or direct experience may be considered in lieu of minimum educational requirements indicated above.

  • Must be 21 years of age or older.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSA)

  • School pupil activity bus (SPAB) certificate preferred.

  • Advanced vehicle operations knowledge and intermediate maintenance experience preferred.

REQUIRED LICENSES, CERTIFICATIONS AND REGISTRATIONS

  • At the discretion of the San Manuel Tribal Gaming Commission, you may be required to obtain and maintain a gaming license.

  • Select One of the Following for Driving Responsibilities: Authorized Driver: Role requires operation or driving of Tribe-owned vehicles or driving patron vehicles. A valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record as determined by the insurance carrier is required.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS/ WORKING CONDITIONS – ENVIRONMENT

The physical demands and working environment described here are representative of those that an employee encounters and must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

  • Primary work environment is in a climate-controlled office setting.

  • Work requires travel to attend meetings, trade shows, and conferences.

  • Incumbents may be required to work evening, weekend and holiday shifts.

  • Must be able to work in a fast-paced, high-demand environment.

  • Strength sufficient to exert up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects and/or move up to 40 pounds occasionally.

  • Sedentary work: involves sitting most of the time. Constantly operates a computer and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, and computer printer.

  • Physical activities that apply to the essential functions of the position are balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, reaching, pushing, pulling, lifting, grasping, talking, hearing, and repetitive motions.

  • Hearing sufficient to hear conversational levels in person, via videoconference and over the telephone.

  • Speech sufficient to make oneself heard and understood in person, in front of groups, in meetings, via videoconference and over the telephone.

  • Visual acuity that meets the requirements of the position: The worker is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as preparing and analyzing data and figures; transcribing; viewing a computer terminal; expansive reading and visual inspection of employees, visitors or facility.

  • Mobility sufficient to safely move in an office environment, walk, stoop, bend and kneel, and enter, exit and operate a motor vehicle in the course of travel to promotional events, meetings, conferences, trade shows and San Manuel properties.

  • Endurance sufficient to sit, walk and stand for extended periods, and maintain efficiency throughout the entire work shift and during extended work hours.

  • The employee may be exposed to fumes or airborne particles including secondhand smoke.

Reasonable accommodation will be made in compliance with all applicable law.

As one of the largest private employers in the Inland Empire, San Manuel deeply cares about the future, growth and well-being of its employees. Join our team today!

title: Website Administrator
description:

title: Business Systems Analyst - Process Automation
description:
IRVING INDEPENDENT SCHOOL DISTRICT

BUSINESS SYSTEMS ANALYST - PROCESS AUTOMATION

JOB DESCRIPTION

JOB TITLE: Business Systems Analyst - Process Automation

WAGE/HOUR STATUS: Exempt

FUNDING SOURCE: Local

REPORTS TO: Director of Information Systems

DEPARTMENT: Information Systems and Servers

DATE REVISED: 7/22/2026

PRIMARY PURPOSE: The Business Systems Analyst - Process Automation makes the District's applications work for the people who depend on them: learning how a department operates, asking the right questions, and turning the answer into a configured, tested, well-documented workflow, form, or integration. The deep specialty is the District's Laserfiche electronic content management (ECM) platform and the business-process automation that runs on it: the forms, approvals, records, and workflows that move work between systems. This is also a generalist analyst who can step into any District system (student, HR, or finance), learn it quickly, and give users and owners a clear answer.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Minimum Education/Certification:

  • A bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience and a track record of delivering student or business solutions.
  • Laserfiche Certified Professional credentials preferred, particularly the Process Automation path (Forms and Workflow) and/or Certified Administrator, or the ability to obtain within twelve months of hire.

Special Knowledge/Skills:

  • Proficiency administering the Laserfiche application platform (repository, security, templates, and user/role provisioning).
  • Demonstrated skill building Laserfiche Forms and Workflows, both automated and human-task.
  • Strong SQL and relational database design, with hands-on integration and ETL between Laserfiche and SIS/ERP systems (e.g., Tyler Munis, PowerSchool eSchoolPlus) and report/query development.
  • Command of the software development lifecycle and business-analysis methodology: requirements elicitation, current-state/future-state process mapping, SDLC, QA/UAT, and change-and-release management.
  • Adaptability: ramps on unfamiliar systems fast and translates fluently between business needs and technical solutions.
  • Strong project-management, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with clear written and verbal communication and the persistence to deliver under deadline and pressure.
  • Working knowledge of student/staff data privacy and security.
  • Effective and responsible use of AI: Uses District-approved AI tools to raise the quality and speed of work, keeps protected data out of non-approved tools, verifies output before relying on it, and retains personal accountability for results.
  • Preferred: Experience in a K-12 district or other public-sector organization, and with the business processes that ride on ECM (HR onboarding, student records, purchasing, Finance/AP, Special Education).
  • Preferred: Light front-end scripting for advanced form behavior (JavaScript/CSS) and C#/.NET for custom Laserfiche workflow activities or SDK work.
  • Preferred: Familiarity with the District's application stack (e.g., eSchoolPlus, Tyler Munis/TCM, Cognos, Power BI, TSDS/PEIMS, UKG Ready) and reporting/analytics tooling (SSRS, APIs, SSIS, Python, DAX).

Minimum Experience:

  • 3–5 years analyzing, configuring, supporting, and testing software backed by a relational database, ideally on a team in an Information Systems department.
  • A minimum of two (2) years administering or implementing Laserfiche, or a comparable ECM platform, including building Laserfiche Workflows and Forms.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES:

Essential Functions, organized by key accountability. The employee must be able to perform each of the following, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Works independently under the general direction of the Director of Information Systems, exercising discretion and independent judgment on matters of significance without day-to-day technical oversight.

Laserfiche Application Administration

Outcome: the Laserfiche application stays healthy, secure, properly licensed, and reliable for every department that depends on it.

  1. Serve as the primary administrator of the Laserfiche application: repository configuration, security management, themes and templates, and in-application user, group, and role provisioning, including named-user/seat license assignment.
  2. Monitor Laserfiche license and seat utilization and capacity, and provide usage and capacity input to support license procurement and renewals.
  3. Coordinate and test Laserfiche version upgrades, patches, and releases with affected departments, documenting issues and validating application function afterward.

Business Process Automation & Solution Delivery

Outcome: manual, paper-bound processes become automated, tested, well-documented Laserfiche solutions.

  1. Lead the districtwide development and implementation of automated business processes, workflows, and forms via the Laserfiche application: designing and deploying Forms (field design, validation, conditional and dynamic logic, layout, and accessibility to WCAG 2.1 AA) and Workflows, both automated (routing, approvals, notifications, document generation, and data writes) and manual/human-task.
  2. Build advanced form behavior and custom Laserfiche workflow activities as needed, including light front-end scripting (JavaScript/CSS) and C#/.NET (SDK) development.
  3. Collaborate with departments (HR, Finance, Special Education, Student Services, Purchasing, Facilities, and others) to analyze existing manual workflows, gather and clarify requirements, and translate them into automated Laserfiche solutions.
  4. Produce and maintain requirements and design documentation: business and functional requirements, as-is/to-be process maps, and design and configuration specifications.
  5. Develop and execute test plans; perform end-to-end functional testing; coordinate user acceptance testing (UAT) with business owners; and run regression testing after platform or solution changes.
  6. Manage change and release for Laserfiche solutions: version forms, workflows, and integrations and promote them through development, test, and production under change control, with documented and reversible deployments.
  7. Maintain an intake and backlog of form and process requests; prioritize, scope, and communicate status to requesting departments and the Director.

Cross-Application Analysis, Integration & Reporting

Outcome: district systems exchange the right data cleanly, and users and leaders get accurate answers and reporting from across the application landscape.

  1. Serve as a generalist analyst across District applications (including student, HR, and finance systems) by rapidly learning unfamiliar systems, asking the right questions, and providing answers and solutions.
  2. Configure, maintain, and enhance other District applications as needed.
  3. Build, maintain, and monitor integrations between Laserfiche and the District's SIS/ERP and other systems using APIs, interoperability standards (REST), and ETL (SSIS), and TSDS/PEIMS submissions.
  4. Write SQL queries against District application databases and read their schemas, including how tables and fields map to the screens and functions users see.
  5. Develop reports using tools such as Cognos Analytics, SSRS, and Power BI.
  6. Analyze, interpret, design, and implement changes to existing systems caused by statutory changes or user needs; read and interpret State and Federal laws to recommend required changes.

Support, Security & Compliance

Outcome: issues get resolved, data stays protected and compliant, and supported systems keep running through critical incidents.

  1. Triage user-reported defects and requests; define requirements; log and manage vendor cases; and test and implement solutions.
  2. Handle student, staff, and District data in accordance with FERPA, the Texas Public Information Act, the Texas Student Privacy Act (Texas Education Code §32.151), and District cybersecurity policy (SB 820 / HB 3834); apply least-privilege access; and support technology audits and vendor data-privacy and security reviews.
  3. Respond to high-priority and critical incidents for supported systems, including working extended or off-hours and being called in as needed.

Documentation & Training

Outcome: the people who use the supported applications understand them, and the work is well-documented.

  1. Provide end-user training on supported applications and processes, and maintain documentation on application processes and procedures.

General Expectations (expected of all employees in this role; not position-defining essential functions)

  • Communicate regularly with supervisor and co-workers, and demonstrate and support positive customer service relationships.
  • Participate in training and continuously update knowledge and skills through self-study and professional development.
  • Operate and implement within District IT, cybersecurity, data-governance, and solution-architecture policies, standards, and controls.
  • Apply responsible and proficient use of AI tools (see Qualifications) in analysis, development, documentation, and support work.

Marginal Functions (peripheral; may be reassigned without changing the fundamental nature of the position)

  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:

None.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Mental Demands: Maintain emotional control and exercise reasoning and problem-solving skills while under stress; communicate effectively, verbally and in writing; exhibit self-motivation and the persistence to set and meet objectives at high levels of quality and effectiveness.

Physical and Sensory Demands: Primarily sedentary work performed on-site at District facilities. Prolonged sitting and repetitive use of a computer keyboard, mouse, and multiple monitors; frequent near-vision work at a screen; and frequent communication by phone, video, and in person. Occasional standing, walking, bending, stooping, reaching, and moving about District facilities.

Lifting: Occasional lifting and carrying of equipment, supplies, or records up to 50 pounds.

Environment and Schedule: On-site position at District facilities; no remote or work-from-home arrangement. Occasional travel between District sites. Occasional prolonged or irregular hours, including availability to remotely troubleshoot and resolve problems during off-hours and to respond to high-priority or critical incidents.

Safety: Perform all duties in a safe and responsible manner. Observe all safety precautions.

The information contained in this job description is for compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and foregoing statements describe the general purpose and responsibilities assigned to this job and are not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills that may be required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Haemme LähiTapiola Varainhoitoon AI Leadia edistämään tekoälyn käytännön hyödyntämistä liiketoiminnan, asiakastarpeiden ja datatiimien rajapinnassa. Tässä roolissa tunnistat tekoälyn mahdollisuuksia, haastat nykyisiä toimintatapoja ja viet kehitysaihioita kohti konkreettisia ratkaisuja.

Tehtävässäsi

AI Leadina toimit tekoälyn hyödyntämisen edistäjänä ja omistajana Varainhoidon liiketoiminnan, kehittämisen ja datatiimien välillä. Autat tunnistamaan, priorisoimaan ja toteuttamaan tekoälyyn liittyviä kehitysaihioita, joilla voidaan parantaa esimerkiksi sijoittamisen palveluita, digitaalisia kyvykkyyksiä, asiakaspalvelua, KYC-prosesseja ja sisäistä tehokkuutta.

Tehtävässäsi pääset muun muassa:

  • tunnistamaan liiketoiminnan kanssa konkreettisia tekoälyn hyödyntämiskohteita
  • muuttamaan liiketoiminnan tarpeita selkeiksi kehitysaihioiksi
  • priorisoimaan kehityskohteita liiketoimintahyödyn, toteutettavuuden ja asiakasarvon perusteella
  • edistämään tekoälyratkaisujen käyttöönottoa ideasta toteutukseen
  • varmistamaan, että ratkaisut ovat käyttäjille ymmärrettäviä, luotettavia ja aidosti hyödyllisiä
  • tukemaan Varainhoidon tiimejä tekoälyn käytössä ja kasvattamaan talon yhteistä osaamista

Odotamme sinulta

Etsimme henkilöä, jolla on hyvä ymmärrys tekoälyn mahdollisuuksista ja rajoitteista sekä kyky viedä ideoita käytäntöön vastuullisesti ja liiketoimintaa tukevasti. Odotamme kykyä arvioida kriittisesti, mihin tekoäly soveltuu ja milloin ratkaisu on riittävän luotettava käyttöön.

Toivomme sinulta:

  • kokemusta tekoälyn tai kielimallien soveltamisesta liiketoiminnan käyttötapauksiin
  • kokemusta MS Power Platform -tuotteista ja Copilotista
  • kokemusta kehittämisestä, digitaalisista tuotteista, palveluista tai liiketoiminnan muutoksen edistämisestä
  • kykyä toimia liiketoiminnan, data-asiantuntijoiden ja muiden sidosryhmien välissä
  • vahvoja yhteistyö-, vuorovaikutus- ja fasilitointitaitoja
  • kokonaisuuksien hahmottamista ja suunnitelmallista työotetta

  • käytännönläheistä, oma-aloitteista ja ratkaisukeskeistä otetta.

Arvostamme ymmärrystä finanssialasta, varainhoidosta tai sijoittamisen liiketoiminnasta, mutta tärkeintä on kiinnostus liiketoiminnan kehittämiseen, tekoälyn käytännön hyödyntämiseen ja yhteistyöhön eri asiantuntijoiden kanssa.

Tässä tehtävässä pääset rakentamaan tekoälyn hyödyntämistä Varainhoidon liiketoiminnan ytimeen. Työsi tukee asiakaskokemuksen kehittämistä, palveluiden uudistamista, sisäisen työn sujuvoittamista ja liiketoiminnan päätöksenteon vahvistamista.

title: Technology Specialist
description:
The Canton Public Schools is seeking an exceptional and dynamic candidate to serve as an Technology Specialist. The Technology Specialist will join a vibrant and supportive team that places a high priority on collaboration, creativity, flexibility, and commitment to the goals of the District and to our students, families and staff.

The Canton Public Schools is an inclusive community for all students and staff and serve over 3,100 students in grades Prek-12, including our 18-22 program. The Canton Public Schools is elevating the educational experience for our students by cultivating a school culture and climate that promotes academic growth and social emotional learning for every student, and ensures high quality teaching and learning through the purposeful design of rigorous and equitable student experiences.

We are eager to find the next member of our team who collaborates with other educators to create the conditions necessary so that every child experiences the true joy of learning, the excitement of achievement, areas of passion, and an authentic sense of belonging in their school.

Job Summary

The District Technology Support Specialist is responsible for providing day-to-day technical support for students and staff throughout the district. This position is assigned to support CPS technology needs and are the primary responsibility of the specialist.

Canton Public Schools maintains a 1:1 Chromebook program grades 5-12. A primary responsibility of this role is the management, tracking, and coordination of Chromebook repairs. The specialist evaluates damaged devices, performs low-level repairs in-house when possible, and escalates more complex repairs by entering tickets into the repair queue and following up through completion.

This position requires strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, along with the ability to diagnose and resolve technical issues efficiently. Resourcefulness, adaptability, and strong customer service skills are essential. The ideal candidate must also demonstrate patience and professionalism while communicating with students, staff, and interdisciplinary teams with varying levels of technical knowledge.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Provide timely technical support for all users by documenting, tracking, and following up on requests submitted through the district ticketing system, as well as responding to emails, messages, and phone calls
  • Provide direct technical assistance and support to students as needed
  • Collaborate with members of the technology team to troubleshoot issues and develop effective solutions
  • Execute assigned tasks and assist in the implementation of technology projects and initiatives
  • Configure, deploy, maintain, and perform repairs on end-user devices and related equipment
  • Reallocate, replace, and install hardware and software throughout the district as needed
  • Coordinate and facilitate the repair process for district-owned devices, including Chromebooks and other instructional technology
  • Maintain accurate inventories, payment records, and other required documentation
  • Perform additional duties and responsibilities as assigned by the Technology Administrator

Qualifications:

  • Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, and/or equivalent work experience preferred
