title: Cybersecurity Operations Teacher
description:
POSITION TITLE: CYBERSECURITY OPERATIONS TEACHER REPORTS TO: Portsmouth Advanced Career Education PACE PRINCIPAL

OVER-TIME STATUS: EXEMPT PAY GRADE: 710

JOB SUMMARY:

Performs professional work providing limited direct instruction and computer assisted services in a specialized subject or assigned group of subjects, motivating students to develop skill in assigned subject matters; does related work as required. Work is performed under the regular supervision of the CTE Principal.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES:

  • Develop and deliver engaging, standards-based lessons in cybersecurity operations, including network security, ethical hacking, incident response, and risk management.
  • Align instruction with local, state and national standards, industry certifications, and career readiness expectations.
  • Use diverse instructional strategies to accommodate various learning styles and abilities.
  • Provide practical, hands-on training through labs, simulations, and real-world scenarios.
  • Utilize cybersecurity tools, platforms, and software to teach best practices in securing networks, systems, and data.
  • Design and administer assessments to measure student understanding and skill proficiency.
  • Provide timely, constructive feedback to help students improve technical and problem-solving skills.
  • Prepare students for industry-recognized certifications (e.g., CompTIA Security+, Network+, TestOut).
  • Stay current with emerging cybersecurity trends, technologies, and threats.
  • Collaborate with industry professionals to ensure the curriculum reflects current practices and standards.
  • Participate in professional development activities and continuous learning to enhance instructional quality.
  • Maintain a safe, organized, and inclusive learning environment.
  • Ensure the proper setup, use, and maintenance of cybersecurity lab equipment and software.
  • Enforce ethical guidelines and responsible use of technology.
  • Mentor and advise students on academic and career pathways in cybersecurity.
  • Facilitate student participation in cybersecurity competitions, internships, and other student work-based learning experiences.
  • Maintain accurate records of student progress, attendance, and achievements.
  • Prepare reports as required by school administration and accrediting bodies.
  • Work with colleagues, administrators, and industry partners to enhance program quality and relevance.
  • Participate in school meetings, committees, and parent conferences as needed.

JOB SPECIFICATIONS/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Thorough knowledge of subject(s); thorough knowledge of education principles, practices and procedures; thorough knowledge of the principles and methodology of effective

teaching; thorough knowledge of school division rules,regulations and procedures; ability to establish and maintain standards of behavior; ability to deliver articulate oral presentations and written reports; ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with other staff, students and parents; ability to operate a personal computer.

This is sedentary work requiring the exertion of up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to move objects, and some light work requiring the exertion of up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects; work requires stooping, kneeling, reaching, standing, walking, pushing, pulling, lifting, and repetitive motions; vocal communication is required for expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word; hearing is required to perceive information at normal spoken

word levels; visual acuity is required for preparing and analyzing written or computer data, determining the accuracy and thoroughness of work, and observing general surroundings and activities; the worker is subject to inside and outside environmental conditions. Some teaching specialties (i.e. music, art, physical education, etc.) may require hearing, vision, physical coordination and/or exertion and effort in excess of those listed above.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Eligible candidates should hold one or more of the following certifications (preferred):

A+ (CompTIA)

Network+ (CompTIA)

Security+ (CompTIA)

CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional)

SSCP (Systems Security Certified Practitioner)

CEH (Certified Ethical Hacker)

SCNP (Security Certified Network Professional)

CASP (CompTIA Advanced Security Practitioner)

CCNA Security

Must possess a Bachelor's or Master's degree in education or a related field. Must possess or be eligible for a Virginia Collegiate Professional License, Postgraduate Professional License or Provisional License with appropriate endorsement to teach specific subject areas. Detailed licensure information is available from the Virginia Department of Education online at: https://www.doe.virginia.gov/teaching-learning-assessment/teaching-in-virginia/licensure

APPLICATION PROCEDURE

All applicants, please submit an online application with supporting documentation.

If you have the desire to help students while positively impacting the community, we’d love for you to join our team! See why our current employees did!

Salary is commensurate based on occupational experience and qualifications.

JOB SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION & QUALIFICATIONS:

Job Summary

The full-time faculty supports Northcentral Technical College’s Medical Coding Specialist program by delivering high-quality instruction and fostering student success. This position is responsible for teaching courses within the program, developing and maintaining course materials, and aligning instruction with program objectives and evaluation procedures. Working 36 weeks within a 52-week academic year, faculty collaborates with colleagues, engages in professional development, and supports College initiatives to enhance the learning experience and achieve program goals.

Please note this is an in-person position located on campus in Wausau, Wisconsin.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

The following duties are primarily performed and are essential for this position. Employees are expected to be able to perform each of these job duties satisfactorily and successfully with or without reasonable accommodation.

Teaching & Student Success:

  • Facilitate student learning through engaging instructional strategies and methodologies across various modalities, including in-person, online, hybrid, and out-of-classroom activities, and mentoring students and peers.

  • Adhere to NTC’s academic calendar, Student Connect hours, teaching assignments, post and maintain office hours, and conduct assigned classes for the scheduled length of time in accordance with the faculty contract.

  • Assess and evaluate student performance by providing timely feedback and grades, maintaining accurate student records, attendance, and lab/clinical evaluations, in compliance with privacy laws, such as FERPA.

  • Develop and maintain course materials including outcome summaries, learning plans, Performance Assessment Tasks (PATs), syllabi, and online Learning Management System templates in the approved College format within designated timelines.

  • Select and utilize appropriate learning materials and resources including textbooks, library resources, equipment, and supplies to enhance learning.

  • Review, revise, and create curriculum in accordance with NTC academic standards and expectations.

  • Assist in planning, developing, implementing, and evaluating a new or modified course/certificate/program.

  • Stay current and focused on evolving learner needs and educational trends.

  • Provide written evaluations upon the student’s request.

Specific Instructional Program Duties:

  • Maintain Medical Coding curriculum alignment with current ICD, CPT, HCPCS, reimbursement, documentation, and health information standards and incorporate significant industry changes into instruction.

  • Integrate authentic coding applications, encoder technology, electronic resources, coding software, and other industry technologies into the student learning experience.

  • Evaluate Medical Coding course sequencing, instructional hours, delivery structure, and student progression and recommend program adjustments that support student success and program sustainability.

  • Provide Medical Coding students with program-specific academic guidance regarding course sequencing, progression, completion planning, professional expectations, and preparation for entry into the coding workforce.

  • Prepare students for employment and applicable professional coding credentials through instruction in coding accuracy, documentation requirements, ethical coding practices, reimbursement concepts, and professional standards.

  • Provide interdisciplinary education and consultation regarding medical coding, clinical documentation, reimbursement, and the revenue cycle to support collaboration with other health programs and College initiatives.

  • Integrate appropriate and ethical use of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies into Medical Coding education while maintaining academic integrity and requiring independent demonstration of coding competency.

College/Program Area Support:

  • Maintain program documentation as required by accreditation, program, or clinical sites standards, if applicable.

  • Coordinate with instructional support services to address student accommodation and modification needs, fostering an inclusive learning environment.

  • Engage and participate in faculty development training, professional day activities, College in-service events, commencement, team time, and other designated College activities.

  • Assist in onboarding and orienting new full-time, part-time, adjunct faculty, and other employees within the program or content area.

  • Actively participate in institutional, advisory and program team, and committee meetings.

  • Attend College Open Houses (on-campus and off-campus, set-up and take down) to assist with student recruitment and in support of Student Services activities.

  • Build and maintain collaborative relationships with business and industry partners, community organizations, and K-12 partners to strengthen program connections.

  • Assist, participate, support, and carry out all duties as assigned.

Professional Development:

  • Maintain Wisconsin Technical College System (WTCS)/Faculty Quality Assurance Standards (FQAS) and Higher Learning Commission qualification and meet requirements, accreditation or licensing standards, as applicable to program areas.

  • Maintain professional certifications, licensures, and credentials as required by the specific program area.

  • Remain up-to-date professionally in the area of content expertise and the teaching profession.

Faculty may be assigned to support key program functions due to accreditation, industry, or institutional needs. Typical responsibilities may include:

  • Serve as liaison with accrediting bodies, industry partners, and College leadership to ensure program compliance and relevance.

  • Coordinate curriculum updates, program reviews, and data reporting to support continuous improvement.

  • Lead communication and planning efforts related to program scheduling, resource needs, and stakeholder engagement.

  • Support recruitment, retention, and student success initiatives in collaboration with College departments.

Minimum Qualifications Required

In limited circumstances, NTC may consider a combination of education, training, and experience which provides the necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties of this position.

Education: Associate's Degree (or Equivalent)

  • Associate degree in Health Information Management, Health Information Technology, Medical Coding, or a related field required, or a technical diploma in a related field with the commitment to obtain an associate degree within three years of employment.

Experience: 2 Years

Additional Experience Information:

  • Occupational instructors must have a minimum of two years (4,000 hours) full-time or equivalent demonstrated relevant occupational experience, one of which must be within the last five years.

  • May waive the occupational experience of one year within the last five years if the candidate has two years of post-secondary teaching experience in the appropriate occupational field within the last five years.

  • NTC will determine whether applicants meet the credentialing requirements of the Wisconsin Technical College System (WTCS), the Higher Learning Commission (HLC), applicable accreditation standards, and/or occupational licensing standards. These requirements must be met at the time of hire and maintained throughout employment, where applicable to the position.

  • Experience in teaching preferred.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

In order to perform the functions and responsibilities of the position (listed above) the following knowledge, skills, and abilities, including language skills, reasoning and mathematical abilities are essential.

Language Skills:

Ability to read, write, analyze and interpret complex documents; present topics to internal and external individuals of all levels.

Math Skills:

Ability to perform and work complex calculations, make comparisons, interpret and provide logical explanations to others.

Reasoning Ability:

Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw conclusions to critically create resolutions; interpret instructions in mathematical or diagram form with abstract and concrete variables.

Technical Skills:

Ability to perform complex operations in a variety of job-specific systems, understand functionality to apply advanced functions, manage/customize and create calculations with data.

Customer Service Skills:

Ability to understand complex concerns and formulate solutions; communicate professionally with various audiences in different situations.

Other Requirements

Individual must possess and maintain at least one of the following professional credentials:

  • CPC (Certified Professional Coder)

  • CCS (Certified Coding Specialist)

  • CCS,P (Certified Coding Specialist, Physician-Based)

  • RHIT (Registered Health Information Technician)

title: Youtube Growth Consultant, US Market
description:
As an International Growth Consultant (IGC) specializing in YouTube and US Market Export, you will serve as the dedicated strategic export advisor driving full-funnel business expansion for APAC’s high-potential export accounts, “Future Giants” (FGs), in the US market. Unlike traditional domestic media specialists, your role operates within the International Growth Consultant job family, blending high-touch C-suite consultative advisory, cross-border market strategy, and deep product mastery. The US export corridor represents a highly significant revenue base, with substantial untapped stretch headroom concentrated across priority APAC accounts, and your core mission is to act as the strategic and narrative bridge between APAC HQ decision-makers and US market execution.

Google's Large Customer Sales (LCS) teams are strategic partners and industry thought leaders to the world's leading brands and agencies. We continuously challenge how customers think about their business and how Google can support growth. We focus on helping these players navigate profound industry shifts and drive outsized business performance by competitively selling Google's full suite of advertising solutions across Search, YouTube, Measurement, and more. As a member of our LCS team, you'll have the unique opportunity to sell at the forefront of technology, collaborating with executives, influencing market-shaping strategies, and delivering tangible results that significantly impact major global businesses and drive the growth of Google.

  • Deliver consultative advisory to C-suite leaders of APAC exporters, driving video strategy that justifies budget shifts into full-funnel YouTube brandformance.
  • Build creator frameworks and partner with US teams to connect brands with top creators, agencies, and custom moments into actionable pitch packages.
  • Establish regional case studies, benchmarks, and incrementality models to demonstrate how upper-funnel video drives concrete business growth over traditional digital channels.
  • Help APAC clients tailor messaging, pacing, and creative tone for US audiences, while using AI tools to streamline localization and video production sprints.
  • Collaborate closely with regional sales leads and global product teams to ensure seamless cross-border execution and unified client success across target markets.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7 years of experience in consultative sales, digital marketing strategy, or brand advertising.
  • Experience with the US advertising market and US consumer landscape.
  • Experience advising advertisers or agencies on brand, brandformance, or video advertising strategies.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Proven track record in international business development, market expansion strategy, or cross-border consultative advisory across APAC and the US.
  • Expertise in steering performance-first advertisers toward adopting upper-funnel brand and video solutions to unlock compound growth.
  • Deep understanding of the US creator ecosystem, social platforms, talent agencies/IMAs, and collaborative sponsorship models.
  • Ability to travel internationally to collaborate on-the-ground with US teams, creator partners, and industry stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence executive leadership and navigate complex, multi-regional internal and external stakeholder environments.
  • In-depth technical mastery of the YouTube advertising portfolio and measurement frameworks.

title: Senior Full Stack Developer
description:

Design, develop, and maintain scalable, secure, and high-performing software solutions by leveraging expertise in C#, React TypeScript, microservices architecture, containerization, database management, cloud technologies, and data engineering. Drive the architecture and delivery of robust APIs, backend systems, and modern frontend applications that support business objectives, improve system reliability, and enable seamless user experiences while adhering to engineering best practices and technical standards.

Education

Experience:

  1. 7 years of professional experience in full stack development with C#/.NET and React TypeScript
  2. Strong experience with microservices architecture, including design patterns, service decomposition, and inter-service communication
  3. Hands-on experience with containerization using Docker and orchestration with Kubernetes
  4. Experience with NoSQL databases, particularly MongoDB
  5. Hands-on experience with AWS services including RDS and Lambda
  6. Proven experience building and consuming RESTful APIs
  7. Experience leading cloud migration projects and strategies
  8. Experience with complex data migration methodologies and tools
  9. Strong grasp of security principles including OWASP guidelines, secure coding practices, and data protection
  10. Experience with version control systems (Git)

Special Knowledge and Skills:

  1. Strong proficiency in PostgreSQL/SQL Server and relational database design
  2. Knowledge of ETL processes and data pipeline development
  3. Excellent problem-solving, debugging, and troubleshooting skills in distributed systems

Preferred Qualifications:

  2. Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and DevOps practices
  3. Experience with message queuing systems (SQS, RabbitMQ, Kafka)

Technical Environment

  1. Backend: C#, .NET Core/Framework
  2. Architecture: Microservices, RESTful APIs
  3. Containers: Docker, Kubernetes
  4. Databases: SQL Server, MongoDB, AWS RDS
  5. Cloud: AWS (Lambda, RDS, ECS/EKS, S3, API Gateway)

Major Responsibilities

  9. Implement security best practices including authentication, authorization, encryption, API security, and container security
  10. Optimize database queries and API performance for high-traffic, distributed applications
  11. Design, develop, and maintain React TypeScript frontends, ensuring seamless integration with backend APIs

None

Frequent use of standard office equipment; prolonged sitting; occasional bending/stooping, pushing/pulling, and twisting; repetitive hand motions (keyboarding and use of mouse); occasional light lifting and carrying (less than 20 pounds); may work prolonged and irregular hours; occasional statewide travel; work with frequent interruptions; maintain emotional control under pressure.

From developing and maintaining our data centers to building the next generation of Google platforms, we make Google's product portfolio possible.   • Implement established compliance processes aligned with Compliance, Strategy, and Risk Management (CSRM) policies, standards, guidelines, and relevant legal or regulatory requirements.

title: Network Technician
description:
Location: Technology Department
Hours: 12 Month | Monday – Friday | 7.5 hours/day
Start Date: ASAP
Salary: Minimum starting $21.00/hour, based on experience

Qualifications:
Currently hold the Monroe County Civil Service title of Network Technician OR be on the current Monroe County Civil Service Network Technician eligible list

Distinguishing Features of the Class:
This is a technical position responsible for the installation, maintenance, operation, and repair of computer hardware, software, and network infrastructure. Work involves analyzing network hardware/software issues, testing equipment, managing inventory, and providing technical support. As part of this role, the position is also responsible for maintaining the district website and providing hands-on hardware and software support for student and staff devices, specifically including Chromebooks and iPads. The employee reports directly to the Director of Technology.

Typical Work Activities:

  • Helpdesk & End-User Support: Serves as a primary point of contact for technical support, answering helpdesk tickets, phone calls, and walk-in requests; provides polite, patient, and effective customer service to teachers, administrative staff, and students to resolve day-to-day technology issues.
  • Chromebook Repair & Maintenance: Diagnoses, troubleshoots, and performs physical and system repairs on Chromebooks (including screen, keyboard, battery, and motherboard replacements) used in 1:1 student deployments.
  • iPad Management & Deployment: Configures, deploys, and maintains district iPads, including managing iOS/iPadOS updates, application deployment via Mobile Device Management (MDM), and resolving hardware or operational issues.
  • Website Management: Maintains, updates, and manages content for the district website, ensuring accurate information, proper layout, and accessibility.
  • Analyzes, tests, and resolves malfunctions in computer systems, microprocessors, network terminals, printers, modems, and data communications hardware/software.
  • Performs hardware and software maintenance, minor repairs, setup, and department workstation configurations.
  • Maintains an up-to-date inventory of computer equipment, Chromebooks, iPads, and replacement parts, documenting daily system issues.
  • Researches, tests, and evaluates new technology, software, and hardware products.
  • Ensures the security, integrity, and efficiency of school network systems.
  • Consults with vendors regarding repairs and replacement parts.
  • Attaches cabling and coordinates with technicians/electricians for hardware installations.


Full Performance, Knowledge, Skills, Abilities and Personal Characteristics:
Good knowledge of micro-computer and network product technology, peripheral equipment, and logical operations of data communication devices; working knowledge of Chromebook hardware repairs and ChromeOS management; working knowledge of iPad hardware, iOS/iPadOS troubleshooting, and basic Mobile Device Management (MDM); working knowledge of basic website design/management principles and content updates; working knowledge of data processing methodology, techniques, and documentation of data security; ability to detect, troubleshoot, and resolve severe micro-computer and network breakdowns; ability to maintain accurate inventory and system records; ability to conduct user workshops and provide technical support; ability to establish and maintain effective professional relationships with staff and vendors; initiative; patience; dependability; good motor skills; physical condition commensurate with the demands of the position.

Minimum Qualifications: Graduation from high school or possession of an equivalency diploma plus EITHER:

(A) Graduation from a regionally accredited or New York State registered college or university with a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Technology, Data Processing, Management Information Systems, plus two (2) years paid full-time or its part-time equivalent experience responsible for the maintenance, configuration or installation of micro-computer hardware and software; OR,

(B) Graduation from a regionally accredited college or university with an Associate's degree in Computer Science, Computer Technology, Data Processing, Management Information Systems, plus four (4) years experience as defined in (A) above; OR,

(C) Six (6) years paid full-time or its part-time equivalent experience as defined in (A) above; OR,

(D) Any equivalent combination of training and experience as defined by the limits of (A), (B) and (C) above.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENT FOR APPOINTMENT IN SCHOOL DISTRICTS AND BOCES:
Per Chapter 180 of the Laws of 2000, and by Regulations of the Commissioner of Education, to be employed in a position designated by a school district or BOCES as involving direct contact with students, a clearance for employment from the State Education Department is required.

FLSA: Non-exempt

The Fairport Central School District is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. The District is committed to achieving a more diverse workforce. Candidates of diverse backgrounds and experience are strongly encouraged to apply.

title: Instructional Technology Coach (ITC)
description:
Performs complex professional work maintaining and updating the division's computer network and related infrastructure and programs; does related work as required. This is an exempt position as defined by the Fair Labor Standards Act. Employees holding exempt positions often are required to follow a flexible work schedule, which may include working extended hours to meet specific job responsibilities. The contracted salary covers all hours worked.

This is light work requiring the exertion of up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects; work requires climbing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, reaching, standing, walking, pushing, pulling, lifting, grasping, and repetitive motions; vocal communication is required for expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word; hearing is required to receive detailed information through oral communications and/or to make fine distinctions in sound; visual acuity is required for color perception, preparing and analyzing written or computer data, visual inspection involving small defects and/or small parts, use of measuring devices, assembly or fabrication of parts at or within arm's length, operation of machines, determining the accuracy and thoroughness of work, and observing general surroundings and activities; the worker is subject to inside and outside environmental conditions.

PRIMARY FUNCTION:

The Instructional Technology Coach is to assist teachers with the integration of technology in the classroom, to train teachers to use technology in an effective manner, and to assist with curriculum development as it relates to educational technology. The ITC is to be a “first responder” in the case of technical problems at schools, performing software, and hardware repairs and referring others to the Service Request Database as needed. The ITC provides assistance by consulting with other teachers, discussing and sharing teaching practices, and supporting efforts to enrich student learning through technology. Instructional technology coaches are available throughout the school day for planning and implementation of integration activities. Instructional technology coaches are intended to serve as resources to classroom teachers, but are not intended to serve as classroom teachers.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Hold a Collegiate Professional License with a specific endorsement in the area to which assigned.

The ITC must demonstrate the ability and professional and personal characteristics necessary for working effectively with school personnel and members of the community. He/she must possess the ability to deliver articulate oral presentations and written reports and the ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with staff, teachers, administrators, and students. The ITC must be knowledgeable about successful integration of technology into the classroom, including new and emerging technologies. He/she must have the ability to diagnose and solve minor computer, peripheral, and network problems. The ITC must be able to communicate effectively with adult learners.

The ITC must be a graduate of an accredited college or university and be a licensed teacher. Successful experience in public education as a teacher is recommended. He/she must have experience in integrating technology in the classroom. He/she must have experience using computers and peripherals effectively in a classroom setting including, but not limited to, printers, scanners, external storage devices, video equipment, such as digital cameras and computer projection devices. He/she must stay current with new and emerging technologies.

PERFORMANCE RESPONSIBILITIES:

Performance expectations include, but are not limited to, the following functions/tasks:

  • Assists teachers and staff, grades PK-12, with the integration of technology in the classroom; provides in-service to groups of teachers/staff as well as individualized assistance as requested.
  • Provides technology-training opportunities throughout the school year for teachers and staff to use technology in an effective manner.
    • Be an effective listener, keen observer and positive communicator who works with teachers on their level and develops skills to reach higher levels of functioning.
    • ITCs should interact with core area teachers regularly. During these meetings the ITC assists teachers in planning lessons, which integrate technology into student learning. The technology should be used in the context of core lessons, not as an add-on to lessons.
    • Supports implementation of the division and state technology plan.
    • Assists with curriculum development as it relates to educational technology.
    • Meets with district and building level administrators to communicate visions of technology integration and to select appropriate software and web services.
    • Maintains school-based webpages as assigned.
    • Provides demonstration teaching to students and teachers in the appropriate use of technology in the classrooms and/or computer labs. Modeling of lessons should be aimed at giving the core teachers ownership of the learning and instruction.
    • Examines and recommends computer hardware and software to teachers and administrators, and makes them accessible for students and teachers.
    • Solves minor problems related to hardware and software issues in classrooms, labs, and school offices and refers teachers to the Service Request Database in the case of more technically challenging problems.
    • Keeps current with updates in educational technology.
    • Develops a rich library of curriculum-driven support materials and technology-enhanced resources for grade levels and subject areas for teachers.
    • Performs related duties as assigned in accordance with the school/system policies and practices.

    TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT: Teacher Scale (10 month employee) 7 hours per day

    EVALUATION:

    Performance on this job will be evaluated in accordance with school board policy and administrative regulations on evaluation of licensed personnel.

    REPORTS TO: Principal

Future Power Market Analyst efficiently manages and leverages power fundamentals analysis to form a view on the future of the power system to inform decision-making within the Trading & Supply organisation.

What you’ll be doing

Shell Energy Europe & Environmental Products is seeking an individual for long-term Power Market Fundamental Analysis of Europe. This position is responsible for supporting finance, investments and strategy department with analysis developed from a deep understanding of the key long-term drivers such as the evolution of demand, generation (wind, solar, gas fired, coal fired, batteries, etc.) transmission, regulatory, etc. This position must build credibility with internal customers so that such foresight can be translated into long term decisions. The emphasis is on developing quantitatively advantaged capabilities, supported as appropriate by models, tools and techniques that yield high quality insight. Collaborating with peers in the Short, Mid-Term and Long-term Fundamentals team to build scalability in this respect is essential.

  • Deliver long-term market view for strategic projects and use fundamental analysis techniques to support Shell group decisions.

  • Research and understand the fundamental drivers to gain an informed view in the context of long-term modelling focused on developing forward pricing views.

  • Monitor market developments in market design/regulatory issues that could impact prices.

  • Work closely with short, mid-term and long-term natural gas and power analysts in market view development.

What you bring

  • Experience with power system analysis

  • Experience with related software & packages (e.g., Plexos, Aurora, EPSI etc.).

  • Good knowledge in energy economics

  • Strong knowledge of the European Energy Markets

  • Very strong numerical and analytical skills (e.g. statistics, optimisation)

  • Exceptional communication and presentation skills, both written and oral.

  • Excellent IT skills incl. ability to model in main languages as Python and in the MS Windows environment (particularly Excel), Experience interfacing with databases (SQL)

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, Economics, or any related degrees required.

  • Good working exposure in Power Fundamentals is a must.

  • Demonstrated understanding of power fundamentals.

After you submit your application, you will receive an email from Shell providing a link to an online assessment (HireVue) that is a mandatory part of the process and has a validity period – please check your spam/junk mailbox if you do not see the email. Once completed, your application will be reviewed to determine next steps. Thank you for your interest in Shell.

What we offer

You bring your skills and experience to Shell and in return you work with talented, committed people on one of the most important challenges facing our planet. You’ll have the opportunity to develop the skills you need to grow in an environment where we value honesty, integrity, and respect for one another. You’ll be able to balance your priorities as you become the best version of yourself.

  • Continuously grow the transferable skills you need to get ahead.

  • Work at the forefront of technology, trends, and practices.

  • Collaborate with experienced colleagues with unique expertise.

  • Achieve your balance in a values-led culture that encourages you to be the best version of yourself.

  • Make an impact in one of the world’s leading energy trading businesses.

  • Benefit from flexible working hours, and the possibility of remote/mobile working.

  • Perform at your best with a competitive starting salary and annual performance related salary increase – our pay and benefits packages are considered to be among the best in the world.

  • Take advantage of paid parental leave, including for non-birthing parents.

  • Join an organisation working to become one of the most diverse and inclusive in the world. We strongly encourage applicants of all genders, ages, ethnicities, cultures, abilities, sexual orientation, and life experiences to apply.

  • Grow as you progress through diverse career opportunities in national and

  • international teams.

  • Gain access to a wide range of training and development programmes.

Shell is working to advance an inclusive, psychologically safe and accessible environment where people with disabilities can excel. If you require any accommodations or accessibility adjustments (e.g. assistive technology, communication support, any other) during the application or interview process, please let us know directly via careers@shell.com . We strive to ensure that our process and workplace is accessible to everyone and are dedicated to making reasonable adjustments to support your needs.

Shell in The United Kingdom

Shell is a vital contributor to the UK, supporting energy security, jobs and economic value. We provide energy to fuel homes, hospitals, schools, vehicles, machinery and factories. Our history here dates back over 125 years. A UK-headquartered global energy leader, and leading FTSE multinational, we are active across the country’s energy system.

In the years ahead, as the UK looks to strengthen energy security and deliver its 2050 net-zero goal, Shell UK aims to play a crucial role. We aim to be a major investor in the UK energy system by helping our customers decarbonise with a focus on transport and industry.

title: EMEA IFM Platform Lead
description:
Job Title

EMEA IFM Platform Lead

Job Description Summary

Job Description

EMEA IFM Platform Lead

Global Occupier Services

London

Cushman & Wakefield is a global leader in commercial real estate services, helping clients transform the way people work, shop, and live. The firm’s 53,000 employees in more than 70 countries provide deep local and global insights that create significant value for occupiers and investors around the world.

Cushman & Wakefield is among the largest commercial real estate services firms with revenues of $10.1 billion across core services of agency leasing, asset services, capital markets, facilities services (branded C&W Services), global occupier services, investment management (branded DTZ Investors), tenant representation, and valuations & advisory.

We have an exciting opportunity for a talented Integrated Facilities Management Regional Leader to join our market-leading Global Occupier Services business based in London working across EMEA.

Role Purpose

The EMEA IFM Regional Leader will be a critical leader, reporting to the International IFM Platform Leader. This individual will be a dynamic leader who thrives in a matrix environment, welcomes new challenges and is passionate about delivering the best innovative services to our clients. He/she will have IFM oversight of the EMEA region, responsible for enabling operational excellence and working in partnership with the Account teams to consistently exceed our clients’ expectations wherever possible. This individual (and their team) will provide support to the Account and Solutions teams related to all aspects of account life cycle including, but not limited to, new business solutions/sales, organic growth/expansion (geography/scope), service levels, contract renewals, team development, governance, innovation, and best practices.

Key Responsibilities

Platform strategy and operating model

  • Demonstrates a Client-Driven approach by marshalling the firm’s resources across all core capabilities and corporate functions to ensure superior service to both internal and external clients
  • Collaborate with Enterprise Client Sales and Solutions to build and win new client relationships. Support the development of new facility management business opportunities with an emphasis on operational feasibility and overall profitability. Support the due diligence process, provide input and guidance regarding contract terms including SLA’s and KPI’s
  • Work in conjunction with Divisional Presidents, Executive Account Directors, and Account Directors to monitor client account requirements and manage the deployment of resources within the Global Occupier Services teams.
  • Facilitate collaboration across clients and markets. Work with other Regional IFM Leads to ensure a high and consistent level of quality of service to all clients globally.
  • Partner with Executive, Regional, Account, and Solutions Development Leaders to identify opportunities to provide organic growth solutions for Occupier clients. Demonstrates a Client-Driven approach by marshalling the appropriate resources across all core capabilities and corporate functions to ensure superior service to clients.
  • Responsible for achieving IFM platform operational business goals and objectives.
  • Actively collaborate with and leverage SME’s to bring best practices to account teams. Work across IFM platform functions (Technical Services, EHS, Workplace Experience, etc) to enable comprehensive IFM support.
  • Provide leadership to ensure continued operational controls (i.e. Operational Reviews), reporting procedures, and systems to effectively ensure execution (including account transition and transformations) and operating efficiency for current and future growth.
  • Support new account transitions and implement IFM programs on new client accounts
  • Actively support the strategy and requirements for business intelligence (AI), reporting, and data management for IFM including developing performance measurements for internal benchmarking and identifying industry data to leverage for external benchmarking.
  • Provide support, leadership and best practice management of assigned direct and matrix reports and the wider IFM organization, including all aspects of talent development, personnel and performance management (including management of under-performance where needed) and succession planning and management for the assigned organization/s.
  • Actively participates with and contributes to the business executive as appropriate. Supports, engages and contributes to leadership discussions, forums, presentations, industry engagements, meetings, townhalls and the like (both internal and external to CW organisation) in line with the needs and expectations of business.

Service delivery and operational excellence

  • Provide platform assurance across the EMEA IFM portfolio — monitor account health, SLA and KPI performance, critical-environment risk, and client satisfaction, and intervene where accounts are off-track.
  • Lead the regional operational review cadence with account leaders; own the escalation route for at-risk accounts and material service failures.

Client relationships and growth

  • Act as the senior IFM subject-matter authority on EMEA pursuits, help shape solution design, operating model, transition plan and pricing narrative, and present to client evaluation panels.
  • Support account leaders in strategic client relationships, quarterly business reviews and expansion conversations; identify cross-sell into adjacent service lines.
  • Build a leadership bench capable of mobilizing new accounts at pace; sponsor development of high-potential facilities and operations managers.

Data, Reporting & Business Intelligence

  • Lead the IFM EMEA approach for centralised reporting, data governance and performance measurement.
  • Drive adoption of AI, automation, analytics, and digital tools to support operational decision making.
  • Ensure data quality, reporting consistency, and meaningful performance insights across the IFM platform.

Maintenance Operations

  • Lead the Maintenance Operations function in the region, governing provision of the RSM function by the Operations Hub and including implementation and ongoing improvement of FAMIS360 and Triana in all accounts.
  • Working with the Technical / Engineering team, ensure account teams establish and implement maintenance programs across client portfolios.
  • SOC approver for FAMIS360 EMEA Shared Instance.

Risk, Compliance & Governance

  • Ensure IFM delivery across EMEA meets Cushman & Wakefield HSE standards and all applicable statutory and regulatory obligations, including critical-environment and high hazard work controls.
  • Provide leadership for IFM operational risk, compliance, and governance programs including BRAC, Risk Registers and incident reporting.
  • Ensure appropriate controls, audit programs, and corrective action processes are established and maintained including the Account Health Check process.
  • Promote a strong culture of risk awareness, accountability, and regulatory compliance.
  • Support operational resilience and business continuity planning across the region.

People Operations

  • Lead, develop, and mentor direct teams across EMEA. Support and guide matrix teams across EMEA to ensure an integrated approach is delivered for accounts - including Procurement & Supply Chain, Remote Site Management, Workplace Experience and Technical/Engineering.
  • Lead the IFM Onboarding program in EMEA, ensuring all new team members are onboarded into the IFM EMEA business.

Experience and Qualifications

Essential

  • 15+ years of demonstrated experience in Facilities Management leadership, strategic planning, and program development including outsourced facility management
  • Technology: Expertise with asset management/CMMS platforms, highly proficient with MS Office Suite, including ability to perform Internet based research
  • Experience with high-level, complex Facility and Engineering operations including asset management, maintenance best practices, safety,
  • Excellent oral and written communication and presentation skills required
  • Strong competency in strategic planning, execution and business acumen
  • Demonstrated multi-country responsibility across EMEA, including experience operating through country management structures and navigating local labor and works council frameworks
  • Accomplished relationship management and interpersonal skills
  • Excellent organizational abilities required
  • Team strategic development and leadership experience
  • Able to travel domestically and when needed internationally




Cushman & Wakefield is an equal opportunity / affirmative action employer. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to ethnicity, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, marital status, or any other legally protected characteristic. Cushman & Wakefield is committed to equity in employment, and our goal is to have a diverse, inclusive and barrier-free workplace. title: Instructional Technology Coordinator
description:
Thank you for your interest in a career with us! The Northshore School District is committed to a diverse workforce that reflects our students and our community, one that embraces and models equity and cultural competency.

This posting is open until filled with the first review of applications occurring on Monday, August 17, 2026.

Job Summary: Consistent with the Northshore School District Strategic Plan and the Instructional Technology Plan, the principal goal of the Instructional Technology Team is to have a positive and equitable impact on student learning by facilitating the effective integration of instructional technologies and digital learning services in all learning environments. The primary role of the Instructional Technology Coordinator position is to coach teachers and other adult learners in the digital and artificial intelligence (AI) literacy skills necessary for effective teaching and learning in modern digital learning environments.

Duties and Responsibilities:

This list of essential functions is not exhaustive and may be supplemented as necessary in consultation with the employee(s) involved.

  1. Collaborate with other members of the Teaching and Learning Division, Special Education, and the Department for Organizational Change and Student Advancement in developing and delivering professional development to teachers for district-wide curriculum adoptions and learning initiatives as it applies to the use of instructional technologies, including computing resources, digital learning services, and learning management systems.
  2. Provide professional development for teachers, paraprofessionals, and administrators in support of district-provided student computing devices and digital learning environments, making purposeful connections to learning outcomes between technology use and learning outcomes for students.
  3. Mentor teachers in integrating current, relevant and supportable technologies into their classroom. This includes, but is not limited to, interactive presentation technologies, digital content creation tools, cloud-based collaboration and productivity services, AI-enabled instructional tools, and communicating with students, families, and the community using district-supported digital tools and learning management systems.
  4. Consistent with district strategic goals and KPIs, team with teacher(s) to develop classroom projects and lesson plans that promote students’ attainment of Washington State learning standards and ISTE Standards, empowering students to use technology, including AI tools where and when appropriate, to collaborate, communicate, generate innovative ideas, investigate, and solve problems.
  5. Partner with teachers to promote students’ acquisition of skills related to digital citizenship, media literacy, and AI literacy. In alignment with the Danielson framework for teaching, support teachers in their understanding of systems and operations and the practice of safe, legal, ethical, and responsible use of technology, including artificial intelligence.
  6. Assist site-based, shared decision-making teams in the development of strategies to support the goals of the School Action Plan in the integration of standard classroom technologies.
  7. Analyze emerging technology trends, including AI and perform research to identify new classroom technologies and recommend district technology standards (including hardware, software, digital learning services, and support structures)
  8. Effectively manage projects of various complexities, frequently more than one at a time.
  9. Advocate for schools and teachers during the installation and implementation of software and hardware and facilitate communication between campuses and the Technology Department.
  10. Take initiative for continued personal and professional growth.
  11. Perform other duties as assigned.

Reporting Relationships: Reports to the Assistant Director of Instructional Technology and Library Services

Working Conditions: Required to facilitate groups and communicate effectively; required to meet inflexible deadlines; requires mental and visual concentration; requires occasional prolonged exposure to visual displays; occasionally required to deal with distraught or frustrated people; occasionally required to work flexible and irregular hours to complete tasks; required to operate a motor vehicle and travel between sites.

Minimum Qualifications:

Education and Experience

The qualified candidate has a bachelor’s degree and experience working in a Pre-K–12 classroom setting, training adults in topics related to instructional practices, and/or curriculum development.

Preferred Experience

Minimum of three (3) years of experience teaching in a Pre-K–12 classroom setting; experience as technology integration specialist or experience in a role developing professional learning experiences for adults in curriculum, pedagogy, or educational technology.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  1. Ability to Apply Knowledge of Instructional Principles and Practices
    • Effectively coach and teach adult learners
    • Demonstrate understanding of the instructional support needs of classroom teachers
    • Model effective classroom practices
    • Demonstrate vision for technology and instruction
  2. Ability to Apply Knowledge of Instructional Technology
    • Apply knowledge of instructional technology standards to create effective learning environments
    • Effectively coach teachers to meet curricular goals using an integration of technology
    • Apply sound instructional practices with available technology resources
    • Learn and quickly apply digital learning technologies
    • Research and assess new technologies to support instruction
  3. Ability to Communicate Effectively
    • Facilitate discussions, listen effectively, and help develop solutions
    • Communicate technical information to non-technical staff
    • Make effective oral presentations
    • Write clearly and effectively
    • Author multimedia products including web, video, and audio broadcasts
    • Maintain confidentiality
  4. Ability to Work Independently to Meet Program Needs
    • Exercise good judgment within scope of assignment
    • Organize work and set priorities to meet deadlines
    • Work effectively under pressure
    • Adapt to accommodate frequent changes in scope and program delivery
  5. Ability to Work Effectively with a Variety of Other People
    • Work effectively as a member of a team
    • Work effectively as a leader of a team
    • Establish and maintain effective working relationships with others

Licenses/Special Requirements

Valid Washington State driver’s license.



Salary: 2026-27 Non-Represented (NNRAP) Professional Technical Salary Schedule; Level I; placement on the salary schedule will be determined by Human Resources DOE. FLSA Exempt.


Work Year: 12 month position, 260 days per year, 8.0 hours per day.

Benefits: Washington state health insurance coverage (SEBB) and a Washington state retirement package, for eligible positions. Generally, you are eligible for SEBB benefits if you are anticipated to work at least 630 hours per school year (September 1 through August 31).

The School Employees Benefits Board (SEBB) benefits include:

  • Medical plans with prescription benefits
  • Dental plans
  • Vision plans
  • Life and AD&D insurance
  • Long-term disability insurance
  • Medical Flexible Spending Arrangement
  • Dependent Care Assistance Program

All offers of employment are contingent upon satisfactory results of background checks with prior employers and/or character references; satisfactory outcome of a criminal history background check (includes fingerprinting); satisfactory outcome of sexual misconduct information from prior school district employers; and approval by the Northshore School Board.

title: PM Technician
description:
About Us

We are a global climate technologies company engineered for sustainability. We create sustainable and efficient residential, commercial and industrial spaces through HVACR technologies. We protect temperature-sensitive goods throughout the cold chain. And we bring comfort to people globally. Best-in-class engineering, design and manufacturing combined with category-leading brands in compression, controls, software and monitoring solutions result in next-generation climate technology that is built for the needs of the world ahead.

Whether you are a professional looking for a career change, an undergraduate student exploring your first opportunity, or recent graduate with an advanced degree, we have opportunities that will allow you to innovate, be challenged and make an impact. Join our team and start your journey today!

Shift: Nights 9:00 PM- 5:30 AM

MINIMUM EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION REQUIRED:

A successful candidate must possess two year’s experience in an industrial/multi-craft maintenance environment with at least 3 years manufacturing experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered. A degree in a related technical field with additional experience or completion of an apprenticeship program would be a plus.

DESCRIPTION:

Work with maintenance technicians on performing routine maintenance duties. Assist in repairing and maintaining machinery and mechanical equipment by performing the following duties:

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED:

  • Must work well in a team environment
  • Strong communication skills
  • Strong hands-on abilities
  • Above average mechanical aptitude
  • Competence with power tools, welding, fabrication, painting, etc.
  • The ability to work overtime
  • Some heavy lifting
  • The ability to stand for long periods of time
  • The ability to climb ladders and steps
  • Clean and maintain work area, tools, and equipment.
  • Work with Maintenance Tech to perform routine maintenance duties
  • Perform preventative maintenance in accordance with PM schedules
  • Assist in equipment moves and installation projects
  • Assist in generating new and/or improving existing PM schedules
  • Assist in training team members for operator PM’s
  • Assist with continuous improvement of company safety practices as well as improved welding processes, techniques, and practices
  • Regular attendance is required
  • All other duties assigned

ELIGIBILITY TO BID FOR ANY HOURLY POSITION INCLUDES:

  • Be a regular full-time Alliance employee
  • Have no more than a Written Discussion for Attendance

Our Commitment to Our People

Across the globe, we are united by a singular Purpose: Sustainability is no small ambition. That’s why everything we do is geared toward a sustainable future—for our generation and all those to come. Through groundbreaking innovations, HVACR technology and cold chain solutions, we are reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency in spaces of all sizes, from residential to commercial to industrial.

Our employees are our greatest strength. We believe that our culture of passion, openness, and collaboration empowers us to work toward the same goal - to make the world a better place. We invest in the end-to-end development of our people, beginning at onboarding and through senior leadership, so they can thrive personally and professionally.

Flexible and competitive benefits plans offer the right options to meet your individual/family needs: medical insurance plans, dental and vision coverage, 401(k) and more. We provide employees with flexible time off plans, including paid parental leave, vacation and holiday leave.

Together, we have the opportunity – and the power – to continue to revolutionize the technology behind air conditioning, heating and refrigeration, and cultivate a better future. Learn more about us and how you can join our team!

Our Commitment to Inclusion & Belonging

At Copeland, we cultivate a strong sense of inclusion and belonging where individuals of all backgrounds, and with diverse perspectives, are embraced and treated fairly to enable a stronger workforce. Our employee resource groups play an important role in culture and community building at Copeland.

Individuals with temporary visas such as E, F-1 with OPT or CPT, H-1, H-2, L-1, B, J or TN, or who need sponsorship for work authorization now or in the future, are not eligible for hire.

Under the direction of an assigned supervisor, acts as liaison to assigned business area and provides and recommends solutions to improve processes and delivery of services to students, faculty, and staff through expansion of existing systems or the use of third party systems and applications; responsible for assisting and leading the updates and changes in the student success web pages; analyze and implement integration/interfacing of systems with the College's ERP system; serve as the administrator of designated third-party applications.

DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS

This classification is a unique and highly specialized role within the district which provides functional and process support for the business units of the district in using information technology systems and tools effectively and efficiently. This classification is assigned to support one or more business units based on the business expertise of the individual assigned and acts as a liaison between the business unit and the technical staff in the Information Technology department. This classification is tasked with understanding system and tool capabilities and their application to the business needs of the supported units.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

It is not intended to be restricted or construed as an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities required of individuals so classified, and not all duties listed are necessarily performed by each employee in this classification.

8. Serves as the content manager of the assigned area webpages.

title: Senior Internal Auditor (IL, USA)
description:
Senior Internal Auditor


Location: Illinois (Hybrid — Multiple Location Options | Relocation Assistance Available)

Compensation: $80K–$103K base


Our client is a large, publicly traded global organization seeking a Senior Internal Auditor to join its Internal Audit team. This role offers broad exposure across a complex business environment, with opportunities to work on financial, operational, risk, and controls-focused audits while partnering with stakeholders across the organization.


The position may be based in either the Chicago area or Central Illinois. Hybrid expectations and compensation within the posted range vary based on work location, experience, and qualifications.


The Opportunity

This is an ideal opportunity for an auditor with approximately 2–4 years of experience who has developed a strong foundation in public accounting or internal audit and is ready to broaden their exposure within a global corporate environment.


You will be expected to:

  • Execute and increasingly lead risk-based audit engagements from planning through reporting.
  • Evaluate financial, operational, compliance, and internal-control risks.
  • Identify control weaknesses and opportunities to improve business processes.
  • Review work completed by other members of the engagement team as your responsibilities expand.
  • Communicate findings and recommendations effectively with business stakeholders.
  • Use data analytics, AI, and other technology-enabled tools to improve audit quality and efficiency.
  • Contribute to initiatives focused on continuously improving the Internal Audit function.


What You’ll Own

  • Risk-based audit planning, testing, documentation, and reporting.
  • Evaluation of internal controls and business processes.
  • Development of practical, well-supported audit findings and recommendations.
  • Collaboration with cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Increasing responsibility for leading audit engagements and reviewing project work.
  • Participation in audit innovation and continuous-improvement initiatives.
  • Travel of up to approximately 30%, primarily within North America.


What We’re Looking For

Approximately 2–4 years of relevant audit experience, ideally including experience with a Big Four or other national public accounting firm.


Hands-on experience with:

  • External audit, advisory, internal audit, or related risk and controls work.
  • Financial and operational processes and internal controls.
  • Audit testing, documentation, and issue development.
  • Working with business stakeholders in a professional environment.
  • Leading portions of engagements or providing guidance to less-experienced team members.


Education

A bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, or a related discipline is expected. CPA, CIA, or progress toward a professional certification is preferred but not required.


Strongly Preferred

  • Big Four or national public accounting experience.
  • Experience at the Senior Auditor or comparable level.
  • Exposure to SOX and internal-control environments.
  • Interest in data analytics, AI, or technology-enabled auditing.
  • Demonstrated initiative beyond assigned audit responsibilities.


Who This Is Not For

  • Candidates seeking a fully remote position.
  • Candidates who are not comfortable with periodic business travel.
  • Candidates without a foundational understanding of audit methodology and internal controls.
  • Candidates looking for a narrowly defined audit role with limited exposure outside their assigned projects.


Why This Role

  • Broad exposure across a large, complex global organization.
  • Opportunity to transition from public accounting into a corporate environment without narrowing your professional exposure.
  • Clear opportunities to take on increasing audit leadership responsibility.
  • Strong career-development opportunities within Internal Audit and across the broader organization.
  • Modern audit environment with an emphasis on data, AI, technology, and continuous improvement.

title: Digital Advertising Specialist
description:
Location: Hybrid
Department: Digital Marketing
Reports To: Senior Digital Marketing & Analytics Lead – B2B Performance (Global)
Type: Full-Time

Role Overview

We are looking for a hands-on Digital Marketing Executive to build, run and optimize our paid digital campaigns and keep our performance reporting sharp, current and trusted.

This is a delivery-focused role at the heart of the Digital team. You will be in the platforms daily, building and managing LinkedIn, Google and programmatic campaigns for huge technology brands and household names, and out of them just as often, pulling the numbers together, spotting what is working, and telling the wider business what it means. You will also be the connective tissue between campaigns and the teams who feed them, coordinating creative, landing pages and assets through Wrike so activity launches on time and to standard.

You will work closely with the Senior Digital Marketing & Analytics Lead, who will set the strategic direction and support your development. The ideal candidate is curious about data, meticulous about execution, and keen to grow into a broader performance marketing career.

Key Responsibilities

Campaign Build & Activation

  • Build, launch and manage paid digital campaigns across LinkedIn Ads, Google Ads (Search, Display, Video) and programmatic platforms.
  • Set up campaigns correctly from the ground up: audience targeting, bidding, budget pacing, conversion tracking, UTM tagging and naming conventions.
  • Monitor live campaigns daily for delivery, spend pacing, disapprovals and anomalies, and act quickly when something needs fixing.
  • Support paid social and display activity as required, ensuring campaigns ladder up to funnel objectives across awareness, demand generation and conversion.
  • Maintain accurate campaign trackers covering budgets, flight dates, audiences and creative versions.

Performance Reporting, Insight & Optimisation

  • Produce regular performance updates (weekly and monthly) for internal stakeholders, vendors and regional teams.
  • Track and report core metrics including impressions, CTR, CPC, CPL, MQL and SQL progression, ROAS and pipeline contribution.
  • Move beyond reporting the numbers: explain what changed, why it changed, and what should happen next.
  • Provide clear, prioritised optimisation recommendations, including creative, copy, audience, bidding, budget allocation and landing page experience, and implement the agreed changes.
  • Run structured A/B tests and document learnings so they can be reapplied across markets and vendors.
  • Connect campaign performance to overall business performance, linking digital activity through to lead quality, opportunity creation and revenue outcomes.

Reporting Dashboards & Data Quality

  • Monitor all digital marketing dashboards daily, checking that data is flowing, refreshes have run and figures reconcile with the source platforms.
  • Maintain and update dashboards in Power BI and Google Looker Studio, adding new campaigns, markets, vendors and metrics as activity evolves.
  • Investigate and resolve (or escalate) data discrepancies, broken feeds and tracking gaps.
  • Identify opportunities to improve dashboard usability and automate manual reporting steps, reducing time spent on assembly and increasing time spent on insight.
  • Help uphold data governance standards, including UTM strategy, naming conventions and consistent metric definitions.

Coordination & Project Management

  • Use Wrike to raise, track and progress requests for creative assets, landing pages, email support and web updates, ensuring campaigns have everything they need ahead of launch.
  • Coordinate across Design/Studio, Web, Content, CRM, Sales and regional marketing teams, and external agency partners, to keep delivery on schedule.
  • Chase, unblock and communicate: keep stakeholders informed of status, dependencies and risks before they become problems.
  • Ensure creative and landing pages meet platform specifications, brand guidelines and tracking requirements before going live.

title: Managing Technical Consultant, Civil Engineer
description:
Step into a leadership role where your technical expertise shapes complex infrastructure projects and your mentorship helps build the next generation of engineers—while driving sustainable impact across some of the world’s most critical industries.

Why This Role Matters

As a Managing Technical Consultant, Civil Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in delivering high-impact engineering solutions that support sustainability, climate resilience, and ESG priorities. This position goes beyond design—you will influence how major industrial, energy, and manufacturing projects are planned, executed, and improved, while helping grow a high-performing engineering team.

What Your Impact Is

  • Lead and contribute to complex, multidisciplinary engineering projects across renewable energy, manufacturing, technology, and industrial sectors

  • Drive sustainable and resilient design solutions aligned with evolving ESG standards

  • Mentor and guide early-career engineers, strengthening team capability and engagement

  • Collaborate with senior leaders to shape project strategy, execution, and client outcomes

  • Deliver high-quality, compliant designs that directly support critical infrastructure development and environmental performance

What You'll Bring

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or related field

  • 6+ years of progressive civil engineering experience

  • Strong experience in site design, grading, drainage, and permitting

  • Proficiency in AutoCAD/Civil 3D and related modeling tools (e.g., Hydraflow)

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and contribute both independently and within teams

  • Strong analytical skills with experience preparing engineering calculations and technical reports

  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey complex technical concepts clearly

  • Knowledge of local codes, permitting, and regulatory requirements

  • Driver's License Required: This position requires a valid driver's license and/or the ability to operate a company vehicle due to the nature of job duties, which include frequent travel to various client locations across a large geographical area.

  • This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship.

Preferred

  • PE or FE certification

  • Master’s degree or advanced education

  • Experience leading or mentoring junior engineering staff

  • Background in land development design including utilities, stormwater, and erosion control

  • Exposure to renewable energy (solar, wind), data centers, oil & gas, or industrial facilities

  • Familiarity with GIS, surveying principles, geotechnical, or remediation projects

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the design and oversight of site layout, grading, drainage systems, and infrastructure from concept through construction

  • Develop and review construction drawings, specifications, and contract documents

  • Perform engineering analysis, evaluate field data, and prepare detailed technical reports

  • Support environmental and compliance-related engineering work across diverse projects

  • Mentor junior staff and promote technical excellence and professional growth

  • Ensure adherence to health, safety, and quality standards

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams and stakeholders to deliver projects on time and within scope

For the Managing Technical Consultant, Civil Engineer position, the anticipated annual base pay is $103,967–$132,573 (USD). Actual pay will depend on factors such as education, experience, skills, location, performance, and business needs. In some cases, pay may fall outside this range. This role may be eligible for bonus pay (casual and fixed term/flex force employees are not bonus eligible).

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off, parental leave, medical, dental, vision, life, disability, AD&D insurance, 401(k) or RRSP/DPSP, and other applicable benefits to eligible employees.

Note: Bonuses, commissions, and other forms of additional compensation are not guaranteed and subject to the sole discretion of ERM and its policies and procedures.

Who We Are:
As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

title: Project Planner
description:
Job Title

Project Planner

Job Description Summary

The Project Planner will be responsible for developing, monitoring, and controlling project schedules for large-scale hotel, resort, and hospitality construction projects. The role will ensure effective planning, progress tracking, resource optimization, and timely project delivery while supporting project leadership with accurate forecasting and reporting.

Job Description

About the Role:

  • Develop, maintain, and monitor integrated project schedules for hotel, resort, and hospitality construction projects from design through handover.

  • Prepare detailed project plans, work breakdown structures (WBS), resource-loaded schedules, critical path analyses, and project progress reports using Primavera P6 and/or MS Project.

  • Coordinate with project managers, consultants, architects, contractors, and stakeholders to ensure alignment of project milestones and deliverables.

  • Track project performance against baseline schedules, identify delays and risks, and recommend recovery plans and mitigation strategies.

  • Generate periodic progress reports, dashboards, earned value analysis, and executive presentations to support project decision-making.

  • Review contractor schedules, evaluate extension of time (EOT) claims, and monitor compliance with contractual project timelines.

  • Support cost and project controls teams through schedule integration, forecasting, and planning-related analyses.

About You:

  • Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, or a related discipline.

  • Minimum 10 years of relevant experience in project planning and scheduling for hotel, resort, or hospitality, construction projects.

  • Strong expertise in Primavera P6, MS Project, project controls, critical path methodology (CPM), and project scheduling techniques.

  • Proven experience in managing complex hospitality development projects from concept/design stage through construction and commissioning.

  • Excellent analytical, reporting, stakeholder management, communication, and problem-solving skills.

  • Knowledge of construction contracts, claims management, risk assessment, and project control best practices.

  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment with multiple stakeholders and project teams.

Why Join Us?

  • Opportunity to work on prestigious hotel, resort, and hospitality developments across diverse locations.

  • Exposure to large-scale projects with international standards and best-in-class project management practices.

  • Strong focus on professional development, technical training, and career growth opportunities.

  • Collaborative and inclusive work environment that values innovation, excellence, and continuous improvement.

We have a vision of the future, where people simply belong.

We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where every individual is respected and valued. We celebrate diversity across all backgrounds and experiences and believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation and success.
