title: Yard Associate
location: Owen Equipment - 20 - Salt Lake City, UT 84104
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Yard Associate supports daily branch operations by maintaining a safe, clean, organized, and customer-ready equipment yard. This position is responsible for staging, moving, inspecting, cleaning, fueling, loading, unloading, and tracking equipment while also supporting service, rental, sales, parts, and delivery activity. The role requires strong attention to safety and detail, dependable follow-through, good communication, and the ability to work outdoors year-round in all weather conditions while working around heavy equipment, trucks, trailers, forklifts, customers, technicians, vendors, and branch personnel.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Yard Operations & Equipment Handling

  • Maintain the equipment yard, storage areas, loading areas, walkways, and traffic lanes in a clean, organized, and safe condition.
  • Stage, park, retrieve, reposition, load, and unload equipment, attachments, tools, parts, and materials using forklifts, pallet jacks, trucks, trailers, or other equipment as required.
  • Assist customers, drivers, technicians, rental staff, sales staff, and vendors with yard activity, equipment movement, loading, unloading, pickup, delivery, and branch support needs.
  • Perform basic yard checks, including confirming equipment location, documenting visible damage, checking fuel or fluid levels when assigned, and identifying equipment that needs service, cleaning, repair, or management follow-up.
  • Assist with general yard upkeep as needed, including mowing, trimming, edging, debris removal, and maintaining a clean, safe, and organized outdoor work area.

Equipment Readiness, Inventory & Branch Support

  • Wash, clean, fuel, organize, and prepare equipment and attachments for rental, sale, service, delivery, customer pickup, or internal use as directed.
  • Support inbound and outbound equipment inspections by documenting condition, missing items, damage, yard location, fuel level, attachments, accessories, and other required information.
  • Assist with inventory control by helping locate equipment, attachments, parts, tools, and supplies; report discrepancies, missing items, damage, or safety concerns to management.
  • Follow all safety policies, yard procedures, traffic flow requirements, PPE requirements, equipment operating rules, and housekeeping standards while working in the shop, yard, and loading areas.

QUALIFICATIONS / EXPERIENCE

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred; one or more years of yard, warehouse, equipment, rental, construction, logistics, material handling, automotive, truck, agricultural, or industrial work experience preferred.
  • Experience operating forklifts, trucks, trailers, or other material-handling equipment preferred; must be willing and able to complete required training and operate equipment safely. CDL and/or Forklift Certification a plus.
  • Basic mechanical aptitude and comfort working around heavy equipment, trucks, trailers, attachments, tools, parts, fluids, and outdoor industrial yard conditions.
  • Strong verbal communication skills with the ability to work professionally with customers, drivers, technicians, vendors, sales staff, rental staff, managers, and corporate departments.
  • Must be dependable, safety-focused, organized, customer-focused, able to follow instructions, ask clarifying questions, report issues promptly, and work independently or as part of a team in a fast-paced branch environment.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS / WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Work is primarily performed outdoors in an equipment yard and active service branch environment, with regular exposure to vehicles, forklifts, trucks, trailers, moving equipment, parts areas, wash areas, and shop operations.
  • Must be comfortable working in normal yard and shop conditions, including noise, dust, exhaust, grease, fluids, weather changes, uneven surfaces, moving equipment, and other industrial surroundings.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, squat, crouch, kneel, climb, reach, push, pull, twist, and use hands and arms throughout the workday.
  • Ability to lift, carry, push, or pull items up to 50 lbs. as needed; heavier items must be moved with assistance or approved material-handling equipment.
  • Must follow all posted safety rules and wear required PPE when working in the yard, shop, loading areas, wash areas, or around operating equipment.

TRAVEL AND SCHEDULE EXPECTATIONS

  • Standard Monday-Friday schedule, with occasional overtime, weekend work, or schedule adjustments based on customer, delivery, rental, service, or business needs.
  • Regular and predictable attendance is required.

title: SOESD - Low Voltage Technician Apprentice
description:
Southern Oregon ESD is seeking a Low Voltage Technician Apprentice who is able to perform journeyperson-level skilled electrical work in repair, alteration, construction, installation, and maintenance of electrical systems and equipment; and perform related duties as assigned by the Electrical Supervisor.
Duties include installation, maintenance, and repair of extended branch circuits, audiovisual equipment, and intercom systems, network cabling, security cameras, and other electrical and limited energy systems and equipment. The successful candidate would also ensure that electrical work performed at SOESD is in accordance with standard practices of the trade and in compliance with state and local regulations. A variety of shifts are available.

About SOESD

Southern Oregon ESD has locations in the Rogue Valley and Klamath County. The Rogue Valley is the cultural and economic heart of southern Oregon, home to legendary snow-skiing, white-water rafting, kayaking, hiking, fishing, as well as numerous cultural venues and events such as art galleries, the Britt Music Festivals, the Ashland Independent Film Festival, and the renowned Oregon Shakespeare Festival, the Ashland Independent Film Festival, and the renowned Oregon Shakespeare Festival.


Low Voltage Technician Apprentice

POSITION GOAL: The Limited Energy Technician Apprentice is responsible for assisting in the installation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of low-voltage systems and infrastructure. This includes voice/data cabling, surveillance, fire alarm, and security systems, intercom, audio/visual, and other limited energy systems. The technician ensures all work is completed in compliance with Oregon codes and safety regulations and supports a safe learning environment for students and staff.


Essential Duties:

1. Install, maintain, and repair various low-voltage systems, including LAN, PA, CCTV, CATV, intercom, A/V systems, wireless access points, fire and security alarms, fiber, and classroom technologies.
2. Read and interpret blueprints, schematics, specifications, and technical manuals to perform skilled installations and repairs in accordance with applicable codes.
3. Conduct diagnostic testing, perform system checks, and troubleshoot limited energy equipment to ensure reliable operation.
4. Collaborate with staff, contractors, and other trades during construction, renovation, or system upgrades to coordinate low-voltage service needs.
5. Estimate time, labor, and materials required for assigned tasks and submit requisitions for materials and equipment.
6. Maintain records of services provided, parts used, and system configurations to ensure accurate documentation.
7. Assist with the evaluation, design, and planning of new systems and infrastructure.
8. Maintain safe working conditions, follow OSHA, OR-OSHA, and district safety guidelines, and promptly report any hazards or incidents.
9. Participate in the training and mentorship of team members or temporary staff as assigned.
10. Attend job-related workshops and in-service trainings to maintain current knowledge of industry practices and code requirements.
11. Operate power tools and mechanical lift equipment safely; maintain and transport necessary tools, materials, and equipment.
12. Assist in obtaining and maintaining permits as needed from regulatory agencies for project compliance.
13. Assist in the training of other personnel in the department.
14. Direct supervision by a licensed LEA journeyman (or supervising electrician with equivalent license) is required.
15. Communicate clearly and appropriately.
16. Participate in professional growth activities.
17. Establish and maintain cooperative work relationships with SOESD employees, local education agency representatives, and others contacted during the course of the workday.
18. Follow established SOESD policies and procedures.
19. Perform physical requirements unaided or with the assistance of reasonable accommodation.
20. Perform other job-related duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Minimum Qualifications:

1. High School Diploma or GED.
2. Valid Oregon Driver's License and safe driving record.
3. Must be enrolled and actively completing coursework related to the LEA licensing program or hold a Valid Oregon Limited Energy-A (LEA) or Limited Energy-B (LEB) license, Oregon Limited Energy Limited Journeyman, or equivalent.
4. Minimum five (5) years of experience in the installation and repair of low-voltage systems.
5. Knowledge of applicable Oregon Building Codes, National Electrical Code, and safety practices.
6. Ability to read and interpret technical drawings and perform accurate installations to specification.
7. Skilled in using testing tools, repair equipment, ladders, lifts, and computers.
8. Proficient in the use of productivity software and internet-based research to support field service documentation and solutions.
9. Ability to communicate effectively, follow oral and written instructions, and maintain positive working relationships with diverse stakeholders.
10. Knowledge of safety procedures, guidelines, and rules.

title: Network Administrator
description:
Job Title: Network Administrator

Reports to: Technology Coordinator

Dept./School: Technology

Exemption Status/Test: Exempt


Primary Purpose:

Administer and operate the district’s central administrative computer networks. Develop, maintain, and monitor all district local area networks (LAN), wireless local area networks (WLAN), and wide area networks (WAN). Responsible for installation, testing, and oversight of all network hardware, personal computers, software, and related equipment.

Qualifications:

Education/Certification:

Bachelor’s degree in computer science or management information systems, or equivalent experience in network administration

Certified Novell Engineer certification (CNE) (include if applicable)

Microsoft Certified Solutions Expert certification (MCSE) (include if applicable)

Cisco Certified Networking Professional (CCNP) (include if applicable)

Special Knowledge/Skills:

Knowledge of LAN, LWAN, and WAN network design and installation

Knowledge of network hardware and software applications including network servers, printers, and other equipment

Ability to work with multiple operating systems and network protocols

Ability to analyze and resolve computer network problems

Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills

Major Responsibilities and Duties:

Network Management

  1. Oversee the installation and testing of network hardware, software, and upgrades, and identify and resolve issues. Implement and maintain all system configurations, and ensure that system maintenance is performed.
  2. Monitor and analyze system utilization; recommend improvements as needed.

Network Security

  1. Develop and oversee implementation and maintenance of security for all systems and networks.
  2. Develop and implement backup procedures to ensure that all network and workstation backups are performed on a regular basis and district data is restored as needed.
  3. Assist with the development and implementation of a disaster recovery plan.

Technical Support

  1. Serve as liaison to software and hardware vendors to maintain appropriate product support.
  2. Develop and maintain network design and configuration documentation. Consult with end users to identify need, analyze systems specifications, and correct related problems.

Other

  1. Identify and recommend the acquisition of software and hardware to meet the networking needs of the district.
  2. Compile, maintain, and file all reports, records, and other documents required.
  3. Comply with policies established by federal and state law, State Board of Education rule, and local board policy.
  4. Follow district safety protocols and emergency procedures.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

Monitor the work and issue work assignments to network and computer technicians.

Mental Demands/Physical Demands/Environmental Factors:

Tools/Equipment Used: Hand tools and test instruments for electronic repairs and cable installations; standard office equipment including personal computers and peripherals

Posture: Prolonged sitting; regular kneeling/squatting, bending/stooping, pushing/pulling, twisting

Motion: Repetitive hand motion; frequent keyboarding and use of mouse; regular walking, grasping/squeezing, wrist flexion/extension, reaching; may climb ladders

Lifting: Regular moderate lifting and carrying (up to 44 pounds); occasional heavy lifting and carrying (45 pounds and over)

Environment: Work is performed in an office environment; frequent on-call and after-hours work; occasional districtwide travel; may be required to be on-call 24 hours a day.

Mental Demands: Work with frequent interruptions; emotional control under stress

title: Senior Consultant, Financial Crimes
description:
About Northern Trust


As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions.


Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide.


With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service.



Financial Crimes Data Management

Senio Consultant, Risk Analytics

Position Summary

Northern Trust's Risk Data Management team is seeking a highly motivated Consultant, Risk Analytics to support Financial Crimes programs including AML, KYC, Transaction Monitoring, Screening, Regulatory Reporting, and Financial Crimes Data Modernization initiatives. This role will serve as a key liaison between business stakeholders, technology teams, and upstream data providers to improve data quality, resolve production issues, enhance reporting capabilities, and deliver strategic data solutions. The successful candidate will lead issue management activities, develop key risk and data quality metrics, monitor trends, and contribute to the design and implementation of scalable data solutions that strengthen the firm's Financial Crimes risk management framework.

Primary Responsibilities

Data Management & Analytics

  • Lead and support data-focused initiatives across Financial Crimes disciplines including KYC, Screening, Transaction Monitoring, and Financial Crimes Reporting.
  • Perform data analysis to identify trends, anomalies, root causes, and opportunities for process improvement.
  • Develop and maintain key risk indicators (KRIs), key performance indicators (KPIs), operational metrics, and management reporting dashboards.
  • Monitor data quality trends and recommend remediation strategies to improve completeness, accuracy, consistency, and timeliness of critical data elements.
  • Create executive-level reporting and presentations that provide insights into financial crime risks, operational performance, and data quality outcomes.

Production Issue Management

  • Coordinate the identification, tracking, escalation, and resolution of production issues affecting Financial Crimes applications and data feeds.
  • Lead root cause analysis efforts and partner with technology, operations, and business teams to drive timely resolution of incidents.
  • Establish controls and monitoring processes to proactively identify data issues before they impact downstream processes or regulatory reporting.
  • Maintain issue logs, remediation plans, and status reporting for management and governance forums.

Business & Data Partner Engagement

  • Develop strong partnerships with upstream data providers, technology teams, Master Data Management (MDM), compliance partners, and business stakeholders.
  • Act as a trusted advisor on data requirements, data quality expectations, and business impacts.
  • Facilitate requirements gathering sessions and translate business needs into actionable data and technology solutions.
  • Support data governance activities including data lineage, ownership, controls, metadata management, and data quality assessments.

Strategic Initiatives

  • Participate in Financial Crimes modernization programs focused on improving data architecture, reporting, automation, and risk measurement capabilities.
  • Support implementation and testing activities for new data integrations, system enhancements, and regulatory requirements.
  • Assist with audit, compliance, and regulatory inquiries by providing data analysis, documentation, and traceability of reporting results.
  • Contribute to the development of sustainable operating models that improve transparency, accountability, and data governance across Financial Crimes programs.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in business, Finance, Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Analytics, or a related field.
  • 3-7 years of experience in risk management, financial crimes, compliance, data management, data analytics, or regulatory reporting.
  • Experience working with financial services data and business processes.
  • Experience supporting large-scale data, reporting, or transformation initiatives preferred.

Required Skills

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Advanced SQL and data analysis skills.
  • Experience with reporting and visualization platforms such as Power BI, Sigma, and other business intelligence tools.
  • Ability to investigate data anomalies, perform root cause analysis, and communicate findings effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Strong project management, issue management, and organizational skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to build effective partnerships across business, technology, risk, and compliance teams.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience supporting Financial Crimes, AML, KYC, Screening, Sanctions, Fraud, or Transaction Monitoring programs.
  • Knowledge of data governance, metadata management, data quality, data lineage, and master data management concepts.
  • Experience with data architecture, data modeling, business architecture, and strategic solution design supporting enterprise data initiatives.
  • Familiarity with modern data platforms and cloud-based analytics environments including Databricks and/or Snowflake.
  • Experience working with Actimize, Fenergo, Master Data Management (MDM) platforms, or other financial crime, risk, and compliance technology solutions.
  • Experience supporting large-scale data modernization, regulatory reporting, or enterprise analytics initiatives.
  • Familiarity with data products, semantic layers, ontologies, and modern data management frameworks used to improve data discoverability, consistency, and business consumption.
  • Understanding of regulatory expectations related to AML, KYC, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, and financial crimes compliance.


Working with Us


As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve.


Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities.


Reasonable Accommodation


Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing adjustments to individuals with health conditions and disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com, or alternatively you can discuss your individual requirements with the recruiter you are working with.



About Our Bangalore Office


The Northern Trust Bangalore office, established in 2005, is home to over 5,600 employees. In this stunning office space, we offer fantastic amenities which include our Arrival Hub - Jungle, the GameZone, and the Employee Experience Zone that appeal to both clients and employees. Learn more.

title: Computer Technician
description:
Position Purpose:
Under the general supervision of the Director of Technology, to maintain the school district's computer and network equipment in operating condition, meeting the technology needs of the district; troubleshooting and repairing computer hardware and software, and resolving immediate computer operational problems.

Essential Performance Responsibilities:

  • Installs and maintain computer operating systems, application software, and related computer equipment.
  • Performs computer and network hardware and software repair (computers, servers, switches, printers, scanners, and programs).
  • Creates and maintains E-Mail and Internet accounts on computers; configures E-Mail and security on computers.
  • Inspects computer and network equipment requiring specialized computer repair and troubleshooting for the purpose of identifying and verifying repair needs.
  • Assesses malfunctions of hardware for the purpose of determining appropriate actions to maintain computer and network operations.
  • Provides technical support to users of hardware and software.
  • Maintains the school-based computer labs in good working order.
  • Trains selected individuals for the purpose of ensuring their ability to use computer systems and new or existing software.
  • Coordinates computer and network-related repair requests.
  • Assists in record-keeping regarding the functioning and inventory of the school district's computers and related equipment, repairs, etc.
  • Assists in making recommendations regarding the purchase of new computers, software, and related equipment.

Additional Duties:
Performs other related tasks as assigned.

Note:

The above description is illustrative of tasks and responsibilities. It is not meant to be all inclusive of every task or responsibility.

Equipment:
Uses computers, servers, switches, scanners and printers, and related equipment.

Travel Requirements:
Travel to school district locations to repair hardware, install software and assist end users.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Extensive knowledge of computer hardware and software installation procedures.
  • Knowledge of all school district personal computer and software applications.
  • Understanding of current operating platforms, computer hardware and associated peripherals, and software applications.
  • Ability to inspect, assess, troubleshoot and repair computer network system, hardware and software.
  • Ability to work independently.
  • Extensive knowledge of E-Mail, Internet, WAN, LAN, and other computer network programs and operations.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with all levels of end-users.
  • Ability to follow oral and/or written instructions.
  • Ability to report work orally and/or in writing to supervisor.
  • Ability to establish and, maintain cooperative working relationship with, staff and others contacted in the course of work.
  • Ability to carry out instructions furnished in written or oral form.
  • Ability to add, subtract, multiply and divide, and perform complex arithmetic operations.

title: Instructional Technology Coach (10.5 month position)
description:
The Instructional Technology Coach empowers educators to integrate technology effectively into teaching and learning. ITCs serve as collaborative partners, instructional leaders, and professional learning facilitators who help teachers design engaging, student-centered lessons that leverage digital tools and strategies. They focus on building teacher capacity, fostering innovation, and supporting continuous improvement in instructional practices.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Coaching and Collaboration
• Partner with teachers to plan, model, and co-teach lessons that integrate technology to enhance student learning.
• Provide individualized and small group coaching to support instructional goals and technology integration.
• Facilitate reflective conversations with educators to improve instructional practices and student outcomes.


2. Professional Learning
•Design and deliver professional learning sessions on effective technology integration, digital pedagogy, and instructional strategies.
•Support teachers in developing personalized learning environments and incorporating learner variability.
•Engage in ongoing professional learning related to content, pedagogy, technology, and leadership.
•Maintain active participation in professional learning networks at local, state, and national levels.


3. Digital Leadership and Innovation
•Promote digital citizenship and model ethical, safe, and responsible technology use.
•Guide educators in selecting and implementing digital tools aligned with curriculum standards and instructional goals.
•Stay current with emerging technologies, instructional trends, and best practices to inform coaching strategies.


4. Data-Informed Support
•Collaborate with teachers to analyze student data and identify opportunities for technology-enhanced learning.
•Assist in evaluating the impact of technology integration on student engagement and achievement.


5. Technical and Instructional Expertise
•Demonstrate proficiency in troubleshooting classroom technologies and supporting teachers with technical challenges.
•Understand and apply instructional design principles to create meaningful technology-rich learning experiences.


QUALIFICATIONS
•Education: Bachelor’s degree in education (master’s preferred).
•Certification: Valid teaching license.
•Experience: Minimum of five years of successful classroom teaching experience.
•Skills: Strong instructional design, coaching, communication, and technology integration skills.


TIME ALLOCATION OF RESPONSIBILITIES (Suggested Time Approximations)
• 50% coaching and collaboration (planning, modeling, and co-teaching lessons with teachers, small group/one-on-one coaching sessions, reflective conversations, and instructional planning)
• 20% professional learning (designing, delivering, and participating in PD)
• 15% digital leadership and innovation (researching and sharing instructional technology tools and best practices, supporting school-wide and division-wide technology initiatives)
• 10% data-informed support (collaborating with schools during PLCs and grade-level meetings on utilizing technology tools to assist with identified areas of need, evaluating the impact of technology integration on learning outcomes)
• 5% technical support (troubleshooting basic classroom technology issues, assisting with setup and basic operations)


REPORTING STRUCTURE
Reports to the Supervisor of Instructional Technology.


ADDITIONAL EXPECTATIONS
•Familiarity with Virginia Standards of Learning, ISTE Standards for Coaches, and Virginia Technology Standards for Instructional Personnel (VSTE).
•Commitment to fostering a culture of innovation and continuous improvement in teaching and learning.

description:

Role
The Systems Engineer I designs, architects and implements complex hardware deployments, software installations/upgrades and significant operational initiatives including highly available web services, Storage Area Networks, SQL databases, Microsoft Active Directory Infrastructure, messaging systems, and other application services.

Essential Functions

Reporting directly to the Supervisor of IT Infrastructure and Security, the Systems Engineer I performs the following duties:

  • Manage the day-to-day operations of data center assigned staff and resources including scheduling upgrades and maintenance that minimally impact core business and instructional functions. This will include performing off hour upgrades, installing patches, service packs, troubleshooting, etc.
  • Perform project management responsibilities including budgeting, RFP development, Disaster Recovery planning, etc.
  • Perform Multi-tiered incident, change management and problem resolution.
  • Securely design and implement key IT infrastructure including scalable web services, Storage Area Networks, internet/intranet services, SQL databases, server virtualization, messaging systems, Active Directory, File Print, and other servers and services.
  • Maintain Public Key Infrastructure. Implements and maintains Information Systems security as mandated by state, county, and internal requirements. Performs routine system audits and vulnerability assessments, verifies IS security compliance.
  • Monitor faults, performance, and capacity issues; prepares remediation reports and documentation.
  • Proactively researches, analyzes, identifies, and resolves trends of utilization or errors.
  • Program, design, and implement applications and scripts to facilitate and automate operational tasks such as disaster recovery, backups, reporting, import/export of user and student information, account maintenance, Active Directory administrative, etc.
  • Continuously identifies opportunities for process and quality improvement and implements applicable technologies and/or process changes.
  • Architect and implement highly available infrastructure including design and test of clustered/fail-over services, fault tolerance, disaster recovery, load balancing, etc.
  • Architect and implement systems management and proactive monitoring tools.
  • Integrity verification, performance tuning, backup, restore, and maintenance of enterprise SQL databases.
  • Implement and oversee large, complex backup systems using OST, NDMP, data deduplication, replication and snapshots technologies. Protect all systems and end user data: schedule and maintain onsite and offsite backups, review backup logs, develop and maintain backup procedures, documenting recovery plans and implement new backup technologies.
  • Document all system administration processes and installation procedures.
  • Updates job knowledge by participating in educational opportunities; reading professional publications; maintaining personal networks; participating in professional organizations.

  • Remain technically current and competent by learning new technologies and obtaining certifications as requested by management.
  • Oversees software/hardware maintenance contracts and manages network services agreements.
  • Manage purchasing of Information Systems infrastructure.
  • Performs other duties as required.


Performs other duties as assigned by the Supervisor of IT Infrastructure and Security.


Required Qualifications

  • Microsoft MCSE/MCITP, VMWare VCP or BS degree in computers or information/system technology.
  • Four (4) years' full time experience providing network management support within a large scale network infrastructure including backup and restore functions, virus protection, patch remediation, implementing/administering Microsoft Server and active directory services.
  • Six (6) years' experience administering Microsoft Server 200x and active directory services may be substituted for the MCSE/BS/VCP.
  • Experience implementing and administering Storage Area Networks or NAS.
  • Experience with programming scripts such as VBS or PowerShell.
  • Two (2) years' experience administering Microsoft Exchange or other messaging systems and two (2) years' experience administering server virtualization technologies (VMWare, Hyper-v), SQL or SAN technologies.
  • Experience with an ability to implement, configure and troubleshoot Windows Servers and services, Active Directory, NAS shares, group policies, provision storage, package and deploy network based applications, etc.
  • Experience and broad knowledge of TCP/IP, Ethernet, ACL's, VLANs, DHCP, DNS, SNMP, SMTP, iSCSI, RFC's, and other network protocols, etc.
  • Ability to work off-hours as needed/required.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with minimal supervision.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently and effectively complete work assignments and projects in a timely fashion. Demonstrated ability to meet deadlines.
  • Capable of performing the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodations.
  • Regular and predictable attendance.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Possession of a Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university (Information Technology related field).
  • Experience architecting and implementing virtualization technologies.
  • Experience designing applications and/or experience with various programming languages.
  • Experience with Microsoft SCCM and/or Microsoft Systems Center Operation Manager.
  • Experience administering SQL, implementing SQL clustering and managing SQL database backups and restoration.
  • Experience designing and implementing Microsoft Lync, Microsoft SharePoint or other collaboration technologies.
  • Experience architecting and implementing high availability systems.
  • Work experience in K-12 educational setting.

title: R2R Associate
description:
ERM is the world’s largest specialist sustainability consultancy, with over 50 years of experience helping organizations navigate complex environmental, social, and governance challenges. We bring together a global community of experts to deliver meaningful impact for our clients and the planet.

The Global Delivery Centre (GDC) in Gurugram is ERM’s global operating backbone. It delivers business enablement services in Finance, HR, IT, and Commercial Operations to ensure ERM’s global business runs seamlessly, efficiently, and consistently.

At the GDC, you will:

  • Be part of a hub that ensures ERM’s business continuity worldwide.

  • Collaborate with colleagues across geographies to support global operations.

  • Drive consistency, compliance, and efficiency in core functions.

  • Work with digital, automation, and AI-enabled tools to optimise how ERM operates.

  • Work in shifts where required, depending on the role. As processes mature and automation increases, reliance on shifts will reduce.

Why this role matters?

As a Record to Report Associate, you will support ERM’s global delivery by executing end-to-end accounting processes including month-end close, general ledger management, reconciliations, reporting, and compliance activities. You will work within Business Enablement Team, partnering with global stakeholders to ensure accuracy, timeliness, and integrity of financial statements while supporting audits and continuous improvement initiatives.


What your impact is?

  • Successfully manage month-end and year-end close activities, ensuring timely and accurate financial reporting.

  • Improved accuracy of financial statements through detailed balance sheet reconciliations and journal entry reviews.

  • Streamlined RTR processes, reducing turnaround time and enhancing operational efficiency.

  • Supporting internal and external audits by maintaining strong controls and complete documentation.

  • Collaborating with cross-functional teams to resolve accounting issues, ensuring compliance and reporting accuracy.

  • Contributing to process transitions and continuous improvement initiatives, enhancing productivity and service quality.

What you’ll bring:

  • 3-5 years of experience in R2R, General Ledger, and Payroll Accounting.

  • Strong knowledge of IFRS/GAAP, financial reporting, and accounting controls.

  • Experience with ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, or Workday.

  • Proficient in payroll reconciliations, salary accruals, and payroll journal entries.

  • Advanced Excel skills with strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

  • Effective stakeholder management and communication skills across Finance, HR, and Payroll teams.

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced Shared Services/GBS environment and meet strict reporting deadlines.

Preferred:

  • Exposure to Global Business Services (GBS), Shared Services, or multinational environments.

  • Familiarity with ERP platforms such as SAP, Oracle, Workday, or Dynamics 365.

  • Experience with payroll accounting, reconciliations, and financial reporting activities.

  • Exposure to automation tools, Power BI, Alteryx, RPA, or AI-enabled finance solutions.

  • Experience in process improvement, standardization, and transition projects.

Key responsibilities:

1. Month-End Close & Reporting

  • Perform month-end, quarter-end, and year-end closing activities

  • Prepare journal entries, accruals, provisions, and adjustments.

  • Ensure timely and accurate submission of financial reports.

  • Analyze financial results and variances vs. budget/forecast.

2. General Ledger (GL) Accounting

  • Maintain and reconcile general ledger accounts.

  • Review and validate entries for accuracy and compliance with accounting standards.

  • Support chart of accounts maintenance and mapping activities.

3. Balance Sheet Reconciliations

  • Perform reconciliations for bank, intercompany, accruals, prepaid expenses, fixed assets, and other key accounts.

  • Investigate discrepancies and ensure timely resolution.

  • Maintain documentation as per audit and policy requirements.

4. Intercompany Activities

  • Process intercompany billings, settlements, and confirmations.

  • Resolve mismatches and discrepancies working with global teams.

5. Fixed Assets Accounting (if applicable)

  • Maintain asset register and execute capitalization/disposals.

  • Process depreciation runs and reconciles fixed asset schedules.

6. Process Improvement

  • Identify gaps and propose automation or standardization opportunities.

  • Participate in transitions, migrations, and system enhancement projects

Game on!

title: TECHNOLOGY ASSISTANT
description:
Technology Assistant

Purpose:

The Technology Assistant provides on-site, front-line technical support for elementary and middle schools, ensuring smooth daily operation of district devices, classroom technology, and instructional software. This position handles basic troubleshooting, enters and triages tickets, manages school-level technology inventory, and supports a positive, responsive customer service experience for staff and students.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong troubleshooting skills with the ability to diagnose and resolve basic hardware, software, and connectivity issues.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

Front-Line Technical Support

  • Serve as the first point of contact for staff and student technology issues in assigned schools.

Ticketing & Escalation

Device & Inventory Management

  • 10 Month Position

description:

As a Delivery Trainer, you are responsible for establishing the right delivery training culture in your delivery station, setting up the training experience, and independently instructing training sessions. You enable the success of Delivery Associates by adapting to different learning styles and taking a hands-on training approach to demonstrate what good looks like. As a Delivery Trainer, you are expected to lead by example and demonstrate the Amazon Leadership Principles at all times. Candidate must hold a valid state-appropriate driver’s license, be able to obtain and maintain their Driver Qualification File (DQF), and be eligible to drive in accordance with Department of Transportation (DOT) requirements.

What else does the team have to offer? We’re glad you asked!

title: Technology Assistant
description:

Responsibilities encompass the installation, configuration, and upkeep of a variety of educational technologies, including computers, peripherals, and classroom presentation systems.   • Basic understanding of computer hardware components, peripherals (printers, scanners, interactive panels), and their functionality.
  • Familiarity with basic networking concepts, including TCP/IP, DNS, and Wi-Fi.
  • Awareness of common software installation and troubleshooting techniques.
  • Understanding of basic user account management principles.
  • Familiarity with educational software and online learning platforms commonly used in K-12 environments (preferred).
  • Proficient in troubleshooting basic hardware and software issues.
  • Skill in installing, configuring, and updating operating systems and applications.
  • Effective problem-solving and analytical skills.Ability to follow technical instructions and procedures accurately.
  • Ability to learn and adapt to new technologies and software quickly.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Ability to maintain a positive and customer-focused attitude when providing support.
  • Ability to exercise discretion and maintain confidentiality regarding sensitive information.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following. This list is meant to be representative, not exhaustive. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The employee is required to follow all Board of Education policies and procedures and to comply with instructions and/or directives from his/her supervisor(s).

  1. Provide first-level technical support to school staff and, when appropriate, students via phone, email, or in person, addressing issues related to hardware, software, and basic network connectivity.
  2. Diagnose and resolve common technical problems involving desktop computers, laptops, printers, projectors, interactive whiteboards, and other classroom technology.
  3. Install, configure, and update operating systems, software applications, and drivers on school-owned devices.
  4. Perform basic hardware maintenance and repairs, such as replacing components, cleaning equipment, and running diagnostic tests.
  5. Assist users with connecting to the school network and troubleshooting basic network connectivity issues, including Wi-Fi access.
  6. Support the use of classroom technology by assisting teachers with setup, operation, and basic troubleshooting during instructional activities.
  7. Assist with the management of user accounts, including password resets and basic profile modifications.
  8. Maintain accurate records of technology inventory, repairs, and support activities using a ticketing system or other designated tools.
  9. Follow established IT procedures and protocols for troubleshooting, issue resolution, and documentation.
  10. Escalate complex technical issues that cannot be resolved at the first level to higher-level IT support personnel.
  11. Assist with the deployment and setup of new technology equipment.
  12. Provide basic training and guidance to users on the proper use of technology resources.
  13. Travel between school sites within the district as needed to provide on-site technical support.
  14. Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

PHYSICAL AND COGNITIVE REQUIREMENTS: The major physical and cognitive requirements listed below are applicable to the Technology Assistant job classification within Martin County Schools. Work in this classification is considered light physical work requiring the exertion of up to 20 pounds of force occasionally and a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to move objects.

Data Conception: Requires the ability to compare and/or judge the readily observable, functional, structural, or composite characteristics (whether similar to or divergent from obvious standards) of data, people or things.

Interpersonal Communication: Requires the ability to speak and/or signal people to convey or exchange information (includes receiving instructions, assignments and/or directions from superiors.)

Language Ability: Requires the ability to read a variety of correspondence, reports, handbooks, forms, lists, etc. and the ability to prepare correspondence, simple reports, forms, instructional materials, etc., using prescribed format.

Intelligence: Requires the ability to apply principles of logical or scientific thinking to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions; to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagrammatic form; and to deal with several abstract and concrete variables.

Verbal Aptitude: Requires the ability to record and deliver information, to explain procedures, to follow oral and written instructions. Must be able to communicate effectively and efficiently in variety of technical or professional languages including education terminology.

Numerical Aptitude: Requires the ability to utilize mathematical formulas; to add and subtract; multiply and divide; utilize decimals and percentages; and to apply the principles of descriptive statistics, statistical inference and statistical theory.

title: Anticipated - Systems Administration Specialist
description:
Systems Administration Specialist

Our Mission for Cambridge Lakes Learning Center is to educate children by cultivating curiosity, challenging minds, and inspiring excellence through collaborative learning experiences.

OUR VALUES IN ACTION. We're looking for professionals who value:

The Whole Child

Shared Responsibility

Curiosity in Action

Creative Problem Solving

Growth Through Challenge

Excellence with Integrity

AT CAMBRIDGE LAKES WE ARE ALL LEARNERS. Our staff is: Resilient, Principled, Playful, Explorers, Empathetic & Reflective.

POSITION SUMMARY. The Systems Administrator is responsible for the daily management, maintenance, and security of NKEC's technology infrastructure, including networks, devices, enterprise systems, and instructional technology platforms. This role ensures reliable, secure, and effective technology access for all staff and students, and serves as the primary technical resource for the organization.

PROFESSIONAL STAFF ROLE, REQUIRED SKILLS & COMPETENCIES. At Cambridge Lakes Learning Center, all staff are learners. In this role, you will:

Network & Infrastructure Management

  • Administer, monitor, and maintain NKEC's network infrastructure, including routers, switches, firewalls, wireless access points, and internet connectivity, ensuring reliable uptime and performance across all school sites.
  • Manage servers, cloud environments, and data storage systems; apply patches, updates, and configurations in accordance with security best practices and vendor guidance.
  • Proactively identify and resolve network performance issues, connectivity failures, and infrastructure vulnerabilities before they impact operations or instruction.

Device & Systems Administration

  • Deploy, configure, and maintain end-user devices, including staff laptops, student Chromebooks/iPads, printers, and peripheral equipment, across all NKEC locations.
  • Administer enterprise software systems, including the Student Information System (SIS), payroll/HR platforms, Google Workspace, and other institutional tools; manage user accounts, permissions, and system integrations.
  • Maintain hardware and software inventory; manage the technology asset lifecycle from procurement through retirement, including tracking, disposal, and replacement planning.

Cybersecurity & Data Privacy

  • Implement and maintain cybersecurity protocols, including endpoint protection, data encryption, access controls, and multi-factor authentication, in compliance with NKEC policy and applicable regulations.
  • Ensure compliance with FERPA, COPPA, and Illinois student data privacy requirements; maintain documentation and controls that protect student and staff data from unauthorized access.
  • Monitor system logs and security alerts; respond to incidents promptly and coordinate with leadership on breach response, recovery, and policy updates.

Instructional Technology Support

  • Provide responsive technical support to instructional staff, ensuring that classroom technology, including interactive displays, projectors, document cameras, and learning platforms, is operational and accessible.
  • Collaborate with academic leadership to evaluate, pilot, and implement instructional technology tools and platforms that support learning goals and the Cambridge Lakes Portrait of a Learner.
  • Deliver training and support resources that build staff confidence and proficiency with technology tools, platforms, and systems.

Help Desk & User Support

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for all technology support requests; triage, prioritize, and resolve issues efficiently through a help desk or ticketing system.
  • Maintain clear documentation of support requests, resolutions, system configurations, and procedures to enable continuity and knowledge transfer.
  • Communicate technical information in clear, accessible language to non-technical stakeholders; ensure staff feel supported and informed throughout issue resolution.

Vendor Management & Budget Support

  • Manage relationships with technology vendors, service providers, and contractors; coordinate procurement, licensing renewals, and service agreements.
  • Track technology expenditures and support administration in annual technology budget planning, including hardware refresh cycles, software licensing, and infrastructure upgrades.
  • Evaluate new technologies, tools, and platforms to improve operational efficiency, instructional effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness across NKEC.

CLLC Professional Standards

  • Demonstrate a high level of professionalism and customer service (UX) in all interactions with students, families, staff, and community stakeholders.
  • Communicate effectively (verbally and in writing) with supervisors and cross-functional colleagues.
  • Champion Cambridge Lakes' Professional Excellence Framework and model full engagement in professional responsibilities as outlined in the Guide to Excellence and Employee Handbook.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience considered.
  • 3–5+ years of experience in systems administration, IT support, or a related technical role; experience in a K–12 school or educational environment preferred.
  • Proficiency in network administration, Google Workspace administration, Microsoft environments, and device management platforms
  • Working knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks, data privacy regulations (FERPA, COPPA), and IT compliance best practices.
  • Relevant certifications (CompTIA A+, Network+, Security+, Google Certified Administrator, or equivalent) preferred.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, customer service orientation, and ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical users.

WORK ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Meet the standards outlined in the contract.
  • On-site role within a school setting; regular presence required across campus to support staff, students, and infrastructure needs.
  • Moderate physical activity, including equipment installation, cable management, and movement throughout the building; occasional lifting of equipment up to 40 lbs.
  • Schedule may include occasional early morning, evening, or weekend hours for system maintenance, upgrades, or emergency response.
  • Valid driver's license preferred; may require travel between NKEC sites on occasion.

OUR COMMITMENT TO YOU: PROFESSIONAL EXCELLENCE FRAMEWORK. We invest in staff success through our Professional Practice Advancement (PPA) program.

COMPENSATION

  • Competitive compensation with adjustments to align with the market and skills
  • Professional Practice Advancement (PPA) contingent bonus is paid out twice a year

FULL-TIME BENEFITS

  • Tuition-Free Preschool
  • Competitive Retirement Benefits, including Healthcare, Vision, and Dental (see Handbook & Guide to Excellence for most current benefits)

Salary Range: $52,000 – $72,000+ annually. Placement within the range is determined by relevant education, professional experience, and applicable certifications

title: Proaktiv Försäkringssäljare Företag (SAK)
description:
Är du en säljare ut i fingerspetsarna som triggas av högt tempo, tydliga mål och daglig kundkontakt? Vill du ta nästa steg i din karriär och arbeta i ett team där hög aktivitet och resultat står i fokus? Då är det dig vi söker!

Om rollen
Som proaktiv försäkringssäljare hos oss är din huvudsakliga uppgift att självständigt och målinriktat kontakta nya och befintliga företagskunder för att erbjuda våra försäkringslösningar. Du ansvarar för hela säljprocessen – från första kontakt till avslut – och arbetar aktivt med främst merförsäljning till befintliga kunder men även nykundsbearbetning.

Vi tror på kraften i hög aktivitet och vet att många kundkontakter är nyckeln till framgång. Därför får du tillgång till effektiva och moderna telefonverktyg som hjälper dig att nå ut till rätt kunder och maximera din försäljning varje dag. Du följs upp på tydliga KPI:er kopplat till antal kundkontakter, bokade möten och försäljningsresultat.

Du arbetar i ett engagerat team där vi stöttar och sporrar varandra mot gemensamma mål. Hos oss är det alltid högt i tak och vi firar framgångar tillsammans!

Vem söker vi?
Vi söker dig som är en driven, självgående och tävlingsinriktad säljare som har ett starkt inre driv, gillar att ta initiativ och motiveras av att arbeta mot tydliga mål och höga aktivitetsnivåer. Du är trygg i telefonen, har lätt för att skapa förtroende och älskar att göra affärer.

Vi ser gärna att du har:

  • Erfarenhet av försäljning via telefon
  • Erfarenhet av försäkringsrådgivning mot företag är meriterande

Vi erbjuder
Hos oss får du frihet under ansvar och möjlighet att påverka din egen och teamets framgång. Du får snabbt ta eget ansvar för kunddialoger och försäljning, och vi ger dig verktygen för att lyckas.

Ansökan
Är du redo att ta nästa steg? Skicka in din ansökan redan idag! Vi intervjuar löpande och tjänsten kan tillsättas innan sista ansökningsdag.

Standard Job Description

Assistant Protection Officer

Organizational Setting and Work Relationships
The Assistant Protection Officer reports to the Protection Officer or the Senior Protection Officer. Depending on the size and structure of the Office, the incumbent may have supervisory responsibility for protection staff including community-based protection, registration, resettlement and education. S/he provides functional protection guidance to information management and programme staff on all protection/legal matters and accountabilities. These include: statelessness (in line with the campaign to End Statelessness by 2024), Global Compact on Refugees (GCR) commitments, age, gender, diversity (AGD) and accountability to affected populations (AAP) through community-based protection, Child protection, Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention and response, gender equality, disability inclusion, youth empowerment, psycho-social support and PSEA, registration, asylum/refugee status determination, resettlement, local integration, voluntary repatriation, human rights standards integration, national legislation, judicial engagement, predictable and decisive engagement in situations of internal displacement and engagement in wider mixed movement and climate change/disaster-related displacement responses. S/he supervises protection standards, operational procedures and practices in protection delivery in line with international standards.

The Assistant Protection Officer is expected to coordinate quality, timely and effective protection responses to the needs of populations of concern (PoC), ensuring that operational responses in all sectors mainstream protection methodologies and integrate protection safeguards. The incumbent contributes to the design of a comprehensive protection strategy and represents the Organization externally on protection doctrine and policy as guided by the supervisor. S/he also ensures that PoC are meaningfully engaged in the decisions that affect them and support programme design and adaptations that are influenced by the concerns, priorities and capacities of them. To achieve this, the incumbent will need to build and maintain effective interfaces with communities of concern, authorities, protection and assistance partners as well as a broader network of stakeholders who can contribute to enhancing protection.

All UNHCR staff members are accountable to perform their duties as reflected in their job description. They do so within their delegated authorities, in line with the regulatory framework of UNHCR which includes the UN Charter, UN Staff Regulations and Rules, UNHCR Policies and Administrative Instructions as well as relevant accountability frameworks. In addition, staff members are required to discharge their responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core, functional, cross-functional and managerial competencies and UNHCR's core values of professionalism, integrity and respect for diversity.

Duties
- Stay abreast of political, social, economic and cultural developments that have an impact on the protection environment.
- Consistently apply International and National Law and applicable UN/UNHCR and IASC policy, standards and codes of conduct.
- Assist in providing comments on existing and draft legislation related to PoC.
- Provide legal advice and guidance on protection issues to PoC; liaise with competent authorities to ensure the issuance of personal and other relevant documentation.
- Conduct eligibility and status determination for PoC in compliance with UNHCR procedural standards and international protection principles.
- Promote and contribute to measures to identify, prevent and reduce statelessness.
- Contribute to a country-level child protection plan as part of the protection strategy.
- Contribute to a country-level education plan as part of the protection strategy.
- Provide inputs for the development of protection policies and standards within the AoR.
- Implement and monitor Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for all protection/solutions activities.
- Manage individual protection cases including those on GBV and child protection. Monitor, and intervene in cases of refoulement, expulsion and other protection incidents.
- Recommend durable solutions for the largest possible number of PoC through voluntary repatriation, local integration and where appropriate, resettlement.
- Assess resettlement needs and apply priorities for the resettlement of individuals and groups of refugees and other PoC.
- Contribute to the design, implementation and evaluation of protection related AGD based programming with implementing and operational partners.
- Contribute to and facilitate a programme of results-based advocacy with sectorial and/or cluster partners.
- Contribute to and facilitate effective information management through the provision of disaggregated data on populations of concern and their problems.
- Assist capacity-building initiatives for communities and individuals to assert their rights.
- Participate in initiatives to capacitate authorities, relevant institutions and NGOs to strengthen national protection related legislation and procedures.
- Intervene with authorities on protection issues.
- Assist the supervisor in deciding priorities for reception, interviewing and counselling for groups or individuals.
- Assist the supervisor in enforcing compliance of staff and implementing partners with global protection policies and standards of professional integrity in the delivery of protection services.
- Enforce compliance with, and integrity of, all protection standard operating procedures.

- Support the identification and management of risks and seek to seize opportunities impacting objectives in the area of responsibility. Ensure decision making in risk based in the functional area of work. Raise risks, issues and concerns to a supervisor or to relevant functional colleague(s).

title: Instructional Technology Specialist (Elem.) - JA Fair Preparatory School
description:
JOB GOAL:

To provide assistance to classroom teachers/students in the effective integration of technology to improve instruction and academic achievement.

TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT: Salary based on a teacher’s (9.75) month contract (200 days), plus benefits package. NOTE: Precise placement on the salary range will be determined based upon education and experience. FLSA: Exempt

QUALIFICATIONS:

  1. Bachelor’s degree (minimum). Master’s degree preferred.
  2. Valid Arkansas teacher certification.
  3. K-5 classroom teaching experience with the ability to effectively differentiate instructional and behavior management strategies for all grade levels.
  4. Successful background experiences in designing and delivering innovative technology lessons that are aligned with both the ISTE standards and AR Computer Science Standards for K-5.
  5. Successful experiences in planning and delivering educational technology professional development.
  6. Successful experience in working with both adults and students.
  7. Experiences in demonstrating exemplary classroom instructional practice for the purpose of effective best practices to improve student achievement results and close achievement gaps.
  8. Experience using Microsoft Office Suite, G-Suite (formerly known as GAFE), SMART Technologies, multiple platforms, OER (Open Educational Resources) and e-School applications.
  9. Experience in troubleshooting user end issues with multiple operating systems: iOS, Windows, and Chrome.
  10. Demonstrates ongoing professional development in the realm of educational technology to include seeking additional training, researching emerging technologies, following educational technology trends, and/or participation in professional organizations/networks related to educational technology.
  11. Evidence of a strong commitment to quality desegregated education.

Such alternatives and additions to the above qualifications may be deemed appropriate by the Superintendent. Such alternatives to the above qualifications as the Board may require.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

The following statements of duties and responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. These statements are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities required of all personnel within this position.

  1. Embrace the K-8 school configuration and best practices with high expectations and promote student success while adopting a student-centered focus that allows students to grow socially, emotionally, physically, and academically.
  2. Supports the vision and mission of JA Fair K-8 Preparatory School by working collaboratively with the administration and ALL staff to create a positive, safe and kid friendly learning environment.
  1. Demonstrates strong work ethics, a passion for creativity and always open minded to new and innovative ideas
  1. Conducts teacher in service sessions on the use and integration of educational technology during the school day and after school.
  2. Collaborates with teachers and facilitators in planning and the implementation of instruction related to differentiating instruction and providing interventions as needed while adhering to the district curriculum map.
  3. Coordinates with principal to plan, implement training, and support the integration of educational technology that aligns with the district curriculum.
  4. Assists students to provide a continuum of support by using assessment data to guide the learning process toward student achievement of the district’s content standards using a variety of manipulatives, technology, and hands-on activities to support individual and/or small group needs.
  5. Provides students with the digital math and literacy skills that they need to develop college/career readiness, prepare for online testing, etc., without sacrificing classroom instruction.
  6. Assists in planning and implementing upgrades and expansions of current district software such as e-School and other approved district software.
  7. Provides support for teachers using educational software to fully implement the literacy and mathematics curriculum, and models the integration of technology for teachers.
  8. Conducts student assessments to identify those eligible for intervention services on a regular basis and provides progress reports as required to plan instruction, and/or assist teachers in learning various assessment techniques.
  9. Regularly analyzes data, create documents, and monitors student progress to provide support for teachers, and maintains a variety of electronic files and/or records (e.g. Test data, student records, and other data regarding proficiency) for the purpose of determining student needs, in order present to staff to monitor and drive further instruction.
  10. Assist in overseeing online testing administration.
  11. Responsible for troubleshooting minor device and application problems, and explores and investigates emerging technologies.
  12. Oversees operation of Educational Technology learning lab plus computers in all classrooms.
  13. Ability to maintain cooperative working relationships, demonstrate sensitivity to and respect for a diverse population, ability to manage multiple deadlines and priorities, and excellent communication skills.
  14. Performs other duties as assigned.

Requirements are representative of minimum levels of knowledge, skills and/or abilities. To perform this job successfully, the incumbent will possess the abilities or aptitudes to perform each duty successfully. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Participate and successfully complete the required Project Lead the Way (PLTW) and The Leader in Me professional development beginning July, 2021 and continuing throughout the school year, both on and off contract.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, stand, walk, go up and down stairs, operate foot and hand controls, use a telephone and write. title: Information Technology (IT) Systems Specialist - Level III
description:
QUALIFICATIONS (Minimum)

An Associate or Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, with a minimum of 3 years of experience in systems administration, design, and support. Industry certifications such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator, VCP-DCV, or equivalent are preferred. Demonstrated experience in leading infrastructure projects and designing secure, scalable system architectures. The ability to obtain an entry-level project management certification within one year of the position start date is required.

Summary:

The IT Systems Specialist – Level III is a senior technical position responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining enterprise-level systems for internal and client environments. This role serves as a technical lead, contributes to strategic infrastructure planning, and builds and promotes solutions that support our customers. The Level III Specialist mentors junior staff and leads complex systems initiatives from concept through execution.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Design, implement, and maintain secure, scalable, and resilient systems architectures for internal and client environments, including virtualization platforms, storage systems, identity management, and cloud infrastructure.

  • Lead major infrastructure projects such as server migrations, virtualization upgrades, storage expansions, and cloud implementations, overseeing planning, documentation, testing, deployment, and fiscal oversight to ensure projects are completed on time and within budget.

  • Serve as project manager for assigned initiatives, ensuring deliverables are met, stakeholders are kept informed, and documentation is maintained with in-person coordination as needed

  • Provide Tier III support for escalated issues involving server infrastructure, storage platforms, virtualization, Active Directory, and core system services.

  • Design and test backup and recovery systems, and participate in disaster recovery planning and execution for critical systems.

  • Develop and enforce systems documentation standards, including architecture diagrams, configuration repositories, and operational procedures.

  • Research and evaluate emerging systems and cloud technologies, recommending improvements for performance, security, or efficiency.

  • Provide mentorship and guidance to Level I and II Systems Specialists, leading training and knowledge-sharing initiatives.

  • Collaborate with vendors, service providers, and district technology leads for systems-related procurement, licensing, and support.

  • Support compliance initiatives, enforce security policies, and recommend risk mitigation strategies to ensure uptime and data protection.

  • Participate in after-hours support rotations and emergency response as needed.

  • Conduct site audits, performance assessments, and capacity planning to ensure optimal system performance.

  • Maintain a valid driver’s license and access to reliable transportation for scheduled and unscheduled travel.

  • Stay current with industry trends and maintain professional certifications.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, emotional intelligence, and communication skills (written and verbal)
  • Explores, identifies, and develops entrepreneurial/alternative revenue generation inside and outside of BLaST IU region.

  • Lift and carry equipment weighing up to 50 pounds as required.

  • Perform other duties as assigned

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Proven leadership in guiding IT teams, delegating tasks, and ensuring the successful completion of complex systems projects.

  • Strong project management skills, including planning, prioritizing, and tracking progress on multiple initiatives, with the expectation of earning a recognized project management certification within one year of hire.

  • Ability to translate technical requirements into actionable plans for both technical staff and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Advanced knowledge of Windows Server and Linux/Unix operating systems, with the ability to oversee installation, configuration, optimization, and lifecycle management.

  • Expertise in virtualization platforms (VMware, Hyper-V), including advanced resource management, clustering, and performance tuning.

  • Deep understanding of Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, and related enterprise services.

  • Proficiency in enterprise storage solutions (SAN, NAS) and related protocols (iSCSI, NFS, SMB).

  • Experience designing, implementing, and managing enterprise backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity strategies.

  • Advanced knowledge of cloud platforms (Microsoft 365, Azure, Google Workspace) and hybrid integrations.

  • Strong grasp of security best practices, including systems hardening, patch management, access control, and multi-factor authentication.

  • Ability to oversee scripting and automation initiatives for operational efficiency.

  • Familiarity with monitoring, alerting, and capacity planning tools for maintaining high system performance and availability.

  • Knowledge of compliance requirements and technology planning specific to educational environments.

  • Skilled in fostering collaboration between IT staff, administrators, and end-users to improve processes and user experience.

title: Skap ferskvaredisken du selv ville handlet i – på MENY Greverud ser vi etter ny ferskvaresjef
description:
I MENY elsker vi mat! For oss er god mat en lidenskap, og noe av det viktigste som finnes. Hos oss er alle MATarbeidere, uansett om du jobber i ferskvaredisken, kolonialen, i kassen eller på kontoret. Å være en MATarbeider i MENY betyr at du alltid gjør ditt beste for å veilede og inspirere kundene våre til matglede. Sammen skal vi hjelpe flere å spise bedre, og leve bedre.

MENY Greverud søker nå etter ferskvaresjef. Som vår nye ferskvaresjef får du et betydelig personal- og resultatansvar, og skal skape matglede gjennom andre - hver dag! Har du erfaring som leder og deler vår tanke om at spiser du bedre, lever du bedre, kan dette være jobben for deg.

Som ferskvaresjef forventes det at man fordeler sin tilstedeværelse gjennom hele butikkens åpningstid, men i hovedsak vil du arbeide på dagtid og annenhver helg.

Stillingsomfang: 100%
Arbeidstid: dag, kveld og helg
Oppstartsdato: snarest - eller etter avtale.

Søknadsfrist: Søknader vurderes fortløpende.

For å søke må du være fylt 18 år og du må kunne beherske norsk.

Hvem er den vi søker etter?
Som ferskvaresjef vil du arbeide med fisk, kjøtt, ost, delikatesser og bakeri, men først og fremst vil du jobbe med mennesker - både kunder og kollegaer. Du vil lede et team bestående av flere dyktige matarbeidere, så du må allerede være trygg i rollen som leder. Din viktigste oppgave blir å motivere, legge til rette for og utvikle dine MATarbeidere, så de kan levere god kundeservice og råvarer av topp kvalitet, sammen med deg.

Ved siden av å være personalleder vil du ha overordnet ansvar for ferskvareavdelingens økonomiske resultater som salg og svinn, IK-mat, bemanningsplanlegging og varebestilling. Du vil samarbeide tett med kjøpmann og assisterende butikksjef, og selv om dine ansvarsområder er definerte må du evne å se butikken som en helhet. Dagligvarebransjen er kontinuerlig i endring så du må kunne omstille deg, jobbe strukturert og effektivt, og ha stor arbeidskapasitet. Fordi du er en av kulturbærerne i butikken må du lede med eksempel, ha godt humør og være opptatt av arbeidsmiljø.

Vi ser for oss at vår ferskvaresjef har erfaring med personalansvar og har fagbrev som kokk, sjømathandler eller butikkslakter. Relevant erfaring eller genuin interesse i mat kan kompensere for fagbrev, det viktigste er at du er flink med folk og har selvinnsikt i lederrollen.

Arbeidsoppgaver:

  • Personalansvar for avdelingens MATarbeidere

  • Innkjøpsansvarlig og totalansvarlig for det økonomiske resultatet for hele ferskvareavdelingen

  • Kontakt med leverandører og kunder

  • Salg og produktveiledning

  • Ansvar for daglig drift av avdelingen

  • Trygg mat og våre internkontrollrutiner

  • Svinn og kvalitetskontroll

Hvorfor skal du jobbe hos oss?
Hos MENY Greverud får du en utfordrende lederstilling i Norges største dagligvarekonsern. Vi hjelper deg å bli god, og er opptatt av å gi grundig opplæring til alle vår ansatte. I MENY er det store muligheter for videre karriere, og vi tilbyr en rekke lederkurs, fantastiske kick-off og faglige samlinger. Her vil du ha varierte og morsomme dager på jobb, frihet under ansvar og gode kollegaer som bryr seg om hverandre.

Å søke jobb i MENY skal være enkelt

Du trenger ikke laste opp søknadsbrev. For at vi skal bli litt bedre kjent med deg, svarer du på spørsmålene om deg og din erfaring. Har du mye på hjertet må du gjerne skrive utfyllende, vi gleder oss til å lese! Og fordi vi synes det er spennende å se hvor du har vært tidligere, må du laste opp CV.

Vi gjør oppmerksom på at alle søknader må sendes inn via søknadsskjema tilknyttet annonsen, dette er av hensyn til ditt personvern, samt at vi ønsker å være sikre på at vi klarer å følge opp alle kandidater på en god måte. Vi kan derfor ikke ta imot søknader på papir i butikken eller via e-post. Søknader behandles fortløpende.
