title: Plumbing Subcode Official
description:
Description

Under direction of the Construction Official, has the subordinate administrative responsibility for administering the plumbing subcode of the State Uniform Construction Code within the concerned jurisdiction, and inspects and/or supervises the inspection of plumbing work in construction projects underway to ensure that compliance with plans and specifications approved in accord with the State Uniform Construction Code is achieved; does related work as required.

Examples of Duties

  • Reviews and approves plans of proposed structures as provided in State Uniform Construction Code regulations for conformity with plumbing and energy subcodes.  
  • Has charge of plumbing inspection staff and activities concerned in the inspection of construction projects.  
  • Develops the inspection work program with effective and appropriate procedures, analyses construction inspection problems, and establishes appropriate work methods.  
  • Has final responsibility in the inspection for plumbing and energy subcode compliance of all new construction and renovation projects.  
  • Plans, organizes, and assigns the work of the organizational unit and evaluates employee performance and conduct, enabling the effective recommendation of the hiring, firing, promoting, and disciplining of subordinates.  
  • Provides appropriate assignments, instruction, and supervision to plumbing inspectors and clerical employees.  
  • Inspects and evaluates plumbing work in construction projects underway to ensure that all work installed conforms to the requirements of the approved plans and the plumbing and energy subcodes, and the regulations of the State Uniform Construction Code.  
  • Inspects plumbing installations in existing buildings to ensure that installations meet the minimum health and safety standards incorporated in the regulations for the State Uniform Construction Code and relevant sanitary and public health laws.  
  • Responsibility for supervising the code compliance for plumbing and energy subcode of all construction and contractors to ensure that required standards are observed in accord with approved plans and specifications.  
  • Takes the initiative in halting construction work by contractors when and if reasonable standards of workmanship, safety, and plans, specifications, and/or legal requirements are not being observed.  
  • Collects and records permit and other fees, issues permits, and verifies that required prior approvals have been obtained and is responsible for ensuring that these actions are in accord with regulations for the State Uniform Construction Code.  
  • Responsible for establishing and maintaining cooperative working relationships with architects, engineers, and construction supervisors.  
  • Reviews construction to ensure that all materials, methods, and assemblies conform to standards referenced by the code and manufacturers' installation directions as well as other matters not shown in a set of plans but required for conformity with the code.  
  • Issues onsite warning, citations, and stop work orders in cases of serious violations of the plumbing or energy subcode which might endanger the health, safety, and/or welfare of the public or building occupants.  
  • Prepares recommendations regarding both temporary and final certificates of occupancy.  
  • Prepares violations reports.  
  • Testifies in court and in administrative hearings.  
  • Prepares inspection reports showing the progress of work on each project relative to construction code compliance, weather conditions, and the percentage of the project completed.  
  • Prepares correspondence.  
  • Maintains and supervises the maintenance of the records, reports, and files required to show the details of each project inspected.  
  • Establishes inspection schedules for plumbing inspection staff and ensures that all buildings being constructed or renovated are inspected at critical points during the course of construction as provided for in regulations for the State Uniform Construction Code.  
  • Identifies and inspects all materials being incorporated in the plumbing construction and renovation of buildings located within the jurisdiction to ensure that they conform to the approved plans and that they meet the necessary performance standards established in the regulations for the State Uniform Construction Code and the adopted subcode.  
  • Serves subpoenas and other legal process notices including notices of violations.  
  • Will be required to learn to utilize various types of electronic and/or manual recording and computerized information systems used by the agency, office, or related units

Typical Qualifications

ICS License:  
  • Knowledge of problems and procedures involved in plumbing inspection work involved in the enforcement of relevant public health laws and, as far as practical, of the broad field of public health.  
  • Knowledge of design and analysis techniques needed to ensure compliance of inbuilding water drainage systems with requirements of the code.  
  • Knowledge of plumbing installation testing methods required to be employed by the code and proper application.  
  • Knowledge of methods of construction, location, and operation of onsite sewage disposal systems, small sewage disposal plants, and private water supply systems.  
  • Knowledge of organization, content, and regulations of the State Uniform Construction Code.  
  • Knowledge of organization and content of the plumbing subcode.  
  • Knowledge of basic classification of structures into class types.  
  • Knowledge of plumbing subcode' s background, purpose, history, and place in local government, and relation to construction code enforcement programs at other levels of government.  
  • Knowledge of plan reading sufficient to permit an understanding of the process and to perform the duties of the position.  
  • Knowledge of material standards in the code and methods by which  those standards are developed.  
  • Knowledge of installation methods and practices required to ensure that all approved materials including joints, conductors, traps, and cleanouts and structural support requirements are installed properly.  
  • Knowledge of plumbing fitting and fixture requirements.  
  • Knowledge of basic inspection report writing including the preparation of violation notices and required record keeping.  
HHS License:  
  • The knowledge and abilities for an ICS license plus knowledge of plumbing system design component which will ensure the technical competence necessary to check the systems design and installation for the large and complex systems which characterize class I buildings including pumps, pressure tanks, and other such plumbing installation required.  
ICS and HHS License:  
  • Knowledge of office procedures for inspectors including forms and records used and purpose of each.  
  • Knowledge of methods of establishing proper review and approval  of permit applications for compliance with the construction code and applicable laws and regulations including application contents, use  of procedure and information sheets for applicants, use of check lists for compliance with applicable ordinances, and processing of applications.  
  • Knowledge of legal aspects of code enforcement.  
  • Knowledge of purpose and fundamentals of stop orders, notices of penalty, and court action.  
  • Knowledge of powers and procedures available to deal with hazardous conditions and emergency situations including emergency work orders, bids, and quotations process.  
  • Knowledge of procedures for processing cases involving condemnations and other violations of the subcode from initiation through final compliance.  
  • Knowledge of the preparation of case records.  
  • Knowledge of situations requiring a warrant, and of the process of obtaining and issuing the warrant.  
  • Knowledge of the administrative hearing process under the State Uniform Construction Code Act  
  • Knowledge of legal aspects of the operations of enforcing agencies including legal processes and rules of evidence.  
  • Knowledge of legal responsibilities of inspection personnel.  
  • Knowledge of methods of appealing hearing decisions to the court,  and of the legal basis of doing so.  
  • Knowledge of related legislation.  
  • Ability to interpret the State Uniform Construction Code and applicable New Jersey Health Law and Code and apply them  to specific cases.  
  • Ability to ensure that all fittings and fixtures installed conform to the requirement of the State Uniform Construction Code.  
  • Ability to analyze plumbing inspection problems.  
  • Ability to organize assigned supervisory and other work and develop effective work methods.  
  • Ability to develop a suitable work program and working procedures  for a group of plumbing inspectors.  
  • Ability to provide assignments and instruction to assigned employees.  
  • Ability to work harmoniously with concerned persons.  
  • Ability to establish and maintain proper relationships with business proprietors, contractors, housekeepers, and others interested and/or concerned with the maintenance of public health standards.  
  • Ability to take a firm and correct stand when needed.  
  • Ability to prepare reports.  
  • Ability to act as a convincing witness in court and to supervise the establishment and maintenance of essential records and files.  
  • Ability to learn to utilize various types of electronic and/or manual recording and information systems used by the agency, office, or related units.  
  • Ability to read, write, speak, understand, or communicate in English sufficiently to perform the duties of this position. American Sign Language or Braille may also be considered as acceptable forms of communication.  
  • Persons with mental or physical disabilities are eligible as long as they can perform the essential functions of the job after reasonable accommodation is made to their known limitations. If the accommodation cannot be made because it would cause the employer undue hardship, such persons may not be eligible.

title: Trajectcoach maatschappelijke opvang
description:
Wil jij bouwen aan een nieuwe opvangvoorziening in Amersfoort én mensen ondersteunen bij een nieuwe stap richting zelfstandigheid? In deze functie werk je op het snijvlak van opvang en wonen. Je helpt mensen die tijdelijk geen stabiele woonplek hebben en draagt tegelijk bij aan de verdere ontwikkeling van een nieuwe locatie en een groeiend team.

Wat ga je doen

Je begint de week met screenings of triagegesprekken. Je brengt de situatie van cliënten in kaart, kijkt welke ondersteuning nodig is en zet de eerste stappen richting een passend vervolg. Op de opvanglocaties werk je aan een veilige en gastvrije omgeving, terwijl je samen met cliënten werkt aan perspectief en doorstroom naar een volgende woonplek.

  • Begeleiden van cliënten: Je stelt samen met cliënten een plan op, biedt ondersteuning bij financiën, aanvragen en dagelijkse zaken en helpt mensen om weer regie te krijgen op hun leven.
  • Organiseren van doorstroom: Je werkt toe naar passende vervolgstappen, zoals doorstroomwoningen, Housing First of begeleiding via BW/BT, zodat de opvang een tijdelijke tussenstap blijft.
  • Samenwerken met partners: Je stemt af met wijkteams, gemeenten en andere betrokken organisaties om trajecten goed op elkaar aan te laten sluiten.

Je werkt op de locaties Westsingel en Smallepad. Op beide plekken ondersteun je cliënten, betrek je hen bij activiteiten op de locatie en draag je bij aan een omgeving waarin mensen zich welkom en gehoord voelen.

Wat krijg je van ons?

We vinden dat iedereen moet kunnen meedoen. Elk idee, elke wens of behoefte is belangrijk. Daarom staan we open voor jouw ideeën en suggesties. Met een open mind werken we effectief samen. Zo laten we je groeien vanuit je eigen kracht en investeren we in je ontwikkeling en gezondheid op de werkvloer.

Verder krijg je:

  • Een jaarcontract voor 24-36 uur per week. Het brutosalaris ligt tussen € 3.168,- en maximaal € 5.216, afhankelijk van kennis en ervaring bij een fulltime dienstverband (schaal 7/8 cao Sociaal Werk).
  • Een individueel keuzebudget (IKB) van 17% van jouw salaris (IKB is opgebouwd uit o.a. 8% vakantietoeslag en de eindejaarsuitkering) én een individueel loopbaanbudget van 1,5% dat je kunt inzetten voor je loopbaanontwikkeling of vitaliteit. Het is mogelijk het IKB maandelijks uit te laten keren.
  • De kans om je continu te blijven ontwikkelen via onze TV-academie.
  • Reiskostenvergoeding en een pensioenregeling (PFZW-pensioenverzekering) en opleidingsmogelijkheden.

Wat neem je mee?

Je haalt voldoening uit het begeleiden van mensen naar meer stabiliteit en zelfstandigheid. Je ziet kansen, houdt overzicht en weet ondersteuning te bieden die aansluit bij wat iemand op dat moment nodig heeft. Je beweegt gemakkelijk tussen praktische begeleiding, samenwerking met partners en gesprekken over de toekomst.

Heb je zelf ervaring als ervaringsdeskundige? Dan moedigen we je van harte aan om te solliciteren.

Verder heb je:

  • Hbo Social Work of een vergelijkbare opleiding
  • Ervaring binnen de maatschappelijke opvang, het sociaal domein of een vergelijkbare werkomgeving.
  • Kennis van financiën, schulden, toeslagen en gemeentelijke aanvragen.
  • Kennis van methodieken zoals Krachtwerk, Presentie of een vergelijkbare werkwijze.

Over het team

De Tussenvoorziening in Amersfoort bestaat uit team Opvang en team Wonen. Team Opvang bevindt zich in een opbouwfase en groeit de komende periode verder uit met opvangcoaches, trajectcoaches en een manager. Als trajectcoach krijg je de ruimte om mee te denken over werkprocessen, samenwerking en de manier waarop begeleiding wordt vormgegeven.

Je werkt nauw samen met team Wonen, dat al acht jaar actief is in Amersfoort met onder andere AMV 18+ en Housing First. Wat begon als een klein team van pioniers is uitgegroeid tot een ervaren en professioneel team dat ongeveer zestig cliënten begeleidt. Door de samenwerking tussen opvang en wonen zorgen jullie voor een goede doorstroom en ondersteuning die aansluit bij de volgende stap van cliënten.

De maatschappelijke opvang in Amersfoort is nog volop in ontwikkeling. Dat biedt ruimte om samen te bouwen, nieuwe werkwijzen vorm te geven en bij te dragen aan een sterke basis voor cliënten én collega's. Jouw ideeën, ervaring en betrokkenheid maken daarin het verschil.

Samen Sterker verder

Ben jij oprecht, krachtig en verbindend? Solliciteer direct en laat ons weten waarom dit de functie voor jou is. Dan nemen wij zo snel mogelijk contact met je op. Heb je vragen? Bel gerust met: Rina Broekman op +31623757859.

We waarderen het dat headhunters en werving- en selectiebureaus met ons mee willen denken, maar wij kiezen ervoor om ons recruitment zelf te verzorgen.

description:
Oldham County Schools is building a world-class technology support team. We're hiring 6 District Technology Assistants as the foundation of our new three-tier support model, serving 22 buildings, over 12,000 students, and 3,000 staff members.

This isn't just a help desk job, you're enabling learning. You'll solve problems, support people, and see the direct impact of your work every day. If you're ready to launch or grow your career in education technology as part of a professional team, we want to hear from you.

This posting is for vacancies starting July 1st, 2026.

District Technology Assistant

Job Goal: To provide timely and effective technology support services to district staff and school personnel from a centralized district office, ensuring that hardware, software and end-user computing needs are resolved efficiently and with a high standard of customer service.

Job Type: ClassifiedJob Class Code: 7525
Position Type: Hourly Reports to: Director of Technology
Terms of Employment: Compensation will be based on 260 contract days on the board-approved 110 salary schedule. This position requires an 8-hour work day.

Minimum Qualifications:

  1. High School diploma or GED required; Associate's degree or post-secondary coursework in Information Technology, Computer Science or a related field preferred..
  2. CompTIA A+ certification required or demonstrated ability to perform equivalent technical support competencies.
  3. Working knowledge of current Windows and Mac operating systems, Microsoft 365 applications, Google Workspace applications and common end-user hardware including computers, printers and peripherals.Familiarity with basic network concepts including wired and wireless connectivity, IP addressing and network printing.
  4. Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot hardware and software issues effectively and communicate technical information clearly to non-technical users.
  5. Strong customer service orientation; ability to work professionally and patiently with students, staff and administrators across a variety of school and district settings.
  6. Organized and detail-oriented; ability to maintain accurate records in a ticketing or asset management system.
  7. Such additional qualifications as the Superintendent or Chief Information Officer may find appropriate and acceptable.

Performance Responsibilities:

  1. Serves as a centralized point of support for district and school technology needs; responds to help desk requests, diagnoses issues and resolves hardware, software and peripheral problems in a timely manner; travels to district and school buildings as needed to resolve issues that cannot be addressed remotely.
  2. Performs setup, imaging, configuration and deployment of computers, tablets, printers and other end-user devices in accordance with district standards and procedures.
  3. Maintains accurate records of support activity, hardware inventory and device status within the district's ticketing and asset management systems.
  4. Assists in the installation, updating and basic troubleshooting of district-approved software applications and operating system updates across managed endpoints.
  5. Supports the setup and breakdown of technology equipment for district events, assessments and special projects as directed.
  6. Communicates clearly and professionally with end users regarding the status of support requests, expected resolution timelines and recommended practices.
  7. Assists with technology-related moves, additions and changes during the school year and summer refresh period.
  8. Performs other duties as assigned by the Chief Information Officer or Superintendent.

Adopted: June 19, 2000

Revised: March 5, 2004, November 10, 2011, October 30, 2014, February 1, 2021, July 1, 2021, April 2026

description:

What You'll Get From Us:

Description of Job

Integrated Document Solutions (IDS) is a full-service, end-to-end document management operation. IDS advises, assists, and supports each agency’s needs, providing a wide variety of cost-efficient document solutions at a professional level.

This position will drive deliveries, provide support for mail operations, as well as security of the North Campus for DPA. It provides support for critical infrastructure jobs and performs duties of a sensitive and vital nature for mail services, facility security and secure storage.

A summary of the duties and responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Delivery driver – drives for the delivery unit to other State agency buildings
  • Mail security – screen and process mail, detecting any harmful items before sending out to state
  • Security desk – manage access to facility, including main entrance and gated parking lot and delivery
  • Campus security – coordinator and administrative support for facility safety and various safety programs


Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights

*A Human Resources Analyst will only review the work experience/job duties sections of the online job application to determine whether you meet the minimum qualifications for the position for which you are applying. Cover letters and resumes WILL NOT be accepted in lieu of the official State of Colorado online application, but may be attached. Applicants must meet the minimum qualifications to continue in the selection process for this position. Work experience and qualifications must be specifically documented on your online application. Do not use "see resume" or "see attached" statements on your application. Resumes WILL NOT be reviewed for minimum qualification screening. If it is determined that you meet the minimum qualifications, your application will also be used as part of the comparative analysis process to identify a top group for further consideration.

This position is advertised in line with the Governor’s executive order (Executive Order 2022 015) focused on skills-based hiring practices that focuses on the knowledge, skills, and abilities specific to the job and aligns the hiring process accordingly. Skills-based hiring reduces potential barriers for applicants and allows for reduced bias in the hiring process by providing a direct description of skills that are unique to the duties assigned to the position with a recognition that the applicant may have developed these skills through education, training or past experiences.

Residency Requirement:

This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application.

Class Code & Classification Description:

G3A3XXADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT II

Experience Only: At least two (2) years of combined experience in delivery, mail sorting, and security.

OR

Education and Experience: A combination of related education and/or combined experience in delivery, mail sorting, and security equal to at least two (2) years.


The exceptional candidate will possess the proven ability or accomplishment in the following preferred qualifications:

  • Previous State service related to the work assigned to the position

  • Previous delivery driver experience


Conditions of Employment:

  • A pre-employment criminal background check will be conducted as part of the selection process.

  • Department of Revenue Tax Check

  • Must have and maintain a valid, unrestricted Colorado Driver's License

  • Shift Work: Position must be available to work any shift including holidays and overtime.

  • Travel - This is a delivery driver position


Comparative Analysis Process The comparative analysis process for this position may consist of a structured application review, an online assessment and a structured interview.

Appeal Rights:

An applicant who has been removed from consideration during the selection or comparative analysis process, you may file an appeal with the State Personnel Board and/or request a review by the State Personnel Director. A standard appeal form is available on the State Personnel Board website,https://spb.colorado.gov/forms-and-filing. If you appeal, your appeal must be submitted in writing on the official appeal form, signed by you or your representative, and received at the following address within ten (10) days of your receipt of this notice: Colorado State Personnel Board/State Personnel Director, Attn: Appeals Processing, 1525 Sherman Street, 4th Floor, Denver, CO 80203. Fax: 303-866-5038. Phone: 303-866-3300. Email address: dpa_state.personnelboard@state.co.us. The ten-day deadline and these appeal procedures also apply to all charges of discrimination. Refer to Chapters 4 and 8 of the State Personnel Board Rules and Personnel Director's Administrative Procedures, 4 CCR 801, for information about the appeals process. The State Personnel Board Rules and Personnel Director's Administrative Procedures are available at spb.colorado.gov.



Supplemental Information

Employment Philosophy: The State of Colorado strives to build and maintain workplaces that value and respect all Coloradans. We are building a Colorado for All through a commitment to equal opportunity and hiring based on merit and fitness. The State is committed to non-discriminatory practices in hiring, employment, and advancement opportunities.

Accommodations: The Department of Personnel & Administration is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, our agency will assist individuals who have a disability with any reasonable accommodation requests related to employment, including completing the application process, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, participating in the employee selection process, and/or to perform essential job functions where the requested accommodation does not impose an undue hardship. If you have a disability and require reasonable accommodation to ensure you have a positive experience applying or interviewing for this position, please direct your inquiries to our ADAAA Coordinator, Heather Siegal heather.siegal@state.co.us

title: DevOps Engineer - AWS Connect
description:
About the job DevOps Engineer - AWS Connect

Software International (SI) supplies technical talent to a variety of clients ranging from Fortune 100/500/1000 companies to small and mid-sized organizations in Canada/US. We are currently searching for aDevOps Engineer - AWS Connect for our IT Consulting client to work on a long term project with a major transportation company.

Type: 6 month contract to start but this will be a long term project with projected extensions

Rate Range: $70 - $90/hr C2C

Location: onsite - client is based in Etobicoke, ON

Number of Roles: 6

Our client's prrojectteam is growing and we are looking for a talented DevOps Engineer with a background in AWS Connectto join theirteam in Etbicoke, ON.

Job Summary:

As a DevOps Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining the infrastructure and tools necessary for our software development and deployment processes. You will work closely with our development team to ensure a seamless and efficient software delivery pipeline.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design and implement automated deployment processes using AWS Connect
  • Monitor and maintain the infrastructure and tools used for software development and deployment
  • Troubleshoot and resolve any issues related to the deployment process
  • Collaborate with the development team to ensure smooth integration of new features and updates
  • Implement and maintain security protocols and best practices for our infrastructure
  • Continuously improve and optimize the software delivery pipeline
  • Stay up-to-date with the latest DevOps tools and technologies and make recommendations for implementation
  • Create and maintain technical documentation for the deployment process and infrastructure
  • Participate in on-call rotation for after-hours support and issue resolution

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience as a DevOps Engineer
  • Strong understanding of AWS Connect and other AWS services
  • Experience with automation and configuration management tools such as Ansible, Chef, or Puppet
  • Proficient in scripting languages such as Bash, Python, or Ruby
  • Experience with containerization and orchestration tools such as Docker and Kubernetes
  • Knowledge of networking and security protocols
  • Experience with monitoring and logging tools such as Prometheus, ELK stack, or Splunk
  • Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills
  • Ability to work independently and in a team environment
  • AWS certifications are a plus

This is a contractor position based in Etobicoke, ON. The contract duration is for 6 months with the possibility of extension. The candidate will be required to work 40 hours per week with a competitive hourly rate. The candidate must have a valid work permit for Canada.

If you are a self-motivated individual with a passion for DevOps and AWS, we want to hear from you! Join our dynamic team at Software International and be a part of our exciting projects.

title: Data Analyst, Probationary
description:
DATA ANALYST

*This position is classified with the Westchester County Civil Service system.

Job Summary:

Under the supervision of the Director of Technology , the analyst enters data into and extracts data from system-wide databases preparing reports for use by teachers and administrators.This position analyzes data to develop spreadsheets, reports and presentations that provide formative and summative data useful in evaluating and improving instruction.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated techniques for analyzing NYS State Assessment Data and other third party and locally developed student assessment data.
  • Experience organizing, disaggregating and generating reports on student assessment data.
  • Experience working in a school setting is preferred.
  • Ability to communicate and present data to administration and teaching staff.
  • Knowledge of student information systems (eSchoolData preferred).
  • Knowledge of SIRS requirements.
  • Understanding of NYSTP requirements.
  • Experience providing training to staff.
    • Experience with the following:Office Suite, MS Access, GSuite for Education
    • Analytics Tools
    • Custom Report Writing

Duties:

  • Prepares and organizes student assessment data and generates custom reports for administrators and building data teams.
  • Monitor and respond to the support help desk for staff and families with regards to data and portal questions.
  • Answers questions related to the district's student management systems, by phone, email and in person.
  • Collects and maintains emergency contact information for students/guardians.
  • Collects data from various school and community sources and enters it into the school district student databases including but not limited to the student information system and data dashboard.
  • Collects and maintains data based on student census, enrollment, and attendance to produce statistical reports.
  • Prepares and organizes data on student test results for analysis, district studies and/or state reports.
  • Prepares correspondence and reports in response to requests for statistical information.
  • Inputs, downloads, organizes, and analyzes student data used for instructional purposes using shared accountability and local school databases.
  • Develops and shares reports on student data.
  • Suggests relationships between data trends, curriculum, instruction, and assessment.
  • Responds to data requests from administrators and teachers.
  • Designs and conducts presentations of data and associated data analysis to school, school system and community groups.
  • Maintains and updates class lists and rosters and assists with sectioning of students.
  • Participates in training to remain current on data sources, data analysis techniques and strategies for developing and conducting presentations.
  • Serves on/interacts with school leadership teams to promote the continuous improvement of instruction.
  • Collaboratively works to manage all aspects of implementation, utilization, and support of school/student information data systems.
  • As needed, monitors the administration of tests and investigates discrepancies in test administration.
  • Provides technical assistance and consultation on considerations in testing set up to the district.
  • Manages data collection from various school and community sources.
  • Systematizes, organizes and integrates data, including necessary data preparation for analysis, district studies, state reports, etc.
  • Manages, troubleshoots, and ensures accurate production processes for report cards, progress reports and other system-generated communications to parents and community.
  • Monitors and ensures accuracy of data, statistics and reports, in compliance with all applicable data and records maintenance standards and requirements.
  • Performs a variety of related requests as assigned by the Director of Technology, Assistant Superintendent of Curriculum & Instruction and Superintendent..

Minimum Acceptable Training and Experience:

Either: a) Graduation from high school or possession of a high school equivalency diploma and five (5) years of work experience in which the primary function of the position was using automated spreadsheet and database programs; or (b) a Bachelor's Degree* and one (1) year of work experience as described in (a); or (c) a Bachelor's Degree* or Master's Degree* in Computer Science, Information Technology, Analytics, Data Science or a closely related field.

*To be considered for the position, a candidate must either:

  • hold the permanent title of Data Analyst in Westchester County OR
  • be reachable on the corresponding Westchester Civil Service list

Salary Range
$68,000-80,000 (2025/2026)

REVISED: 5/12/2026 (HR Department)

The Yorktown Central School District is an equal opportunity employer.

Position Title:

Financial Operations Recovery Specialist III

Job Description:

Virtual: This role enables associates to work virtually full-time, except for required in-person training sessions, providing maximum flexibility and autonomy. This approach promotes productivity, supports work-life integration, and ensures essential face-to-face onboarding and skill development. Alternate locations may be considered if candidates reside within a commuting distance from an office.

  • May review and monitor associates work for quality standards.
  • May review department policy and procedure manuals for accuracy and works to ensure procedures and polices are accurate and complete.
  • Assists in special projects to find and prevent overpayments and to identify process improvements.

  • Researches voluntary refunds for accuracy.

title: Computer Technician I-IV (DOE) (8hrs)
description:
JOB VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT
COMPUTER TECHNICIAN I-IV
CLASSIFIED VACANCIES
Internal/External Applicants

Date Issued: July 22, 2026 Closes: Open until filled

The Kodiak Island Borough School District is accepting applications for a Computer Technician for the 2026-2027 school year:

COMPUTER TECHNICIAN I-IV
Location: District Wide Services, Kodiak, AK
Hours: 8 hrs/day, 5 days/week, 11 months
Salary: Computer Technician I: Entry Range 16.5, Step 1: $23.91 per/hr
Computer Technician II: Entry Range 18, Step 1: $25.24 per/hr
Computer Technician III: Entry Range 20, Step 1: $26.97 per/hr
Computer Technician IV: Entry Range 22, Step 1: $28.81 per/hr



COMPUTER TECHNICIAN I
Position Summary:
The Computer Technician I, under direction of the Technology Supervisor or designee, is involved in computer maintenance and associated limited area network activities. Work is usually performed under immediate supervision although work assignments that are repetitive in nature, once learned, can be carried out without difficulty under only general supervision. Assignments include software installation or parts replacement and occasional operating system troubleshooting.

Qualifications:

  1. Must possess a general computer and networking background.
  2. Must be able to assist in the maintenance and repair of computers and related equipment and able to perform tasks independently, follow oral and written direction, learn operating policies and procedures, comprehend written material and interpret and apply rules and instructions.
  3. Must be able to establish and maintain cooperative relations with those contacted in the course of work.
  4. Must possess the potential and initiative to upgrade computer maintenance skills through on-the-job training or by other means.
  5. Capable of performing all work in a neat and professional manner.
  6. Must possess a valid State of Alaska motor vehicle operator's license with no insurance restrictions.
  7. Ability to maintain confidentiality of students, staff, school business, materials, and information.
  8. High school graduate or equivalent.
  9. Ability to work well with public, students, staff and parents.
  10. Ability to safely, regularly lift and/or move up to 20 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 70 pounds.


Responsibilities:

  1. Perform tasks requiring general or specialized computer skills or techniques requiring some decision making, and the ability to work independently as required.
  2. Able to install operating system software specifically modified to the location and use of the system.
  3. Safely load and unload heavy materials and equipment; move or aid in moving heavy boxes or equipment.
  4. Assist in wire installation and termination in local and remote sites.
  5. Perform maintenance tasks within own specialty area, or as assigned.
  6. Perform hard drive formats and reinstallation of operating system software.
  7. Assist and perform computer maintenance tasks as directed under general supervision.
  8. Perform maintenance duties within scope of position at village school locations as assigned.
  9. Maintain confidentiality of students, staff, school business materials and information.
  10. Other duties as assigned from time to time.




COMPUTER TECHNICIAN II
Position Summary:
The Computer Technician II, under direction of the Director of Information Technology or designee, is a position of skilled computer work experience and some technical ability involved in Local Area Networks, Wide Area Networks and associated service activities. These are performed in a wide variety of computer maintenance and enhancement duties combining several skills and knowledge areas. Work is usually performed with minimal supervision. Assignments frequently involve the use of specialized software and equipment. Work of this class requires previous computer experience plus initiative and judgment to work without close supervision as necessary.

Qualifications:

  1. Must possess a general computer or networking background with a high skill level in a troubleshooting software and hardware issues.
  2. Must be able to follow oral and written directions, learn operating procedures and policies, comprehend written material and interpret and apply rules and instructions, establish and maintain cooperative relations with those contacted in the course of work, function independently when required, convey information orally or in writing.
  3. Have a working knowledge of all software utilized by the district.
  4. Capable of performing all work in a neat and professional manner.
  5. Must possess the potential and initiative to upgrade personal computer skills.
  6. Must possess a valid State of Alaska motor vehicle operator's license with no insurance restrictions.
  7. Must possess an A+ certificate or equivalent.
  8. Ability to maintain confidentiality of students, staff, school business, materials, and information.
  9. High school graduate or equivalent.
  10. Ability to work well with public, students, staff and parents.
  11. Ability to safely, regularly lift and/or move up to 20 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 70 pounds.


Responsibilities:

  1. Perform jobs requiring general plus specialized skills and experience in several information technology areas.
  2. Perform installation of operating system software in specialized configurations and custom installations of all district-use specialized software.
  3. Assist in or perform computer maintenance including servers and special use systems.
  4. Perform Local Area Network troubleshooting and repair as directed.
  5. Configure laboratory environments for optimal performance with specialized software packages.
  6. Assist in equipment and software research and selection for district needs.
  7. Assist or perform specialized equipment configuration and maintenance.
  8. Ability to make general estimates of material needs.
  9. Perform maintenance duties within scope of position at village school locations as assigned with little supervision.
  10. Maintain confidentiality of students, staff, school business materials and information.
  11. Other duties as assigned from time to time.




COMPUTER TECHNICIAN III
Position Summary:
The Computer Technician III, under the direction of the Director of Information Technology or designee, is an experienced position of skilled technical ability and supervisory work. Work performance covers a variety of skilled repair and network related tasks. Assignments frequently involve the use of standard and specialized software and tools as well as sophisticated testing equipment. Responsibilities extend to supervision and training of lower level maintenance personnel in the execution of assigned duties.

Qualifications:

  1. Must possess an advanced computer and LAN technology knowledge.
  2. Must have the ability to competently and professionally construct, maintain, repair and improve computers, networks or related systems and equipment.
  3. Must have a working knowledge of the all software and hardware utilized by the school district with special emphasis on common applications and system architectures.
  4. Must have ability to interpret and follow troubleshooting documentation from all vendors and equipment manufactures.
  5. Must be able to follow oral and written directions, learn operating policies and procedures, comprehend written material and interpret and apply rules and instructions, establish and maintain cooperative relations with those contacted in the course of work, function with a moderate level of independence, convey information orally or in writing, and instruct and supervise subordinates as directed.
  6. Must be capable of performing all work in a neat and professional manner with the initiative and potential to continue to upgrade personal information technology skills.
  7. Must possess a valid State of Alaska motor vehicle operator's license with no insurance restrictions.
  8. Must possess an A+ and a MCSE certificate or equivalent.
  9. Ability to maintain confidentiality of students, staff, school business, materials, and information.
  10. High school graduate or equivalent.

title: Senior Network & Systems Engineer
description:
JOB TITLE: Senior Network & Systems Engineer

DEPARTMENT: Technology

REPORTS TO: Technology Coordinator

APPROVED BY: BCBOE

DATE: 6/12/26

SUMMARY OF DUTIES

The Senior Network & Systems Administrator serves as a primary technical authority for the District’s technology infrastructure. This role is responsible for the architecting, implementation, security, and high-level tier-3 maintenance of Local Area Networks (LANs), Wide Area Networks (WANs), wireless networks, virtualized servers, cloud environments, and endpoint systems. The ideal candidate brings extensive technical experience to ensure system reliability, enterprise-grade security, and seamless support for instructional and administrative operations across all District sites.

QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS

  • Education & Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a closely related field, paired with a minimum of 5 to 7+ years of progressive hands-on experience in network engineering and systems administration. Equivalent combinations of advanced certifications and extensive field experience will be considered.
  • Certifications (Preferred/Recommended): Industry-recognized credentials such as Ci CompTIA Network+/Security+, Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator, or VMware VCP.
  • Background Check: Clear criminal background check free of felony convictions and capable of passing a physical examination as prescribed by the Board.
  • Character: Strong ethical standard, high integrity, and proven dependability in a public education environment.

CRITICAL SKILLS & EXPERTISE

Network & Infrastructure Engineering

  • Advanced administration of enterprise LAN/WAN/WLAN architectures, subnets, VLANs, VPNs, routing protocols, and firewalls.
  • Expertise with managed switches, routers, access points, and network security appliances.
  • In-depth knowledge of DNS, DHCP, IPAM, Active Directory, and Group Policy Management.

Systems & Cloud Administration

  • Enterprise administration of Windows Server OS, Linux environments, virtualization platforms (Hyper-V/VMware), and cloud ecosystems (Microsoft 365, Azure, or Google Workspace).
  • Experience managing centralized endpoint management systems (MDM), automated software deployment, and patch management.
  • Solid background in network backup routines, disaster recovery planning, and system redundancy.

Security, Compliance & Automation

  • Implementation of cybersecurity best practices, network access control (NAC), content filtering, and threat detection.
  • Proficiency in scripting and automation tools (e.g., PowerShell, Bash) to streamline administrative workflows.
  • Familiarity with data privacy, backup verification, and emergency recovery operations.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS & SKILLS

  • System Architecture: Design, configure, and optimize local and wide-area infrastructure to support high-density user environments.
  • Tier-3 Technical Escalation: Diagnose and resolve complex network outages, hardware failures, and systemic software issues that exceed lower-tier support capacity.
  • Strategic Planning: Plan and organize large-scale infrastructure projects, technology rollouts, and hardware refresh cycles while adhering to established timelines.
  • Communication & Collaboration: Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical staff and non-technical district stakeholders.
  • Physical Capability: Ability to lift and move heavy rack-mounted equipment (up to 50 lbs), navigate wiring closets, and perform installations safely.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Network & Systems Management

  1. Architect, configure, monitor, and maintain the District’s core network infrastructure, servers, storage systems, and internet connectivity to ensure high availability.
  2. Manage and optimize Active Directory, domain controllers, cloud tenant services, email environments, and identity/access management systems.
  3. Conduct proactive monitoring of network bandwidth, server loads, and hardware health to preemptively identify and resolve performance bottlenecks.

Security, Backup & Disaster Recovery

  1. Manage District firewalls, intrusion prevention systems, content filters, and endpoint protection solutions to secure administrative and student data.
  2. Establish, test, and execute robust backup, restoration, and disaster recovery plans to maintain business and instructional continuity.

Project Management & Support

  1. Research, evaluate, and recommend new hardware/software solutions to align technology infrastructure with educational and administrative goals.
  2. Serve as the technical escalation point for complex support tickets; collaborate with external vendors and software providers to resolve high-level infrastructure issues.
  3. Maintain accurate, up-to-date documentation regarding network topologies, system configurations, IP schemes, software licensing, and hardware inventory.

Mentorship & Operations

  1. Provide technical guidance, operational insights, and informal mentorship to junior technology support staff and field technicians.
  2. Perform other infrastructure-related duties as assigned by the Technology Coordinator.

PROFESSIONAL EXPECTATIONS

  • Complete required professional development, safety training, and in-service sessions.
  • Display consistent self-control, professionalism, and tact when interacting with staff, students, parents, and community members.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and secure workstation/server room environment.
  • Adhere to District policies regarding attendance, punctuality, ethical conduct, and safety standards.

TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT

  • Work Year: Designated by the current school calendar and board policy, including paid holidays as applicable.
  • Salary: Commensurate with the adopted classified personnel salary schedule based on experience and certifications.
  • Benefits: Sick leave and personal leave provided as outlined in Board policy.
  • Status: At-Will Employee under the direction of the Superintendent.

EVALUATION

Performance of this job will be evaluated in accordance with provisions of the Board’s policy on Evaluation of Classified Personnel.

The information contained in this job description is for compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (A.D.A.) and is not an exhaustive list of the duties performed for this position.

title: Academic Pharmacy Fellow
description:
Position Summary:

MCW School of Pharmacy is seeking applications for an Academic Fellow. This individual will be appointed as a full-time, year-round non-tenure track Clinical Instructor. This position is a 2-year post-graduate opportunity, designed to prepare pharmacists for a career in pharmacy education through training in teaching, curriculum development, college service, mentoring, scholarship and clinical practice with an anticipated start date of 7/1/2027. Individuals that have completed PGY1 or PGY2 training program can apply for a one-year fellowship.

The clinical responsibilities of the fellow will be consistent with experiences provided in a PGY1 residency. The fellows will be exposed to a variety of teaching responsibilities, including lecturing, facilitating small group-based learning, course coordination and student assessment. In addition to extensive academic experience, the fellows will also participate in direct patient-care rotations in primary care. This position reports to the Academic Fellowship Director in the School of Pharmacy.

The training year will consist of approximately 60% teaching- and academic-related duties and 40% clinical practice. Highlights of the training program include participating for the entire year on a college committee, extensive teaching experience and flexible clinical practice opportunities. At the end of the training program, academic fellows will be well prepared for a career in academia.

Position Highlights:

Teaching and College Service

  • Design, implement, facilitate, and deliver innovative educational content within the Doctor of Pharmacy program

  • Develop skills in educational training through a variety of classroom experiences (i.e. didactic lecturing, facilitating skills labs, and small group active-learning environments)

  • Participate in a longitudinal specialty area of academia (i.e. Assessment, Curriculum, Admissions, Faculty Affairs, etc.)

  • Develop skills necessary for successful course coordination, precept Introductory and/or Advanced Pharmacy Practice students on clinical rotations

  • Engage in mentorship activities through student organizations and community service

  • Exhibit professionalism through participation in pharmacy and interprofessional organizations and serving as student organization mentor

  • Complete the MCW School of Pharmacy Teaching Certificate Program

  • Complete the MCW Kinetic 3 Teaching Academy

  • Precept students in a clinical telehealth program

Scholarship

  • Complete the MCW School of Pharmacy Research Certificate Program

  • Complete a research project related to the scholarship of teaching, learning and/or education

  • Present research data at a professional meeting and the Annual MCW School of Pharmacy Research Symposium annually

  • Submit paper for publication (systemic review, educational innovation, etc.)

  • Represent the college at selected professional meetings (regional and national presence)

  • Submission of a grant proposal will be taught and is highly encouraged

Clinical Practice

  • Refine clinical practice skills by maintaining clinical practice skills and providing patient-centered care in a specialty of fellow’s choice (ambulatory care, internal medicine, cardiology, etc.)

  • Develop pharmacy practice experience and expertise in support of the clinical knowledge expected of a faculty member

  • Coordinate and participate in health fairs and population health initiatives

Qualifications

  • Applicants must hold a PharmD degree from an accredited U.S. program (or equivalent)

  • Individuals who have completed a PGY1 pharmacy residency or a PGY-2 specialty residency or a fellowship and are interested in pursuing a career in academia are highly encouraged to apply. Applicants without a PGY-1 residency will be interviewed based on their academic performance/experience.

  • All applicants must be eligible for Wisconsin licensure and obtain Wisconsin licensure within 120 days of employment.

Screening will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled, though applications received by December 31. 2026, will be given first consideration. Applicants should submit a letter of application describing their qualifications, curriculum vitae, and contact information for four references via the MCW Careers Site. Please contact Sarah Paul, School Administrator sapaul@mcw.edu for additional information or questions.

Medical College of Wisconsin

The Medical College of Wisconsin (MCW) is the state’s only private medical school and health sciences graduate school. MCW consists of a School of Medicine with campuses in Milwaukee, Green Bay and Central Wisconsin, a School of Graduate Studies, and a School of Pharmacy. MCW is a major national research center ranking in the top third of U.S. medical schools in NIH funding and is the second largest research institution in Wisconsin. Academic medicine is at the core of everything we do at MCW, bringing together scientists, clinicians, students and community members to solve the most complex challenges in health and society. MCW is a diverse group of thought leaders collaborating to pioneer pathways to a healthier world. Every study we conduct and every patient we see leads to new learning and a continuous cycle of life-changing knowledge and innovation.

Approximately 1,780 MCW physicians and approximately 905 advanced practice providers care for more than 484,000 patients of all ages annually at Froedtert Hospital, Zablocki VA Medical Center, Children’s Wisconsin, and many other hospitals and clinics throughout eastern Wisconsin, representing more than 5.1 million patient visits annually.

The beautiful, safe and modern campus of the Milwaukee Regional Medical Center (MRMC) houses Froedtert Hospital, Children’s Wisconsin, Curative Care Network, Versiti Blood Research Institute and the Milwaukee County Behavioral Health Division. These member entities share a common mission of excellence in patient care, medical education, biomedical research and community service.

Commitment to MCW Values

All of our endeavors at MCW, from our internal operations to our interactions with our partners, are driven by our shared organizational values: acting in Caring ways – engaging in Collaborative efforts – approaching our world with Curiosity – advancing Inclusive practices – demonstrating Integrity in all we do – treating everyone with Respect. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment that values diversity in backgrounds, experiences and perspectives through merit-based processes, and in alignment with all applicable laws. We believe that embracing human differences is critical to realize our vision of a healthier world, and we recognize that a healthy and thriving community starts from within. Our values define who we are, what we stand for and how we conduct ourselves at MCW. If you believe in embracing individuality and working together according to these principles to improve health for all, then MCW is the place for you.

Milwaukee, the largest city in Wisconsin, is located on Lake Michigan’s western shore. A metropolitan area with more than 1.6 million people, Milwaukee is an affordable, comfortable place to live, work, and play, big enough to be exciting and uncongested enough to get around easily. Milwaukee’s many neighborhoods have incredible charm, accommodating a variety of lifestyles, from high-rise apartments to small farms. Nestled along a magnificent bluff overlooking Lake Michigan, Milwaukee’s downtown is home to botanical gardens, lakefront museums, a theater district, the world champion Milwaukee Bucks, the Milwaukee Brewers, bustling nightlife, and award-winning restaurants. The lake and its harbors are skirted by scenic parklands and provide first-class opportunities for recreation, including hiking, cycling, boating, and more. A recent study ranked Milwaukee as the 15th most walkable of the 50 largest US cities. Milwaukee has all the advantages of a large, vibrant city but without the stress or cost.

Employees, students, applicants or other members of the MCW community (including but not limited to vendors, visitors, and guests) may not be subjected to harassment that is prohibited by law or treated adversely or retaliated against based upon a protected characteristic.

title: Associate Director of Information Technology, Infrastructure
description:
General Responsibilities Under the general direction of the Director of Information Technology, the Associate Director will be responsible for the daily operations of the ESD and contracted districts' external wide area networks, internal local area networks, K-20, data center and private cloud operations, and the hardware to support those networks. Those operations are delivered with excellent customer service. This is a working manager position that requires deep understanding of network and server technologies to create innovative services to support districts and the greater ESD mission. Salary: The full salary range for this position is $114,732.80-$139,588.80. Offers are made at the beginning of the range. Effective 09/01/2026, the salary range will be $117,707.20-$143,208.00. Offers are made at the beginning of the range. Assignment: The position is full time, year round. Employees are required to maintain regular attendance to carry out the duties and responsibilities of the position Essential Functions/Other Functions Essential Functions:
  1. Assist the Director of Information Technology in the management, service delivery, innovation, and business development of the Information Technology (IT) department
  2. Maintain responsive and accountable services, with rapid response to internal and external clients and appropriate follow-through.
  3. Manage internal and external client expectations and anticipate client needs; continually reviewing existing services in light of changing technology and designing appropriate new services in response to rapid changes in information.
  4. Manage internal and external technology infrastructure design and support implementation of emerging technology, hardware and software acquisition and implementation that supports internal and external programs.
  5. Ensure routine maintenance, updates, and monitoring of internal networks for agency and district clients.
  6. Hire, supervise and evaluate program staff.
  7. Maintain secure infrastructure for the agency and district clients across all areas of cybersecurity.
  8. Maintain regular attendance to carry out the duties and responsibilities of the position
Other Functions:
  1. Participate in technology related activities to keep abreast of current trends.
  2. Participate as an active member of the business services leadership team.
  3. Other duties as assigned to support the success of the agency.
Minimum/Preferred Qualifications & Skills Minimum Qualifications:
  1. Bachelor's Degree in Information Systems, Computer Science or similar field of study plus four years of related work experience. Equivalent combinations of related education, experience, certification, and training may also be considered.
  2. Experience building and fostering partnerships including participation, facilitation, and negotiation of programs and services for technology users.
  3. Experience in technology planning, deployment, and support.
  4. Experience with TCP/IP, NAT, SIP, DNS, DHCP, Ping, Telnet, Trace Route, SSH, NFS, TFTP and protocol analyzers such as WireShark
  5. Experience with complex network protocols such as VLANs and Q-in-Q (IEEE802.1ad).
  6. Experience with network security protocols and hardening network devices.
  7. Experience with current copper and fiber cabling and testing standards.
  8. Experience with BGP and OSPF routing protocols, switches, and firewalls configuration and management.
  9. Recent successful experience in the management of highly complex TCP/IP networks (networks that contain multiple routers, multiple routing protocols, and multiple media, including wireless).
Preferred Qualifications:
  1. Master's Degree in Information Technology, Business Administration or a related field.
  2. Experience installing, configuring, and maintaining all manner of server hardware and associate network equipment, including local and network-based storage technologies.
  3. Recent successful experience in the use, deployment, and maintenance of modern enterprise system software, such as VMWare, Linux, and Microsoft Windows.
  4. Working technical knowledge of scripting code using PHP, shell, and other Linux and Windows server scripting languages and tools.
  5. Working knowledge of load balancing, clustering, and web application security..
  6. Experience in technology planning, deployment, and support in a public sector or non-profit environment, utilizing grant programs such as E-Rate.
  7. Recent working knowledge of data center facilities including HVAC, power, security, and fire suppression systems and energy efficient practices.
  8. Successful experience in a regional educational service agency or K-12 education environment.
  9. A broad knowledge of existing and emerging technologies.
  10. Ability to apply thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills, collaboration and persuasion, creative solutions, as well as an orientation towards clients and achieving results.
  11. Ability to communicate openly and effectively at all levels within the organization and with various audiences.
Working Conditions/Employment Requirements Working Conditions
  1. Requires frequent travel.
  2. May be required to work flexible hours to meet deadlines.
  3. Office environment.
  4. Able to operate keyboard to accomplish required tasks.
  5. Frequent sitting, stooping/bending, lifting/carrying up to 30 lbs.
Employment Requirements - ESD job offer is contingent upon satisfying the following:
  1. Successful completion of a criminal history check through the Washington State Patrol.

title: Strategic Technology Services Specialist
description:
A vacancy exists for a Strategic Technology Services Specialist at the Montgomery County Intermediate Unit. The Strategic Technology Services Specialist serves as a key operational resource within the Office of Technology Services' Strategic Technology Services team, supporting the effective delivery of internal operations and external technology services. This position manages and supports conference center operations, procurement activities, contract administration, Board approval processes, E-rate documentation and tracking, financial workflows, and billing functions. Acting as a liaison among MCIU offices, school districts, vendors, and community partners, the Strategic Technology Services Specialist ensures operational efficiency, financial accountability, regulatory compliance, and exceptional customer service. Through strong organizational, analytical, technical, and project support skills, this position contributes to revenue-generating services, process improvement initiatives, and the successful execution of OTS programs, projects, and strategic priorities.

Qualifications:

  • Associate's degree or equivalent work experience required. Bachelor's degree preferred.
  • Certificate(s) in Computer Science, Information Technology, Project Management, and/or industry-recognized related areas preferred.
  • 1-3 years of progressive experience in project coordination, procurement, A/V management, or a related field required.
  • Expertise (includes one or more of the following):

    • Professional approach to their work that includes very strong customer service skills.

    • Interfacing frequently with customers and stakeholders.

    • Strong technology skills, including extensive use of Microsoft applications as well as MCIU software.

    • Specialized skills in area to be able to work autonomously as proven through work experience.

  • Technical proficiency in AV systems, event scheduling software, and basic troubleshooting, required.
    • Experience with client relations, scheduling, and problem-solving.
    • Excellent customer service and communication skills.
    • Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and make decisions.
  • Experience coordinating purchasing, financial reconciliation, billing, budgeting, or related functions preferred.

  • Ability to work as a member of a team, follow directions, and follow through with completed assigned tasks with minimal supervision.

  • Ability to work in an environment with frequent interruptions.

  • Ability to manage time, meet deadlines, and read and understand highly technical documents.

  • Excellent communication skills, organizational skills, and problem-solving skills; ability to use technology to work effectively.

  • Valid driver's license and safe driving record without major traffic violations; travel to school buildings as required.

  • Original certificates of clearance from the State Police, Child Abuse Registry, and PDE FBI.

Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Manage all aspects of conference center operations, including reservations, scheduling, event logistics, facility readiness, customer service, operational procedures, utilization analysis, performance reporting, and continuous improvement initiatives designed to maximize customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, and revenue generation.
  • Work directly with the Marketing and Communications team to develop and implement outreach strategies that increase awareness of conference center services, expand external partnerships, and support revenue-generating opportunities.
  • Develop, maintain, and analyze operational reports and performance metrics related to conference center utilization, purchasing activities, revenue generation, and other assigned functions to support organizational planning and decision-making.

  • Manage OTS contract administration and Board approval processes, including maintaining contract documentation, preparing Board agenda items and supporting materials, monitoring approval timelines, and ensuring the completeness, accuracy, and compliance of submitted documentation.
  • Monitor procurement timelines to ensure compliance with organizational purchasing procedures.
  • Serve as an operational liaison among OTS staff, MCIU offices, school districts, vendors, and external partners to support technology services, organizational initiatives, and strategic projects.
  • Support and maintain E-rate documentation, application tracking, invoicing support, compliance records, and related technology billing activities for participating Local Education Agencies, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and adherence to program requirements.
  • Support and maintain OTS monthly billing processes, documentation, tracking activities, and related financial procedures to ensure accurate and timely invoicing, reporting, and revenue recovery.
  • Oversee shipping logistics, ensuring the efficient and timely delivery of IT equipment for MCIU and contracted Local Education Agencies.
  • Participate in cross-functional projects supporting organizational efficiency and innovation.
  • Maintain a high level of customer service, professionalism, confidentiality, and attention to detail.
  • Identify opportunities for process improvement and operational efficiencies.
  • Maintain current knowledge and a base understanding of internal and external client systems and new technologies.
  • Project a positive image of the IU and its programs and services.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned by the Supervisor of Strategic Technology Services.

title: Computer Vision Engineer, Reality Labs
description:
The Reality Labs organization is helping more people around the world come together and connect through Virtual Reality and Wearables products. With global departments dedicated to research and development in computer vision, machine learning, haptics, social interaction, and more, Reality Labs is committed to advancing the state of the art through ongoing research and development. The potential to change the world is immense - and we’re just getting started.

Our Mixed Reality (XR) organization is focused on advanced research and development of machine perception technologies from early concepts to production level across all of Reality Labs' products and surfaces. These include Quest products, Meta Glasses and Family of Apps (Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp). We develop core capabilities across a range of product domains including avatars, AR/VR remote presence and calling, commerce, content sharing, spatial computing, sensor calibration, and more.

In this role, you will be researching and applying a range of software, computer vision and machine learning techniques for solving challenges that bridge virtual and real worlds and will impact billions of people. We're addressing a variety of technical challenges in the areas of real-time image processing, 3D graphics, SLAM, scene reconstruction, machine perception, visualization and human interaction. As well there are opportunities to collaborate with researchers in Reality Labs (RL) and Facebook AI Research (FAIR).

title: Verzorgende IG Kleinschalig Wonen
description:
Voor onze kleinschalige woonlocatie Singelhof zijn wij op zoek naar een Verzorgende IG. Een unieke werkplek met een warm en hecht team, waar je dagelijks bijdraagt aan de zorg, het welzijn en een fijne leefomgeving van onze bewoners met een somatische zorgvraag.

Wat ga je doen?

Voor locatie Singelhof hebben wij een mooie vacature voor een Verzorgende IG. Het betreft een unieke werkplek met een hecht en betrokken team, waar je dagelijks een belangrijke bijdrage levert aan het welzijn van ouderen met een somatische zorgvraag. In deze functie ondersteun je bewoners bij de dagelijkse zorg en begeleiding en zorg je ervoor dat zij een fijne en waardevolle dag beleven. Je werkt 8-uursdiensten in de dag, avond en nacht, waarbij je ook om het weekend inzetbaar bent. Een afwisselende functie binnen een warme en persoonlijke woonomgeving.
Als Verzorgende IG draag je elke dag bij aan het welzijn van onze bewoners. Jij maakt het verschil door persoonlijke zorg, oprechte aandacht en professionele ondersteuning. Je werkzaamheden bestaan o.a. uit:

  • Het bieden van passende persoonlijke verzorging;
  • Het uitvoeren van verpleegtechnische handelingen;
  • Het signaleren van veranderingen in de gezondheid of behoefte van bewoners;
  • Het creëren van een warme, veilige en liefdevolle woonomgeving.

Wat moet je weten over deze locatie?

Singelhof lijkt gewoon maar is een bijzonder woon-zorgcomplex. In Singelhof hebben we twee woongroepen in aparte woningen van zes bewoners gehuisvest. Het Kleinschalig Wonen biedt huisvesting en zorg aan bewoners met psychogeriatrische problematiek. Tevens bevindt zich in Singelhof een ontmoetingscentrum en een recreatieruimte waar bewoners en buurtgenoten terecht kunnen voor diverse activiteiten en een kopje koffie.

Wat krijg je?

  • Salaris in FWG 35 (CAO-VVT);
  • Contract voor 16-32 uren per week alle diensten;
  • Vitale werkomgeving met ruimte voor persoonlijke ontwikkeling via het Foreestcollege;
  • Vaste wensdag (een dag die je wel of niet wilt werken) daar houden we rekening mee;
  • Prettige werkomgeving met fijne collega’s;
  • Veel voldoening uit het ondersteunen van onze bewoners;
  • Bekijk onze aantrekkelijke secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden via deze link.

Bovenop deze al mooie arbeidsvoorwaarden bieden wij je ook een zeer aantrekkelijk Meerkeuzesysteem Arbeidsvoorwaarden. In ons Meerkeuzesysteem Arbeidsvoorwaarden vind jij vast een mooi voordeel waar wij jou blij mee kunnen maken.

  • Via Pieter van Foreest kun je voordelig een fiets leasen;
  • Voordelig kopen van elektronica;
  • Voordelig een dagje weg of sparen voor leuke producten? Via Fun bij Pieter is dit mogelijk;
  • Lekker sporten met korting? Wij betalen een deel van je abonnement;
  • Heb je een keer behoefte aan een langere vakantie? Dan kun je hiervoor extra verlofuren inkopen.

Jouw profiel:

  • Afgeronde opleiding tot Verzorgende IG of eerder behaald diploma die hieraan voldoet;
  • Warme persoonlijkheid met respect en integriteit voor onze bewoners en familie of mantelzorgers;
  • Ervaring in de omgang met cliënten met somatische problematiek is een pré;
  • Beschikbaar voor alle diensten in overleg;
  • Flexibele instelling in taken en werktijden;
  • Positieve en energieke instelling;
  • Gastvrij en representatie.

Heb je vragen?

Werken bij Pieter van Foreest is werken bij een veelzijdige en vooruitstrevende organisatie. Je krijgt de ruimte om je te ontwikkelen en we waarderen het als je zelf initiatief neemt. We vinden het belangrijk voor onze cliënten dat we persoonsgericht werken en zodoende bijdragen aan hun welbevinden. Dat is waar we het voor doen. Bij Pieter van Foreest is er altijd een plek waar jouw kwaliteiten tot zijn recht komen. We bieden namelijk een breed pakket aan zorg, behandeling en welzijn voor ouderen. Dit doen we in de regio’s Delft, Pijnacker-Nootdorp, Westland en Midden-Delfland. De organisatie telt 28 locaties, biedt thuiszorg, hulp bij het huishouden, revalidatie en herstel, ontmoetingscentra en diverse services en diensten. Samen met 3850 medewerkers en 1550 vrijwilligers maak jij hét verschil voor onze cliënten. En dat wordt gewaardeerd! Pieter van Foreest behoort, zowel met de Thuiszorg als de Verpleeghuiszorg, tot de top 5 best gewaardeerde Wijkverpleging - en Verpleeghuiszorgorganisaties op Zorgkaart Nederland .

title: Skap duften av nybakte brød og bakevarer - bli bakeriansvarlig på MENY Ski Storsenter
description:
I MENY elsker vi mat! For oss er god mat en lidenskap, og noe av det viktigste som finnes. Hos oss er alle MATarbeidere, uansett om du jobber i ferskvaredisken, kolonialen, i kassen eller på kontoret. Å være en MATarbeider i MENY betyr at du alltid gjør ditt beste for å veilede og inspirere kundene våre til matglede. Sammen skal vi hjelpe flere å spise bedre, og leve bedre.

Stillingsomfang: 100%
Arbeidstid: dag, kveld og annenhver helg
Oppstart: 01.10.2026 - eller etter avtale

Søknadsfrist: vi behandler søknader fortløpende


For å søke må du ha fylt 18 år, du må også kunne beherske norsk.

Hvem er den vi søker etter?
For å lykkes som bakeriansvarlig må du kunne arbeide selvstendig, ha en viss grad av struktur og orden, ha evne til å beregne mengder ut ifra salgstall og svinn. Du må også trives med å være i aktivitet, da store deler av hverdagen vil være preget av gåing, ståing og løfting. Mange av oppgavene i bakeriet er rutinepreget, så denne stillingen passer for deg som liker forutsigbarhet i oppgavene.

Arbeidsoppgaver:

  • Daglig drift og utvikling av bakeriet

  • Sørge for at din avdeling er velfylt og ryddig

  • Åpne/stenge avdelingen

  • Bestille varer, varemottak

  • Opplegg av varer og IK-mat

  • Lære opp MATarbeidere som skal ha vakter i bakeriet, og tilrettelegge for at de mestrer sine oppgaver når du ikke er der

Hvordan er det å jobbe på MENY Ski Storsenter?

Alle som begynner i MENY vil lære å ta ansvar, mestre stress, håndtere mennesker og ikke minst butikkdrift. Vi har en interaktiv kursplattform, ulike klasseromskurs som gir deg faglig påfyll og et traineeprogram med fokus på å gå fra ansatt til å bli leder, for å nevne noe. Satser du på MENY, satser MENY på deg!

Her på MENY Ski Storsenter vil du jobbe i en av de største og fineste butikkene i landet. Vi har derfor noen flere ansatte enn i mange andre butikker og et høyt fagnivå. Her er det med andre ord mange å lære av. Vi satser og liker å drive god butikk. Om vi skal låne en idrettsmetafor så kan du si at vi liker å «blø for drakta».

Vi er opptatt av å trives på jobb og liker å spre glede og latter. Vi tar vare på hverandre og er opptatt av at alle skal bli sett. Å drive en stor butikk er avhengig av godt samarbeid mellom alle. Velkommen skal du være!

Å søke jobb i MENY skal være enkelt

Du trenger ikke laste opp søknadsbrev. For at vi skal bli litt bedre kjent med deg, svarer du på spørsmålene om deg og din erfaring. Har du mye på hjertet må du gjerne skrive utfyllende, vi gleder oss til å lese! Og fordi vi synes det er spennende å se hvor du har vært tidligere, må du laste opp CV.

Vi gjør oppmerksom på at alle søknader må sendes inn via søknadsskjema tilknyttet annonsen, dette er av hensyn til ditt personvern, samt at vi ønsker å være sikre på at vi klarer å følge opp alle kandidater på en god måte. Vi kan derfor ikke ta imot søknader på papir i butikken eller via e-post. Søknader behandles fortløpende.
