title: Senior Systems Analyst Coordinator - SIS
description:
Full-Time and Permanent; 7.5 Hours/Day; 252 Days/Year; 12 Months/Year; Grade F

DEFINITION

Performs advanced computer systems analysis work on the NPS student information management systems (SIS) and assists the Senior Coordinator with management of the SIS workgroup. An employee assigned to a position in this class is responsible for working with school-based and central office personnel to determine their information and data processing needs, coordinating the processing of SIS functions, and training users in the use of the SIS. The specific SIS work involves coordinating and supporting one or more major SIS functions and providing coordination and support to schools and central administration for other SIS functions assigned by the Senior Coordinator, SIS.

SUPERVISION

Work is performed under the general supervision of a Senior Coordinator, Student Information Systems. Established policies and procedures provide guides for the work. Most work decisions are made independently. All work is reviewed for errors and conformance to established standards and procedures. May exercise direct supervision over other specialists/analysts and provide technical supervision over staff assigned to projects managed by the position.

DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS

This is the most advanced systems analyst level in the information systems specialist series. It is distinguished from the Systems Analyst - Coordinator classification by its broader scope, increased complexity, responsibility for coordinating major SIS functions, and assistance with SIS workgroup management.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE CLASS (May not include all duties performed by each position in the class).

Takes the lead in the coordination of multiple major SIS functions. Major functions would include student scheduling, grade reporting, enrollment, discipline, special program management, and system administration responsibilities. For these functions, prepares documentation and training materials, and organizes and conducts training sessions for school-based SIS users, including but not limited to: principals, assistant principals, teachers, and office staff.

Manages and coordinates the development, implementation, and operation of systems and programs that interface with the Student Information System (SIS) applications and databases.

Confers with NPS administration to identify information needs and potential data sources; supervises the collection, extraction, and use of data from SIS databases; and oversees the design of forms, reports, and related tools for presenting information.

Identifies SIS data inaccuracies and works with other systems analysts responsible for other SIS functions, and with information systems professionals responsible for reporting and record keeping, to identify data inaccuracies, and to develop error reports, documentation, and procedures for users to aid in the correction and elimination of SIS data errors.

Leads other information systems staff in the development of informational presentations or reports; assigns portions of projects to staff and provides technical work direction; checks and tests work for acceptance; monitors and reports progress to supervisor.

Confers with user staff to determine information needs; determines potential sources of information; collects data into or extracts data from SQL databases; designs forms, reports, and related items for information presentation.

Performs cyclical SIS processes such as grade reporting, academic history rollover, state discipline extract production. Responds to ad hoc requests for summary information not available in standard reports.

Assists Senior Coordinator, SIS, with workgroup management responsibilities such as budget planning, professional development planning for junior IS specialists, and computer system updates.

Performs related work as required.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES

Ability to analyze, troubleshoot and improve complex automated systems and processes.

Ability to lead project teams and to coordinate large-scale, long-term projects and processes.

Thorough knowledge of automated grade books.

Thorough knowledge of SQL.

Thorough knowledge of the principles, concepts and techniques of computer systems analysis and programming.

Thorough knowledge of computer design, hardware capabilities, operating systems and software.

Thorough knowledge of the general organization and functions of a large public school system.

Ability to design, develop, coordinate, and present large scale informational and training presentations.

Ability to use SQL database query and reporting tools to produce information presentations and reports.

Ability to provide technical guidance to information systems staff and to evaluate their work.

Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.

Ability to read and interpret highly technical manuals covering computer hardware and software, and to interpret technical instructions into common language for users.

Ability to listen effectively and to accurately determine the needs of information requestors.

Skill in writing, documenting, debugging and testing application programs in an accurate, efficient and timely manner.

MINIMUM EDUCATION, TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

Possession of a bachelor’s degree in computer science, management information systems, or a related field (graduate level course work preferred), and extensive experience in working as a computer systems analyst with responsibility for major application programs, some of which shall have been at the level of Systems Analyst - Coordinator, preferably including applications used in public school systems. Working knowledge of the district SIS (Synergy) is a plus.

LICENSE/CERTIFICATION

Valid driver’s license.

PHYSICAL ATTRIBUTES

This work involves physical effort encountered in everyday activities including sitting, walking, standing, bending, reaching. It may also require carrying a laptop computer and working in small, tight areas.

HAZARDS

Work involves exposure to normal, everyday risks. Work requires sustained use of desktop computers.

UNUSUAL DEMANDS

The work may entail overtime and after hours on call response. Furthermore, this work is subject to changing requirements, priorities, and interruptions. Resilience under pressure is essential.

  • Stewarding our AI amplified Databricks based framework, maintaining it and improving it incrementally as we learn.

  • Designing data models that bring sources from anywhere in the world into a single coherent shape.

  • Building data solutions for domains like custom MDM, geocoding, client mastering, and profiling. Real estate context is a plus but not required.

  • Designing and implementing stable, automated ingestion pipelines from diverse sources.

  • Owning production troubleshooting and root cause analysis. When things go wrong, you diagnose and resolve pipeline failures, performance issues, and data quality problems by working through code, logs, and documentation systematically.

  • Reporting on data quality and shipping the improvements that move the numbers.

What we are looking for

Core technical skills

  • Systems thinking. You see the bigger picture and build for scale rather than for the ticket in front of you.

  • Production troubleshooting and root cause analysis. You diagnose and resolve pipeline failures, performance issues, and data quality problems under pressure, working through code, logs, and documentation systematically rather than guessing.

  • Data modeling. You design cross functional data products, establish data contracts, and handle complex business rules.

  • Advanced SQL, including window functions, query optimization, and MERGE/UPSERT operations.

  • Python and PySpark. You write reusable, parameterized functions and work comfortably with JSON, CSV, and Parquet.

Platform knowledge

  • Deep experience with Databricks (Declarative Pipelines, DABS, Delta Lake, Spark optimization, job orchestration).

  • Familiarity with the Azure ecosystem.

  • Working understanding of Unity Catalog.

About you

  • Around 6 or more years of relevant experience.

  • A degree in a quantitatively rigorous field such as computer science, data science, econometrics, mathematics, or physics.

  • Driven and curious. You want to work on things that have not been figured out yet.

  • Strong written communication. Async updates and clear documentation are part of the job.

Nice to have

  • Experience with agentic data engineering, using coding agents in real delivery and building the harness around them: repo conventions, reusable context, tests and guardrails that make agent output trustworthy.

  • Geospatial data processing (H3 indexes, spatial SQL, point in polygon at scale).

  • Recursive CTEs and complex SQL patterns.

  • Infrastructure familiarity (Azure Portal, resource management, CLI).

  • Strong Git workflows and code review habits.

  • Real estate domain experience.

What we offer

  • Autonomy. We set the high level roadmap. You decide how to get there.

  • Dedicated learning time and a team that levels each other up. The frontier moves weekly. We give you the time to keep up with it, and you will be surrounded by people doing the same.

  • A rare growth path. You will build leading capability in a field where very few organisations in our sector have yet begun, giving you a skill set you could not have assembled elsewhere in this industry.

description:
General Purpose of Position

The Quality Assurance Technician must strive to meet Reinke Manufacturing company goals by maximizing both internal and external customer satisfaction, eliminating product quality defects and eliminating process waste and scrap. The Quality Assurance Technician engages in the daily activities required to assure that all Reinke Manufacturing Company processes and products meet established quality expectations and specifications. The Quality Assurance Technician is also responsible for the continuous improvement of all Reinke Manufacturing irrigation products and services by the maintenance, implementation and development of the Reinke Quality System. The incumbent must conduct the performance of duties and responsibilities in coordination with all functional areas and in agreement with Reinke policy and procedures.

Essential Functions

  • Must be capable of working on multiple projects, managing multiple tasks simultaneously and be capable of working with deadlines and due dates.
  • Must be self motivated and capable of working with limited supervision.
  • Will take quality checks of all the products being produced; i.e. fabrication, welding, assemblies, galvanizing, etc.
  • May need to assist Supervision with training of the employees on the production documentation and how to build products per documentation; i.e. drawings, schematics, assembly and inspection plans.
  • Must have good problem solving skills; be capable of devising solutions to quality and production issues by making data driven decisions.
  • Must have good writing skills; be capable of writing reports and accurately recording and reporting quality inspection data.
  • Must be capable of basic arithmetic, demonstrated knowledge of the ability to add, subtract, multiply, divide, use fractions, decimals, and calculate averages and percentages.
  • Must be capable of organizing, working on and supporting teams, must be willing to take team leadership roles as needed.
  • Must have good communication skills; be capable of interacting with all levels of plant staff.
  • Must be capable of following written and verbal instructions
  • Must assist with calibration within the company. Gather tools due for calibration. Audit calibration records for the tools located. May need to serve as Alternate UL Representative for the facilities requiring it. May need to calibration tools.
  • Must be able to understand and interpret blueprints; technical and service bulletins; production specifications; inspection plans and process procedures and work instructions.
  • Continually audit production documentation; i.e. IPIs, travelers, bill of materials, routings, work instructions, inspections and schematics. Assist in keeping the documents up to date, revise and restructure as needed.
  • May need to understand product structures; i.e. bill of materials and routings.
  • May need to be able to take a product and break it down step by step, then create and document work instructions and or inspection plans for products being built.
  • May need to be able to work with Engineering and Supervisor to take a product and break it down by bill of material structure and routing information, then restructure, revise and create what is necessary to lean out the product.
  • Must have a very good work ethic, must be team oriented with a positive, supportive outlook, and dedicated to quality and continual improvement of both the product and the process.
  • Must understand that this position carries a great deal of independent thinking and individual responsibility.
  • Must have basic computer skills; i.e. e-mail, word processing, spreadsheets, and be willing to train in paperless and Mapics.
  • Must have some working knowledge of measurements using various measuring and gauging equipment.
  • Must be familiar and cognizant of safety rules, regulations and guidelines as dictated by company policy.
  • Must be able to handle various physical requirements of the position.
  • Must maintain a good attendance record in accordance with company policy.
  • Must be capable of performing other related duties and tasks as needed under direction of Supervisor.

Describe Critical Skills, Experience, Training, Education, or Licenses Required

Receives on the job training. Some basic weld knowledge is required. Advanced weld knowledge is required for the trainer positions of the weld product. Advanced electrical assembly knowledge is required for the trainer position of the electrical product.

*Achieving Tech Level I requires successful completion of greater than half of the required training categories. *Achieving Tech Level II can be achieved by successfully completing greater than half of the NDT required training categories. Or by completing one or more of the other four categories in the Level II section.
In order to perform QA training roles (electrical, welding, or other) it’s preferred that an individual have 3 or more years of work experience and be proficient in building the product they would be training.

Machines, Tools, Equipment and Personal Protective Equipment Used

This position requires use of tape measure; micrometers; calipers; mill meter; profile tester; and ordinary hand tools. This position requires safety glasses with side shields, steel-toed shoes, hearing protection. Gloves may be requested on occasion.

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Global Payouts, ABPX
description:
In the Amazon Global Payouts team, we're embarking on an ambitious journey to transform our global payouts architecture. As we advance into the next generation of payouts capabilities, we're seeking an exceptional Engineering Leader to join us in revolutionizing how Amazon handles payouts worldwide.

In this role, you'll be at the forefront of modernizing our Payments APIs and developing cutting-edge payout systems that serve millions of Amazon's sellers, vendors, and partners globally. This isn't just about maintaining existing systems – it's about reimagining and rebuilding critical financial infrastructure that will power Amazon's worldwide operations for years to come.

We're looking for someone who brings both deep technical expertise and strong leadership capabilities. You'll drive product direction, shape roadmap planning, and lead project execution while working closely with talented engineers to develop innovative solutions. The ideal candidate will thrive in our unique environment that combines the agility of a startup with the resources and scale of Amazon.

This is more than just a leadership role – it's an opportunity to shape the future of payments at one of the world's largest companies. If you're passionate about solving complex technical challenges at massive scale and have the leadership skills to drive transformative change, we want to talk to you.

You'll be joining a team that values innovation, thinks big, and is committed to revolutionizing how payments work at Amazon. Together, we'll build the next generation of payment capabilities that will support Amazon's continued growth and success worldwide.

The Global Payouts organization enable Amazon Businesses to send payments to beneficiaries (Seller, Flex, Vendors, etc.) World Wide. We develop highly available, secure and resilient systems to disburse millions of transaction integrating with banking partners.

title: ServiceNow IRM Senior Analyst
description:
About Northern Trust


As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions.


Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide.


With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service.



ROLE MANDATE

Lead the functional analysis and definition of enterprise Governance, Risk and Controls capabilities delivered through ServiceNow Integrated Risk Management. The role combines deep IRM platform knowledge, broad GRC domain expertise, and senior-level business analysis to turn complex risk, compliance, audit, and control needs into clear, scalable, testable solutions. The successful candidate will operate as the bridge between Risk, Compliance, Audit, Operations, Product Management, Architecture, Engineering, Data, and Testing teams.

Position Summary

The Senior ServiceNow IRM Business Analyst is the functional lead for one or more GRC capabilities and a subject matter expert in the end-to-end risk and control lifecycle. This individual leads discovery, process analysis, requirement definition, solution validation, and adoption activities for ServiceNow IRM. The role ensures that business outcomes, regulatory expectations, enterprise taxonomies, data standards, and platform best practices are reflected in the delivered solution.

This is not a generalist requirements role. The successful candidate should be able to challenge unclear requests, connect requirements across GRC disciplines, identify downstream impacts, and guide stakeholders toward consistent enterprise processes that favor sustainable, out-of-the-box platform capabilities over unnecessary customization.

Key Responsibilities

GRC and IRM Functional Leadership

  • Provide senior-level functional expertise across the ServiceNow IRM suite and the broader governance, risk, compliance, and audit ecosystem.

  • Connect requirements across the end-to-end lifecycle, including taxonomy and foundational data, identification and assessment, controls, testing and monitoring, issues and remediation, reporting, and assurance.

  • Advise stakeholders on fit-to-platform options, process standardization, reuse, and implications for adjacent capabilities.

  • Act as the functional owner for assigned capabilities from discovery through implementation, validation, deployment, and continuous improvement.

Discovery, Process Analysis and Requirements

  • Plan and facilitate workshops with business, risk, compliance, audit, operations, data, and technology stakeholders.

  • Document current-state and target-state processes, business rules, decision points, roles, handoffs, data needs, controls, pain points, and expected outcomes.

  • Translate business and regulatory needs into unambiguous functional requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, data definitions, and traceability artifacts.

  • Perform gap, impact, dependency, and root-cause analysis across processes, data, workflows, integrations, reporting, security roles, and operating-model responsibilities.

  • Maintain requirement quality throughout delivery, including versioning, approvals, traceability, and change control.

Solution Definition and Delivery Partnership

  • Partner with Product Owners, architects, engineers, platform teams, data teams, and test leads to shape scalable ServiceNow IRM solutions.

  • Lead functional design reviews and showbacks, confirm that proposed configurations satisfy business intent, and document decisions and tradeoffs.

  • Support backlog refinement, prioritization, sprint planning, dependency management, release planning, and readiness activities.

  • Identify where requests conflict with enterprise standards, duplicate existing functionality, introduce control gaps, or create unsustainable customization.

  • Support production triage and enhancement analysis by distinguishing defects, data issues, training gaps, process gaps, and new requirements.

Testing, Adoption and Operational Readiness

  • Define end-to-end business scenarios and acceptance criteria spanning multiple IRM capabilities and lines of defense.

  • Coordinate functional validation and user acceptance testing, including test data, expected outcomes, defect clarification, retesting, and business sign-off.

  • Ensure process documentation, role guidance, training inputs, communications, support procedures, and reporting needs are ready for release.

  • Partner with change and business teams to drive adoption, capture feedback, and prioritize improvements based on business value and control outcomes.

Salary Range:

$95,600 - 162,400 USD

Salary range is a good faith estimate of base pay. Northern Trust provides a comprehensive benefits package including retirement benefits (401k and pension), health and welfare benefits (medical, dental, vision, spending accounts and disability), paid time off, parental and caregiver leave, life & accident insurance, and other voluntary and well-being benefits. Northern Trust also provides a discretionary bonus program that may include an equity component.


Work Authorization


Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. Northern Trust will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work visa status for this opportunity (no sponsorship is available for H-1B, L-1, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, F-1, J-1, OPT, CPT or any other employment-based visa).


Working with Us


As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve.


Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities.


Reasonable Accommodation


Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing adjustments to individuals with health conditions and disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com, or alternatively you can discuss your individual requirements with the recruiter you are working with.

title: Product Manager - Tech, Amazon Robotics - S&O - PACE
description:
The Amazon TD PACE (Tech Deployment - Product, Analytics and Customer Experience) within S&O (Strategy and Operations) organization is seeking a product manager – technical (PM-T) to drive customer experience and product strategy. This PMT will own AI centered systems/tools used during the planning and execution of robotics deployment in our fulfillment centers. They will facilitate the organization in making data driven bar raising decisions, through seamless partnership with the deployment teams and becoming an expert on field usage of the systems and tools they own. This is a fantastic opportunity to work with some of the best engineers in the industry and shape the direction of one of the world’s largest robotics driven fulfillment networks.

The organization you are part of is composed of teams which invent for rapid scaling of complex technical solutions, develop products for industrial equipment automation, and provide product ownership through unique field deployment expertise on robotic deployments. The software tools you build will improve deployment quality, cost, speed and add features that reduce complexity creating ease of use and operational excellence.

The focus of this PM-T role is the software products and associated AI Agents used to manage deployment of Amazon fulfillment center technology globally. These software products are leveraged by Amazon internal project managers, Amazon internal program managers, and internal and external installers. The scope of these products include functionality such as: project initiation, project planning, project execution, project monitoring & control, project budgeting, mobile application access, standard work instruction, task automation, and data insights and visualization. The products standardize, track, and enable automation in deployment execution which improves reliability and repeatability of Amazon’s deployment and testing processes.

In PACE, our PM-Ts are expected to listen attentively and speak candidly. Those conversations start with our customers and work backwards to collaborate with our development teams in the TD organization. Our PM-Ts seek data and diverse perspectives and use that insight to respectfully challenge decisions. We push ourselves and our development teams to accomplish more with less. We think big and do not sacrifice long-term value for short-term results. Your success as a TD PM-T will be measured on ROI (known internally as entitlement), customer satisfaction, and attainment of the product’s committed benefits.


Key job responsibilities
Product Focus
- Works with field teams to understand their problems and aggregate them into comprehensive use-cases.
- Support a complex robotics deployment organization through in-field product feedback gathering
- Evangelist of the product in the field, seeking new opportunities to increase depth and breadth of the installation base.
- Establishes the tangible and intangible value proposition of solving the problems in the use-case.
- Identifies capabilities to solve customer problems and works them into the strategy.
- Communicate roadmap updates to stakeholders and customers.
- Accountable to the customer for delivery of promised product value.
Voice of the customer
- Document understanding of the field customers, customer tasks, and their problems for the team’s use.
- Advocate for the customer’s needs with the team creating the robotics product.
- Gathers inputs from stakeholders, customers, and product team to determine prioritization.
- Seek or facilitates customer feedback on designs, early versions of product features, or demos.
Strategy
- Creates a benefit + entitlement VS effort analysis of the proposed product capabilities.
- Defines tangible and intangible (soft) benefit to be created by execution of the product roadmap
- Defines a roadmap with a goal of delivering the maximum benefit to the customer and long-term company value.
- Produce clear, concise documents (e.g., functional, technical specifications, PR/FAQs).
- Impacts and defines the customer experience (CX), feature usability, success metrics (e.g., customer delight, efficiency, ROI), and team-level business goals.


A day in the life
Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners and their children. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment. The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:

1. Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
2. Maternity and Parental Leave Options
3. Paid Time Off (PTO)
4. 401(k) Plan

If you are not sure that every qualification on the list above describes you exactly, we'd still love to hear from you! At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

Position Summary:

  • This position is responsible collecting semen and inseminating hens, up to 1,500 birds a day / 180-240 per hour with a two {2} person team, in egg production areas by performing all essential duties in rotation with others. Other duties may be assigned.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Catch rooster and control for milking per animal welfare guidelines (25%)
  • Stimulate male and collect semen into vial, visually observe collected semen for viability (25%)
  • Catch hen, invert, and present oviduct for insemination per animal welfare guidelines (25%)
  • Performs simple math [addition, subtraction, multiplication and division] as part of recording information according to instructions and Cobb standards ie: bird weight, medications, feed intake, and mortality (15%)

Other duties, responsibilities, and activities: (10%)

  • Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice. Such as: Move birds between houses, lab sample swabs, operate a high pressure and regular water hose, maintains foot pans and hand sanitizer, maintain equipment by checking fluid levels, filters, tire pressure, and clean/disinfect to remove debris, maintains a clean and organized work area.
  • Inspects birds to determine quality and progress by weighing birds weekly; carry out swabbing duties as needed; sanitation of breakroom, boot rooms, equipment, and vehicles; properly euthanize weak/ill birds in accordance with company policy
  • Supervises and assists with: Records information according to instructions such genealogy, bird weight, medications, feed intake, and mortality
  • Assist with the collection and evaluation of semen quality based on parameters like motility, mobility, density, color, and volume, input semen quality data using tablets, laptops, and scanners as needed

Biosecurity/Animal Welfare Requirements:

  • The jobsite is a biosecure environment which requires showering, changing clothing and footwear before entering the facility. Appropriate clothing and footwear are provided by the Company. No jewelry may be worn on the jobsite except for medical ID jewelry and body piercings covered by appropriate clothing. Must be willing to sign an agreement to avoid any avian species (chickens, ducks, birds, etc.). Must be willing to sign and abide by the Company Biosecurity and Company Animal Welfare Guidelines.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

  • Physical: Must regularly lift and control hens and roosters weighing up to 16 pounds and carry catch frames weighing up to 10 pounds for distances up to 300 feet. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand majority of shift on a concrete floor; repetitive use of arms to reach and hands to handle or feel animals, objects, or tools up to 8 hrs per day; walk; sit;, or feel objects, tools, or controls; balance; bend and stoop; talk or hear. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision; distance vision; color vision; peripheral vision; depth perception; and the ability to adjust focus.
  • The successful candidate(s) must be willing and able to perform the physical requirements of the job with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Tools and Equipment: Requires use of hand tools such as pipettors and tips, vials; equipment such as catch frames; safe operation of vehicle to and from work area.
  • Environment: Required to work on wet, slippery surfaces and in hot, dry, dusty, wet and cold environments.
  • Personal Protective Equipment Required: Safety goggles and/or glasses, chemical gloves, waterproof apron, and rubber boots are required. Arm protectors are available if desired.
  • Chemicals Commonly Used: Semen extender, disinfectants, vehicle fluids, and lubricants.
  • Safety: Team member is expected to follow all applicable safety policies and procedures. These include but are not limited to Hazard Communication, Respiratory Protection, LOTO and Personal Protective Equipment. Team member is expected to identify, address and mitigate safety related risks.

title: Summer Analyst
description:
Are you looking for an internship where your work directly contributes to a billion-dollar plus business? Headquartered in St. Petersburg, Florida, Dynasty Financial Partners powers the back and middle office of independent financial advisors within the wealth management industry operating as RIAs (Registered Investment Advisor). For 15 plus years, Dynasty has supported a select group of advisor-owned RIAs to help them better serve their clients, grow their businesses, and build long-term enterprise value.


As of Q2 2026, the Dynasty Network includes 750+ advisors managing $142B+ in platform assets, growth that's backed by some of the largest names in finance. As a premier WealthTech platform, Dynasty Financial Partners enhances RIAs in its network by delivering proprietary middle and back-office support such as technology, growth and investment platform capabilities. In addition, Dynasty’s investment bank offers flexible capital solutions and M&A support for advisors inside and outside the network, helping them grow, scale, and even liquidate their business.


During the program, summer analysts get real ownership over work that drives the business. Over the 10-week period, summer analysts will be assigned to support up to two business units within the firm. Below is a broad description of the business units covered in our program.


Summer Analyst Business Units:

  • Transitions: Onboarding new advisors and client accounts from previous advisory firms that want to join the Dynasty network and utilize our services to grow their RIAs. High level of logistical planning and project management can be expected. • Operations: Account servicing and lifecycle management, trade execution/rebalancing/model management, billing/advisor payouts, transaction reconciliation, and oversight of investment managers and programs — possibility to engage in client facing related business activities.
  • Outsourced Chief Financial Officer (OCFO): Provides Outsourced CFO services to RIA Network Partners. Services include preparation of all phases of the accounting cycle, production of monthly financial statement packages, preparation of operating budgets and financial projections. Financial performance is review with each Network Partner quarterly. Opportunity to engage in client facing related functions.
  • Relationship Management: Understanding what's important to our clients, business consulting, contract and pricing negotiation, and playing a “quarterback” role for the relationship. Learning/Managing a CRM (Salesforce) and updating raw data related to the network partner and/or their clients.
  • Human Resources: Recruiting and onboarding for the firm, supporting summer analyst program logistics and culture-building, with exposure to payroll and tax coordination alongside the Finance team.
  • Dynasty Investment Bank: Exposure to M&A transactions and strategic advisory engagements, including the development of pitch book presentations, marketing materials, industry research, and other deal-related materials. Summer Analysts will gain insight into transaction execution while working alongside senior bankers with prior bulge bracket experience across a variety of client engagements and capital deployment opportunities on both sides of the capital stack.
  • Dynasty Connect: The outsourced front-office growth engine for Network RIAs. Interns will gain exposure to investor-advisor matching within the Dynasty Network, prospecting strategies, and CRM-driven business development processes. There may also be opportunities to observe advisor outreach efforts, including prospecting and cold-calling activities that support institutional sales initiatives.
  • Business Development Operations: Support data cleansing and analysis in Salesforce, help manage the pipeline, and build reports that inform the team's sales process. You'll develop a working understanding of the competitive landscape across the wealth management industry, with possible exposure to live deals the team is actively working on.
  • Compliance: Assisting Network RIAs with regulatory filings, reviewing marketing and client communications, performing compliance best practice checks, and helping firms stay aligned with applicable regulatory requirements and internal policies.
  • Marketing / Public Relations (PR): Split across Corporate Marketing/PR and Network Partner Marketing/PR – day-to-day tasks involve brand management and deliverables, campaigns, email content, social content, and press for both Dynasty and our Network Partners.
  • Investments: Conducting portfolio analysis, understanding Dynasty Managed Model offering, learning about Dynasty's Platform offerings, developing market outlooks, performing other investment research, and supporting advisor-facing platform education and consulting.
  • Technology: Summer analysts work closely with different groups within our technology organization, embedding with the teams that run data and analytics, software and AI engineering, product, plus Dynasty Labs, our innovation arm that partners with leading technology companies to build AI products for the Network, including the Dynasty AI Suite and the Dynasty Virtual Assistant. You work hands-on with the same frontier AI development tooling our engineers ship with.
  • Finance: Exposure across the team's three core functions: FP&A (budgeting and forecasting), Accounting, and Middle Office (internal reporting) — plus evaluating corporate development opportunities, projecting revenues, updating pricing models, and paying invoices.

title: Solutions Architect II, State and Local Government, WWPS SLG/EDU
description:
Are you passionate about helping State and Local Government unlock the transformative power of cloud technology? Amazon Web Services is seeking a Solutions Architect II to serve as a trusted technical advisor to customers across North Florida. In this role, you'll combine your communication skills, problem-solving abilities, and eagerness to learn new technologies to guide diverse organizations through their cloud journey.

This is more than a typical technology consulting role. You'll work at the intersection of innovation and public service, helping local government agencies and K-12 schools architect solutions that modernize their operations, improve citizen and student experiences, and achieve mission-critical outcomes. Your ability to understand complex technical challenges and translate them into actionable solutions will help grow our State and Local Government businesses while making a meaningful impact on communities across the region.


Key job responsibilities
- Design and deliver cloud architecture solutions that meet infrastructure and application requirements for State and Local Government customers, incorporating best practices for security, scalability, and performance
- Lead architecture reviews, technical workshops, and proof-of-concept projects that demonstrate innovative cloud solutions and help customers envision transformative possibilities for their organizations
- Serve as a trusted technical advisor by taking the time to understand each customer's unique business context, technology challenges, and long-term goals, then translating those needs into technical requirements
- Collaborate with account teams, professional services, and AWS engineering groups to scope customer engagements with clear objectives, drive timely delivery of value, and ensure customer success throughout their cloud adoption journey
- Educate customers and internal teams by developing and delivering technical content such as presentations, workshops, and best practice guidance, while capturing and sharing knowledge that advances the broader Solutions Architecture community


A day in the life
Your day might begin with an architecture review session with a county IT department exploring modernization options for their legacy systems, followed by leading a hands-on workshop for a city's public safety team. After collaborating with your account team to develop a migration strategy for a K-12 district's on-premises student information system, you'll build a proof-of-concept that demonstrates using AI/ML services to identify at-risk students. You'll wrap up by joining a strategic planning discussion with a city CIO about how cloud technology can drive their smart city and digital government transformation objectives.

About the team
You'll join a collaborative team of Solutions Architects supporting State and Local Government and K-12 customers in Florida, as well as Higher Education customers across Florida, Georgia, and Tennessee, delivering exceptional technical guidance and driving cloud adoption across the public sector.

Our team thrives on the mission-driven nature of our customers, enabling these organizations serving communities and students. We foster continuous learning, knowledge-sharing, and innovation, where each member contributes expertise while growing across multiple domains. As part of AWS, you'll have endless learning opportunities working with cloud technologies shaping the future of government and education.

title: Part-Time Residential Weekend Monitor
description:
Part- Time Residential Weekend Monitor - Saturday's and/or Sunday's

Shift: 8A.M. - 4P.M.

Women’s Residential Program

Great opportunity for students or individuals seeking meaningful experience in the human services field
Hourly Rate: $17/hour | $19/hour (overnight coverage)

Shape Futures. Support Women’s Recovery. Strengthening Families and Communities.

Are you ready to make a difference during the moments that matter most? Imagine being a steady, supportive presence for women as they work toward safety, stability, recovery, and independence. As a Residential Weekend Monitor at our Maternal and Infant Program facility, you play a vital role in creating a safe, structured, and respectful environment where women—many of whom are justice-involved, parenting, or healing from trauma—can rebuild their lives.

This position is ideal for individuals who are mission-driven, dependable, and interested in gaining hands-on experience in women-centered residential services, substance use recovery, and trauma-informed programming. You will join a collaborative team committed to empowerment, accountability, cultural humility, and dignity.

What You Will Do

Responsibilities focus on resident supervision, safety, program support, and team collaboration during overnight, weeknight, and weekend shifts in a women’s residential setting.

Residential Supervision & Safety

  • Provide direct supervision, structure, and supportive presence to women residents during assigned overnight and/or weekend shifts.
  • Maintain a safe, calm, and respectful living environment that supports recovery and emotional regulation.
  • Conduct and document resident safety and quality assurance checks at least hourly during overnight shifts.
  • Enforce program expectations consistently while using a trauma-informed, gender-responsive approach.
  • Respond to crises using approved de-escalation and crisis intervention techniques.
  • Follow emergency protocols and contact On-Call Staff as required.
  • Observe and document medication self-administration in accordance with agency medication administration guidelines (this role does not administer medications).
  • Provide basic first aid and seek emergency medical care when necessary.
  • Assist with resident transportation needs, including distributing bus tokens when appropriate.

Facility & Security Responsibilities

  • Maintain building security, including locking doors and windows, activating alarms and exterior lighting, and ensuring an orderly overnight environment.
  • Respond appropriately to emergencies, including contacting police, fire, or medical services when warranted.
  • Identify and report maintenance or safety concerns to the Program Manager.
  • Serve as a professional and respectful agency representative to neighbors, visitors, volunteers, and community partners.

Team Collaboration & Communication

  • Maintain clear and timely communication through log notes, shift reports, and staff consultation to support continuity of care.
  • Provide thorough shift crossover communication to incoming staff.
  • Support coworkers with resident needs as appropriate.
  • Attend relief staff meetings with the Program Manager as requested.
  • Model expectations and job duties for new or training overnight staff.

Program & Resident Support

  • Supervise residents during recreational activities and daily/weekly house responsibilities.
  • Assist with resident orientation, including program expectations, safety procedures, visitation policies, and first-week requirements.
  • Support women’s adjustment to the program by reinforcing routine, accountability, healthy boundaries, and family/children’s visitation.
  • Assist the SUD Counselor with monitoring for substance use, including conducting urinalysis and breathalyzer screenings, documenting results, and consulting On-Call Staff as needed.
  • If infants reside in the facility, follow the Baby Care Manual and support mothers with infant care in a respectful, nonjudgmental manner.

Administrative & General Duties

  • Work scheduled shifts reliably. If unable to work due to illness or emergency, make every reasonable effort to secure coverage.
  • Complete all required documentation in accordance with agency policies and confidentiality standards.
  • Orient visitors and volunteers to program rules and expectations as needed.

title: Jr. Industrial Engineering Technician

title: Director of Student Transportation, Operations, and Logistics
description:
Job Title: Director of Student Transportation, Operations, and Logistics

Wage/Hour Status: Exempt

Reports to: Chief of Operations and Infrastructure Pay Grade: AM-7

Dept./School: Transportation Initiated Date: July 2026

WHO WE ARE

La Joya Independent School District (ISD) is committed to excellence for students and our community. We have a strong, 100-year legacy in the Rio Grande Valley. The district’s vision - Educational Excellence: The Right of Every Student - conveys our urgent focus on students.

Our work is rooted in three (3) Operational governing levers which require collaboration and deep commitment to supporting one another as we serve the school district and community.

  • Culture of Accountability
  • Equity by design
  • Destination District for staff and Students

We are focused on ensuring every student in La Joya ISD has access to a high-quality, best-fit school as we work to improve from a B-district to an A-rated district. We serve more than 22,000 students in more than 30 schools and span six municipalities, covering more than 220 square miles.

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are seeking an experienced, visionary, and results-driven leader to serve as the Director of Student Transportation, Operations, and Logistics. This individual will provide strategic leadership and oversight of the district's transportation logistics operations, ensuring the safe, efficient, and reliable transportation of students while supporting the district's mission of providing exceptional educational opportunities.

The Director is responsible for planning, coordinating, scheduling, routing, fleet utilization, and overseeing all logistical operations of the Transportation Department. This role provides executive oversight for the implementation, administration, optimization, and continuous improvement of the district's Transfinder transportation management system and all associated modules, including Stopfinder, Infofinder i, Wayfinder, and Tripfinder, ensuring these systems are fully leveraged to enhance routing efficiency, communication with families, field operations, trip management, and overall transportation performance.

The Director ensures compliance with all applicable federal, state, local, and district regulations while promoting operational excellence through innovation, continuous improvement, data-driven decision-making, fiscal responsibility, and exceptional customer service. This position is responsible for establishing best practices, monitoring key performance indicators, utilizing transportation analytics, and implementing technology-driven solutions that improve operational efficiency, student safety, and service reliability.

This position requires exceptional leadership, strategic planning, organizational expertise, and the ability to manage complex transportation systems that serve the needs of students, campuses, and district programs. The successful candidate will collaborate closely with district leadership, campus administrators, transportation personnel, parents, regulatory agencies, Transfinder representatives, and community partners to develop innovative transportation solutions that maximize safety, service quality, routing efficiency, fleet utilization, and operational effectiveness.

We are looking for a leader who demonstrates professionalism, integrity, sound judgment, and an unwavering commitment to student safety. The ideal candidate is a proactive problem solver with the ability to optimize routing and resource utilization; oversee and continuously improve the district's use of Transfinder and its integrated modules (Stopfinder, Infofinder i, Wayfinder, and Tripfinder); leverage transportation technology, GPS systems, and performance data to support informed decision-making; lead organizational change; and cultivate a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement throughout the Transportation Department. The Director must possess outstanding communication and relationship-building skills and be committed to delivering high-quality, technology-driven transportation services that positively support student success and district operations.

WHY LA JOYA ISD

You will be joining a district that is building on a legacy of achievement while rapidly improving and creating systems to reach new heights for student outcomes. You will receive intentional, targeted support in your leadership journey and have access to the highest-quality, research-based resources and instructional materials. We are also a district focused on continuous improvement and rigorous analysis of where we need to grow and learn.

Education/Certification Qualifications:

Required

  • Bachelor's degree Public Administration, Logistics, Educational Administration, or a related field.
  • Valid Texas Driver License with an acceptable driving record.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain all certifications required by the Texas Education Agency (TEA), Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS), and Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT).

Preferred

  • Master's degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Transportation Management, or related field.
  • Texas School Bus Driver Certification (CDL) (or ability to obtain).
  • Certified Director of Pupil Transportation (CDPT) or equivalent professional certification.

Professional Experience:

  • Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in school transportation, logistics, fleet management, or operations management.
  • Minimum of three (3) years in a supervisory or management capacity.
  • Experience managing transportation routing software, fleet operations, GPS systems, and transportation technology.
  • Experience developing transportation budgets and managing departmental expenditures.
  • Experience coordinating transportation for regular education, special education, extracurricular activities, field trips, and emergency operations.
  • Experience working in a public-school environment is preferred.

Special Knowledge/Skills:

  • Thorough knowledge of federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and policies governing public school transportation operations.
  • Knowledge of the Texas Education Code (TEC), Texas Education Agency (TEA) transportation funding requirements, Texas Student Data System (TSDS) transportation reporting, route services, ridership reporting, transportation allotment requirements, and all applicable state reporting processes.
  • Knowledge of Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) regulations, Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) requirements, and industry best practices for school transportation.
  • Advanced knowledge and experience with Transfinder and its integrated modules, including Stopfinder, Infofinder i, Wayfinder, and Tripfinder, for routing, parent communication, trip management, navigation, and transportation operations.
  • Knowledge of routing software, GPS tracking systems, telematics, fleet management systems, and transportation technologies used to improve operational efficiency and student safety.
  • Strong understanding of vehicle utilization, route optimization, logistics planning, transportation scheduling, bell-time analysis, and fleet capacity management.
  • Knowledge of school bus safety procedures, emergency management protocols, crisis response planning, and transportation risk management.
  • Knowledge of procurement procedures, contract administration, vendor management, and budget development related to transportation operations.
  • Ability to prepare, validate, analyze, and submit accurate state transportation reports, operational reports, performance metrics, and compliance documentation in accordance with TEA and district requirements.
  • Ability to analyze transportation, routing, ridership, and operational data to identify trends, improve efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance service delivery.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and project management skills with the ability to oversee multiple districtwide transportation initiatives simultaneously.
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to effectively collaborate with district leadership, campus administrators, parents, staff, regulatory agencies, and community partners.
  • Strong leadership, coaching, change management, and team-building skills with the ability to develop high-performing teams and foster a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Advanced proficiency in Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Drive, Calendar), Microsoft Office Suite, data management systems, and transportation management software.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality, exercise sound judgment, make data-driven decisions, and solve complex operational challenges in a fast-paced environment.

Major Responsibilities and Duties:

Leadership and Administration

  • Provide leadership and strategic direction for all district transportation logistics operations.
  • Develop departmental goals, objectives, and performance measures aligned with district strategic initiatives.
  • Establish procedures that promote safe, efficient, and cost-effective transportation services.
  • Recommend operational improvements through continuous evaluation of transportation processes.

Transportation Logistics

  • Direct daily transportation logistics, routing, scheduling, and dispatch operations.
  • Oversee the development and implementation of efficient bus routes.
  • Monitor route performance and adjust routes based on enrollment, traffic patterns, road construction, and safety concerns.
  • Coordinate transportation services for regular education, special education, extracurricular activities, athletic events, field trips, and district programs.
  • Ensure efficient utilization of buses, personnel, and resources.

Fleet Operations

  • Coordinate fleet assignments to maximize operational efficiency.
  • Collaborate with Fleet Maintenance to ensure buses meet all inspection, preventive maintenance, repair, and safety requirements.
  • Monitor fleet preventive maintenance schedules, vehicle availability, and fleet utilization to minimize downtime and maximize service reliability.
  • Assist in long-range fleet replacement planning, lifecycle management, and capital improvement recommendations.

Safety and Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and district transportation regulations.
  • Develop and monitor emergency transportation plans.
  • Coordinate transportation services during emergencies, evacuations, and district events.
  • Maintain required transportation records, reports, and documentation.
  • Promote a culture of safety and continuous compliance.

Budget and Financial Management

  • Assist in preparing and managing the departmental budget.
  • Monitor expenditures and transportation-related contracts.
  • Evaluate operational costs and recommend efficiencies.
  • Participate in procurement planning for vehicles, equipment, and transportation services.

Technology and Data Management

  • Utilize transportation software and GPS systems to improve routing efficiency.
  • Analyze operational metrics and transportation performance data.
  • Prepare reports for district leadership, administration, and the Board of Trustees.
  • Maintain accurate transportation records and operational dashboards.

Customer Service

  • Respond to transportation concerns from parents, campuses, and district administrators.
  • Collaborate with school principals and district departments to address transportation needs.
  • Promote positive relationships with students, parents, staff, and the community.

Other Duties

  • Attend Board meetings, administrative meetings, and professional development as assigned.
  • Serve on district committees as designated.
  • Perform other duties assigned by the Deputy Chief of Operations & Infrastructure or Chief of Operations & Infrastructure.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

Directly supervises assigned transportation personnel, which may include:

  • Transportation Route Supervisors
  • Transportation Dispatchers
  • Transportation Administrative Staff
  • Transportation Logistics Specialists
  • Bus Drivers
  • Fleet Mechanic Manager
  • Other assigned transportation personnel

Responsible for:

  • Hiring recommendations
  • Employee training and professional development
  • Performance evaluations
  • Scheduling and work assignments
  • Employee coaching and corrective action
  • Ensuring compliance with district policies and procedures
  • Promoting teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement

Working Conditions:

  • Frequent districtwide travel.
  • Occasional evening and weekend work as needed.
  • Ability to respond to transportation emergencies outside normal business hours.
  • Work performed in both office and outdoor environments.
  • Moderate exposure to weather conditions, vehicle operations, and maintenance facilities.

Performance Indicators

Success in this position will be measured by:

  • Safe and timely transportation of students.
  • Improved route efficiency and fleet utilization.
  • Compliance with all transportation regulations.
  • Reduced transportation costs through operational efficiencies.
  • Positive customer service and stakeholder satisfaction.
  • Accurate reporting and documentation.
  • Effective supervision and development of transportation personnel.
  • Successful implementation of transportation initiatives supporting district strategic goals.

title: Senior Cloud Platform Engineer
description:
Cloud Protection protects Fortune 500 enterprises and government organizations worldwide from malware, phishing, and identity-based attacks in Salesforce. Our work builds on more than 30 years of experience in analyzing malware and defending against advanced threats — expertise few security companies can match.

It's our people who make that possible. Newly independent after years as WithSecure's most autonomous business unit, we combine the focus and speed of a startup with decades of cybersecurity depth. We're a diverse team that values passion, purpose, and genuine wellbeing at work, and we're looking for people who want to set the standard for Salesforce security with us. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

We're looking for a Senior Cloud Platform Engineer to help build and own the AWS foundation for Cloud Protection for Salesforce (CPSF) — a fast-growing cybersecurity SaaS product by WithSecure™.

CPSF is a real-time threat protection solution that scans files, URLs, and QR codes across Salesforce workflows — including Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, and Agentforce. It's already trusted by Fortune 500 companies globally, and we're scaling fast. We're building a new, independent AWS environment from the ground up, and you'll own entire layers of that foundation end to end — designing it, building it in Terraform, proving it works, and standing behind it in production.

This is a small, hands-on team, so the scope is broad: the judgment you bring to decisions that can't be undone later matters as much as the code you write.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate our AWS landing zone — multi-account organization, guardrails, and account vending — so every new account is governed from the moment it exists.
  • Own our infrastructure-as-code estate in Terraform, including the module library, layered environments, and the review gates on the changes that carry real risk.
  • Build and own the network: multi-region VPCs, centralized egress, DNS, and private connectivity to external services.
  • Own data protection and identity: encryption and key management, SSO federation, least-privilege access, and break-glass paths that are actually rehearsed.
  • Own the evidence and observability plane: audit logging, configuration recording, security findings, dashboards, and alerting from the first day of every account's life.
  • Own delivery: OIDC-based deployment from CI, artifact and container registries, and policy and security checks that run on every change.
  • Plan and execute the migration of live production workloads into the new environment — staged rehearsals, cutover, soak period, and decommissioning what's left behind.
  • Build and maintain a controls baseline as code mapped to the frameworks we report against (SOC 2, ISO 27001), and keep the environment answerable by query rather than screenshots.
  • Spot the decisions that can't be undone later, flag them early, and take end-to-end ownership of the ones that affect the whole organization.

What are we looking for?

  • Substantial hands-on experience building and running production AWS at multi-account, multi-region scale — not just consuming it.
  • Deep Terraform experience, including the unglamorous parts: state, imports, adopting resources you didn't create, module design, and the review workflow around them.
  • Real breadth across networking, IAM, encryption and key management, logging and audit, backup and recovery, CI/CD, and cost.
  • Experience with at least one migration, re-platforming, or carve-out that touched live production — including the parts that went wrong.
  • A track record of owning an irreversible infrastructure decision, and being able to talk through how you approached it.
  • Comfortable working where the documentation is imperfect and the right answer has to be established, not just looked up.
  • Based in Finland (Uusimaa area) — this is a hybrid role with regular time in our Helsinki office.
  • Fluent English — written and verbal.

Nice to have: compliance-driven infrastructure work (SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar), AWS Control Tower and account-vending automation, and CloudFormation experience.

If you don’t tick every box above, don’t worry — we’re more interested in your potential and willingness to learn.

The salary displayed on this page represents a range for the role. Final compensation is discussed individually and depends on experience, skills, and the local market.

What will you get from us

  • Meaningful work with real-world impact – your work helps protect businesses and critical infrastructure from modern cyber threats.
  • Flexible ways of working, including up to 30 days per year working abroad and paid sick leave from day one.
  • A strong focus on well-being, with mental health support and comprehensive benefits.
  • Continuous learning, modern tools, and a people-first culture that values trust and collaboration.

title: Director of Technology [BASAS 11B] (Anticipated Vacancy (SY26-27)
description:
This position is an anticipated vacancy. It is expected to be vacant by 08/31/2026. However, the current incumbent has a right to rescind their retirement, leave, or resignation up until the day of the expected vacancy date. Your hire will not be confirmed until the position is vacated, and you may start the year as a Long-Term Substitute if the position does not become vacant by the start of the school year.

Position Overview:

The Madison Park technology director is responsible for securing, maintaining, and distributing the technology necessary for classroom instruction and building operations. The technology director also serves as an in-house help desk for staff having difficulties with hardware or software. The technology director will also ensure that technology integration is a priority and effectively implemented in classrooms. The director will work with members of the leadership and support staff to ensure that the necessary testing occurs across all grade levels in accordance with BPS and state testing schedules and work to create pathways for students to be responsible users of technology in the school space. This person will work to implement and support new technology processes and procedures for both adults and students that ensure that technology use is seamless and a priority. This includes the usage and integration of cell phones, Ipads, and other digital devices that enhance the schools overall ability to support students.

Job Goals:

  • Anticipate technology needs and proactively create plans the acquisition of new technology
  • Secure needed technology and funding to enhance programmatic goals.
  • Track, maintain, and replenish building technology in support with the district and any additional school funding via grants or otherwise
  • Distribute building technology.
  • Work to create policy and sustainable practices for technology use and integration schoolwide.
  • Support staff and students in acquiring the skills necessary to navigate technology needs within the school.
  • Assist with yearly generation of teacher and student schedules.
  • Prioritize planning and supporting the growth and development of a computer science pathway.
  • Train and supervise any additional staff in supporting the technology needs of the community.
  • Works directly with district support to develop best practices to support a large comprehensive high school while also making sure that collaboration is prioritized and our nuanced needs are met.

Responsibilities:

  • Secure, maintain, and distribute instructional and operational technology (e.g. Chromebooks, Chromebook carts, big screen TVs, video projectors, projector bulbs, document cameras, staff laptops, power supplies, speakers, audio-visual accessories, photocopiers, toner, paper, headphones, language lab equipment, electronic signage, and online services).
  • Set up and maintain systems for distributing, repairing, and replacing student Chromebooks, training and coordinating stipended technology coordinators.
  • Train, coordinate, and supervise student volunteers who assist with copy room maintenance and other technology-related tasks.
  • Provide on-the-spot technical support to staff members and students having difficulties with hardware or software.
  • Budget for technological needs and prioritize requests in accordance with funds availability.
  • Maintain Madison's website and post materials submitted by others.
  • Develop custom information technology solutions (e.g. library sign-up system, classroom coverage communications spreadsheet, tools for generating student and teacher schedules, numerous spreadsheets, automated system for posting events to schoolwide calendar, custom website interface scripting).
  • Select and use off-the-shelf information technology solutions (e.g. parents’ night scheduling software).
  • Prepare and send complex mail-merged emails to families regarding school events.
  • Any additional administrative duties necessary for school success
  • Assist with planning and implementing the yearly process of producing a master schedule for teachers and students, implementing advanced custom solutions for anticipating student course requests, allocating staffing resources, collecting student course requests, and generating teacher and student schedules.
  • Assist with developing implementing building policies such as cell phone and chromebook policies
  • Work to create, finalize, and support testing for MCAS, SAT, PSAT, MAP.

Qualifications-Required:

  • Education: Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in educational technology, information technology, computer science, or a related field.
  • Massachusetts license for Director/Supervisor
  • Experience:
    • Significant professional experience in a technology leadership role, with a preference for experience in K-12 education environments,
    • Proven track record of successfully managing technology projects and initiatives.
  • Skills and Competencies:
    • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex ideas clearly and persuasively.
    • Excellent leadership and team management skills, fostering a collaborative and inclusive work environment.
    • Deep understanding of the role of technology in education and its potential to transform teaching and learning.
    • Ability to manage budgets and resources effectively, ensuring the efficient use of technology investments.
    • Advanced proficiency with JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Google Docs, Google Sheets, and online databases.
  • Other:
    • Current authorization to work in the United States.

Qualifications - Preferred:

  1. Teaching experience in an urban, K-12 educational setting.
  2. Experience as a school administrator.
  3. Experience in Grant writing and fundraising.
  4. BPS values linguistic diversity and believes that candidates who speak another language bring added value to the classroom, school, and district culture and diversity. BPS is particularly interested in candidates who are fluent in one of BPS' official languages: Spanish, Creole (Cape Verdean), Creole (Haitian), Chinese, Vietnamese, Portuguese, & Somali.

title: Network Information Security Engineer/Analyst
description:
Network Information Security Engineer/Analyst
10-Month Contract Position - contract end date June 30th, 2027

Contract Length: 10 Months (Ending June 30th, 2027)

Starting: ASAP
Salary Lanes: H-J $85,600- $137,200 depending on experience
Contact: Ryan Neff
Phone: 385-579-7245


Purpose Statement
The Network Information Security Engineer/Analyst is responsible for protecting the district's network, servers, devices, technology services, systems, and data. This position supports the district's information security program through network security monitoring, threat hunting, vulnerability assessment, security hardening, incident investigation, security policy development, and implementation of security best practices.
The position works closely with Technology leadership, IT support staff, and district personnel to identify and mitigate security risks while maintaining the availability and reliability of district technology services.


Essential Functions

  • Monitors network, server, endpoint, email, and security systems to identify vulnerabilities, suspicious activity, and potential security threats.
  • Performs network threat hunting and security analysis to identify indicators of compromise, unusual activity, and potential attack paths.
  • Investigates, documents, and assists with the response and remediation of cybersecurity incidents and security breaches.
  • Conducts security assessments and testing of network infrastructure, servers, applications, endpoints, and other technology systems; analyzes findings and recommends appropriate remediation.
  • Performs security assessments and hardening of servers, switches, routers, wireless infrastructure, endpoints, and other network-connected devices.
  • Recommends security configurations, protocols, access controls, and security requirements for technology systems and solutions being evaluated or purchased by the district.
  • Advises Technology leadership on cybersecurity risks, security controls, network architecture, and best practices related to district systems and data.
  • Works with IT support staff to monitor enterprise systems, network traffic, and other threat vectors for vulnerabilities or potential compromise.
  • Supports the security of district user accounts, permissions, authentication systems, email, antivirus/endpoint protection, malware prevention, and other security services.
  • Maintains accurate security-related documentation and records, including access permissions, system configurations, security assessments, incident records, licenses, and audit documentation.
  • Develops and maintains security procedures, technical documentation, reports, recommendations, and other written materials.
  • Researches current and emerging cybersecurity technologies, threats, vulnerabilities, and industry best practices and makes recommendations based on district needs.
  • Provides security guidance, training, and technical assistance to IT staff and other district personnel.
  • Serves as an advisor to the Student Data Security Committee and provides guidance regarding the protection and appropriate handling of student and district data.
  • Responds to security-related requests and inquiries from district personnel and provides technical guidance, troubleshooting, and recommendations.
  • Participates in meetings, workshops, training, and professional development activities related to information technology and cybersecurity.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Relevant professional experience in network security, cybersecurity, network administration, systems administration, or a related field.
  • Working knowledge of network infrastructure, servers, endpoints, operating systems, firewalls, wireless networks, identity and access management, email security, and endpoint protection.
  • Knowledge of cybersecurity principles, vulnerability management, threat detection, threat hunting, incident response, and security hardening.
  • Ability to analyze security risks, troubleshoot complex technical issues, investigate incidents, and recommend effective solutions.
  • Ability to communicate technical and security concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritize multiple responsibilities, maintain accurate documentation, and exercise sound judgment when handling security-related matters.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and appropriately handle sensitive, student, and district information.


Certifications, Licenses & Clearances

  • CompTIA Security+, CISSP, or other relevant cybersecurity certification preferred.
  • Valid driver's license and evidence of insurability.
  • Successful completion of required pre-employment testing, fingerprinting, background clearance, and applicable security/CJIS training.
  • Commitment to ongoing professional development in cybersecurity and information technology.


Responsibility


This position works under limited supervision and is expected to exercise independent judgment when evaluating security risks, investigating incidents, and recommending solutions. The position may lead, guide, or coordinate the work of other IT personnel on security-related initiatives.
The position has the potential to significantly impact the security, availability, and integrity of district technology systems and data.


Work Environment
The position is performed primarily in a technology and office environment. Job functions may require occasional lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling, stooping, kneeling, crouching, crawling, and significant fine-finger dexterity.
The position generally requires a combination of sitting, standing, and walking and is performed in a generally hazard-free and clean environment.

Experience
Job-related experience in information security, network security, systems administration, network administration, cybersecurity, or a closely related field is required.

Education
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, or a related field preferred.
Equivalent combinations of education, training, and relevant professional experience may be considered.
Required Testing, Certifications, and Licenses

  • Pre-employment proficiency testing as required by the district.
  • CompTIA Security+ or equivalent cybersecurity certification preferred.
  • CISSP or other advanced cybersecurity certification preferred.
  • Valid driver's license and evidence of insurability.



Continuing Education / Training / Clearances

  • Ongoing professional development in cybersecurity, network security, data protection, and related technologies.
  • Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) training, when applicable.
  • Fingerprint and background clearance as required by the district.
