title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
description:
Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent, On-Site
Location: Suite 865, 401 – 9th Avenue SW, Calgary, AB T2P 3Z5

About Arcobi

Arcobi (formerly Arcus Power) is at the forefront of the global shift towards electrification and low-carbon power systems. Our AI-driven Energy Cost Management platform is revolutionizing power management by enabling users to optimize operations based on electricity prices, peak demand periods, and market opportunities. Originally a tech startup in Calgary, Arcobi is now expanding globally.

The Team

Our diverse team of data scientists, software developers, electrical engineers, and market analysts is committed to creating intelligent models that support efficient energy resource consumption. Arcobi fosters a collaborative, innovation-driven, and dynamic culture, where everyone's input is valued.

Your Role

We're seeking an exceptional Senior Full Stack Engineer who combines technical excellence with a passion for crafting beautiful, intuitive user experiences. You'll build enterprise-grade applications where visual appeal meets best-in-class functionality—creating interfaces that energy market professionals and Fortune 500 companies rely on to optimize electricity usage and integrate renewable energy.

This role is for someone who believes that enterprise software doesn't have to be ugly. Working closely with our product team, you'll architect modern React applications with TypeScript that are as delightful to use as they are technically robust. If you obsess over details—from component architecture to the perfect button hover state—and want your work to accelerate the clean energy transition, this is your opportunity.

What You'll Build

Modern Frontend Applications

  • Build responsive, pixel-perfect React applications using TypeScript
  • Create reusable component libraries and design systems (Storybook)
  • Implement sophisticated data visualizations using D3, Visx, or Recharts
  • Design and maintain a cohesive design system with careful attention to typography, color, and spacing
  • Partner with product and design to deliver production-ready features
  • Ensure exceptional performance and accessibility across all interfaces
  • Design and implement RESTful APIs using FastAPI and Python
  • Build microservices architectures for real-time data delivery
  • Implement robust authentication, authorization, and security practices
  • Create background jobs and data processing pipelines
  • Ensure system reliability through testing and monitoring

End-to-End Ownership

  • Ship features from concept to production, across frontend and backend
  • Collaborate with designers to refine user flows and interactions
  • Integrate ML models and analytics into user-facing features
  • Participate in code reviews and mentor other engineers
  • Contribute to architectural decisions and technical direction

Your Qualifications

Must Have:

  • 5-7+ years of full stack experience building production applications
  • Expert-level proficiency in React and TypeScript
  • Strong backend experience with Python and FastAPI
  • Proven track record building polished, user-friendly UIs
  • Experience with component libraries and design systems
  • Proficiency with state management (Redux, Tanstack, Context API, Zustand)
  • Experience with SQL and NoSQL databases
  • Strong grasp of RESTful API design and microservices architecture
  • Familiarity with modern build tools (Vite, Webpack, etc.)
  • Experience with Git workflows and CI/CD pipelines

Highly Valued:

  • Experience with data visualization libraries (D3.js, Visx, Recharts, Plotly)
  • Proficiency with Storybook for component development and documentation
  • Background in building enterprise SaaS applications
  • Experience with Figma and translating designs to production-quality code
  • Experience with Mantine component library and styling approaches
  • Familiarity with testing frameworks (Vitest, React Testing Library, Playwright)
  • Knowledge of Python ecosystem (Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, async patterns)
  • Understanding of time-series data and real-time analytics interfaces
  • Background in performance optimization and lighthouse scores
  • Experience with design tokens and theming systems
  • Contributions to open-source projects or component libraries
  • Craft & Polish: You sweat the details and deliver pixel-perfect implementations
  • User Empathy: You think deeply about user workflows an UX impact
  • Systems Thinking: You design components and APIs for reusability and maintainability
  • Ownership: You ship complete features, deliver customer value, and stand by the reliability and available of your work, not just crunch through tickets
  • Collaboration: You work effectively with designers, product managers, and engineers
  • Pragmatism: You balance perfection with shipping and know when "good enough" is right
  • Communication: You articulate technical decisions and can advocate for users

What Arcobi Can Offer

  • Comprehensive health and wellness benefits
  • RRSP matching program
  • Three (3) weeks of annual paid vacation
  • Opportunities for professional growth in AI, MLOps, and energy technology

Join Us

This is your chance to build beautiful, powerful applications that drive the energy transition. If you're a craftsperson who believes enterprise software can be delightful, if you care deeply about both code quality and user experience, and if you want your work to have real climate impact—we want to build this with you.

At Arcobi, every component, every interaction, every API moves us closer to a decarbonized future.

title: Data Center Technician
description:
Join our dynamic AWS team and become a critical guardian of global cloud infrastructure! You'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of the world's most innovative technology platform, ensuring seamless data center operations that power millions of businesses and services worldwide.

Data Center Technicians should be willing to work both independently and with a team. Work prioritization, organizational skills, effective communication, and the ability to react quickly are critical to success. In addition to hardware and network repair, candidates will install equipment, create documentation, innovate solutions, and fix problems within the data center space. This team works in an environment that operates 24/7. Traveling within and outside of the regional work area is required.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
- Performing server rack installations, hardware break-fix on various components, troubleshooting network issues, and responding to operational incidents that impact service availability, escalating to senior technicians and management as needed/required
- Serving as a primary contact point for both internal and external stakeholders, including engineers, software developers, vendors, and contractors
- Performing on-call duties and participating in scheduled maintenance and change management activities
- Contributing to documentation and process improvement initiatives based on your analysis of operational issues
- Helping to train and onboard new team members

Physical requirements:

- Regularly lift and/or move up to 40 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 41+ pounds
- Working in cramped and/or elevated locations
- Bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching
- Standing and walking for up to 8+ hours a day
- Ascending and descending ladders, stairs, and gangways safely and without limitation
- Work in a noisy environment
- Work shifts longer than 8 hours to support 24/7 operations (covering both night and day shifts).

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:

- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

A day in the life
As a Data Center Technician professional, you have industry-leading technical abilities and demonstrate a breadth of knowledge while you:
-Take ownership of technical issues brought by their customer base, engaging other teams when needed to drive resolution
-Solve problems at their root and step back to understand the broader context
-Maintain service level agreements through the implementation of proactive issue detection and reporting

You will be required to work shift work that will include days/nights/weekends/holidays. Traveling within and outside of the regional work area is required. You will be responsible for having a reliable personal vehicle and valid driver's license to travel within the regional work area, as company transportation will not be provided.

A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Program Manager at Google, you’ll lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish — working with stakeholders to plan requirements, manage project schedules, identify risks, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. Your projects will often span offices, time zones, and hemispheres. It's your job to coordinate the players and keep them up to date on progress and deadlines.

As a Program Manager, Contract Governance and Execution, you will be responsible for driving the strategic execution, governance, and operationalization of long-term supply chain commitments across a complex, global supplier ecosystem. In this role, you will work closely with cross-functional partners, including Sourcing, Engineering, Finance, and Legal, to mitigate supply chain risks, secure critical component capacity, and ensure end-to-end alignment from raw materials to finished systems.

In this role, you will translate executive supply chain strategy into structured execution roadmaps, manage portfolio commitments, and build scalable governance frameworks for proactive risk management.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving team behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

title: Senior Full Stack Developer

At Lexful, we aren’t just building a tool; we are redefining how the Managed Service Provider (MSP) industry operates. For decades, IT documentation has been static, fragmented, and manual—becoming an operational risk rather than an asset. We are changing that.

As the creators of the industry’s first AI-native IT documentation platform, Lexful turns "stale" data into real-time contextual intelligence. Our mission is to move MSPs away from legacy storage and toward a modern "KnowledgeOps" ecosystem. Joining Lexful means joining a team of industry veterans and innovators backed by Top Down Ventures. East Side House cares for the individuals, families, and communities we serve by expanding opportunities to live more fulfilling lives through education, career, and supportive services.

Summary/ Objective

East Side House (ESH) is a community resource in the Bronx and Northern Manhattan. We believe education is the key that enables all people to create economic and civic opportunities for themselves, their families, and their community. ESH’s Learning to Work Program aligns with our mission by providing high quality programs and services within community centers and school partnerships.

Reporting to the Program Director, the Student Advisor is responsible to provide support over a wide variety of areas including college and career readiness, academic progress monitoring, day-to-day student issues, social-emotional and personal development. Student Advisors will follow the Primary Person Model where they will be the first point of contact for students, parents, and staff members. It is expected to work collaboratively with our partner school faculty and staff to ensure each student’s academic success.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Program Director, the Student Advisor, will be responsible for but not limited to the following:

Cohort Management & Support Services:

  • Primary person advisor for assigned cohort of students
  • Conduct regular one on one sessions with students, at least twice a month
  • Support students to create SMART goals and to work toward implementation
  • Partner with the students, family and/or caring adults, school, and Community School teams to develop an individualized plan for each student
  • Conduct and support student advisory groups in collaboration with school faculty
  • Provide updates on progress of students to Leadership and key school staff as needed; participate in weekly case conferencing with school and CS staff
  • Providing crises intervention and counseling for students as needed, under supervision of Program Director.
  • Document all interactions with students on assigned data systems as required.
  • Providing attendance outreach through phone calls, texts through agency telephone, letters, remotely, and/or home visits
  • Organize and implement special activities/events that meet the recreational, cultural, social needs of the school community.
  • Support new student admission process (outreach, open houses/intake interviews, new student orientation, parent orientations)
  • Partner with students to identify opportunities and referrals based on need and aspiration of student and family.
  • With Program Director, create best practices for cohort management and support services to ensure high quality and demographic appropriate.

College & Career Readiness and post-graduation planning: (if applicable for Middle School/High School)

Assist students to define career interests for exploration through internships, job shadowing and other career exploration activities.

  • Partner with ESH Workforce Development and College Access Counselor and Internship Coordinator for postsecondary planning.
  • Educate students about colleges, the college admissions process, FAFSA, trends, procedures, and testing; advise students as they go through the process and help them aspire realistically and choose wisely.
  • Track students’ academic progress using report cards, progress reports other resources provided by the school and program.
  • Help students identify their strengths and challenges in order to develop SMART goals and take advantage of opportunities for ongoing growth
  • Support students to develop employability skills (Resume Building, Cover letter writing, Mock Interviews, completion of job/internship application, job shadowing opportunities) through individual and group activities.

Family & Community Engagement:

  • As an extension of our Primary Person Model (PP) model: build strong relationships with families to provide support, resources, and opportunities for growth.
  • Work to implement family structures with the school: regular parent workshops tailored to parent needs, volunteer opportunities, and formal connection to community resources (alignment with the Dual Capacity-Building Framework for Family-School Partnerships.
  • Work with families in need of additional supports on an individual basis; access to ESH’s internal Social Services Department which offers an array of supportive services including individual and family counseling, entitlement screening, and referral services as well as school-based adult education opportunities such as work training programs, high school equivalency courses, and English language classes.


Collaborative Practices:

title: Private Pricing Programs & Exp, GDSP 3PX
description:
Are you a detail-oriented problem solver who thrives at the intersection of contracts, customer experience, and operational scale? Someone who can manage complexity across multiple concurrent deal cycles while identifying opportunities to streamline, automate, and improve?

We're looking for a [Senior] Private Pricing Contract Experience Manager to join the AWS Private Pricing Programs & Experiences (3PX) organization. PACE supports the end-to-end private pricing deal cycle, from intake through contracting, for AWS's customers. Our mission is to accelerate deal velocity, maintain the highest quality bar, and continuously improve the seller and customer experience at scale.

In this senior role, you'll own strategic initiatives with significant bottom-line impact, define and execute strategy with limited oversight, and influence cross-functional partners across Legal, Sales, Finance, and Product to remove systemic friction from the contracting process. You'll lead and orchestrate mechanisms across teams, communicate with direct and indirect stakeholders up to the VP level, and create scalable, long-term solutions that raise the bar for the entire organization.

The ideal candidate combines operational rigor with a builder's mindset. You manage ambiguity with confidence; whether the approach is defined or you must determine it yourself. You shift fluidly between tactical execution and strategic thinking, and are energized by finding scalable solutions to manual, repetitive work. You proactively leverage tools, especially including AI and automation, to continuously improve how work gets done, not just to complete today's task but to make tomorrow's easier. You communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders, use data to inform every decision, and are known as a subject matter expert your peers and cross-functional partners seek out for guidance.

Key job responsibilities
- Manage multiple, complex private pricing contracting cycles simultaneously from intake and triage through execution, exercising high judgment and autonomous decision-making in ambiguous situations to drive deal velocity while maintaining the highest quality standards
- Own the contract process end-to-end, coordinating across internal teams (Legal, Sales, Finance) and external stakeholders to drive requests to closure; identify tradeoffs and negotiate actionable solutions
- Deliver results through scalable mechanisms — identify bottlenecks, track key input/output metrics, and generate actionable recommendations that improve team efficiency and customer experience
- Leverage automation opportunities and emerging tools (including AI-assisted solutions) to reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and scale self-service capabilities
- Create or optimize procedures to improve team, initiative, or mechanism efficiency; identify better practices for tracking and execution and make it easier for others to follow
- Lead cross-functional projects that drive operational improvements, communicating results and financial impact to direct stakeholders and contributing to business mechanisms (QBR, MBR, WBR)
- Define and own the strategic roadmap for your program area — determining goals, setting priorities, establishing best practices, and measuring success at the team and org level with limited oversight
- Lead and orchestrate initiatives that span multiple teams or geographies, driving adoption of best practices for operational excellence and accelerating progress through cross-team mechanisms
- Influence senior leadership (Director level and above) with data-driven recommendations; represent the team in cross-organizational forums and contribute to strategic documents (OP1, QBR, GTM)
- Mentor and develop team members; invest in educating and training critical personnel on mechanisms and solutions; raise the performance bar through knowledge sharing
- Identify systemic gaps and mitigate long-term risks before they appear on the roadmap; drive resolution through partnership with engineering, product, and legal teams

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

title: Core Data and Compliance Specialist
description:
Qualifications:

Required

  • Bachelors degree or equivalent.
  • Demonstrated experience working with complex databases, student information systems, data reporting, or comparable information-management systems.
  • Advanced computer skills and demonstrated ability to learn complex information systems.
  • Strong proficiency with spreadsheets, data analysis, reporting tools, and database applications.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze large amounts of information and identify errors, inconsistencies, and trends.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and reporting deadlines simultaneously.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality when working with student and employee information.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively.

Preferred

  • Associate's or bachelor's degree in information systems, data management, business, education, public administration, or a related field.
  • Three or more years of experience working in a Missouri public school district.
  • Experience with Missouri Core Data and MOSIS reporting.
  • Experience with student information systems.
  • Knowledge of Missouri DESE reporting requirements.
  • Experience conducting data audits and resolving data-quality issues.
  • Experience providing technical training or professional development to adult learners.
  • Knowledge of Missouri school accountability and reporting requirements, including MSIP and APR.
  • Experience working with student enrollment, attendance, scheduling, assessment, personnel, or program data.

Fair Labor Standards Act Status: Exempt

Reports to:

Deputy Superintendent responsible for District data, accountability, or compliance

Job Goal:

The Core Data & Compliance Specialist is responsible for coordinating, validating, maintaining, and submitting accurate district data required by the Missouri Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE) and other state and federal agencies.

The position serves as a district expert and primary point of contact for Missouri Core Data and the Missouri Student Information System (MOSIS) and works collaboratively with district administrators, Human Resources, Finance, Special Education, Technology, Student Services, Curriculum and Instruction, school administrators, registrars, secretaries, and other staff responsible for generating, maintaining, or reporting district data.

The Core Data & Compliance Specialist helps ensure that district information is accurate, complete, timely, secure, and compliant with applicable state and federal requirements. The position provides leadership in data validation, reporting procedures, staff training, troubleshooting, documentation, and continuous improvement of district data-management processes.

Performance Responsibilities:

Core Data/MOSIS Reporting and Compliance

  1. Serve as the District's primary coordinator and subject-matter resource for Missouri Core Data and MOSIS reporting.
  2. Coordinate the collection, review, validation, correction, submission, and certification of information required by DESE through Core Data, MOSIS, and related state reporting systems.
  3. Coordinate all required DESE reporting cycles and ensure submissions are completed accurately and within established deadlines.
  4. Maintain a comprehensive annual calendar of Core Data, MOSIS, state, and federal reporting requirements and communicate deadlines to appropriate district personnel.
  5. Monitor changes to DESE reporting requirements, data definitions, file layouts, business rules, code sets, procedures, and timelines and communicate relevant changes to district personnel.
  6. Review state submissions for errors, warnings, inconsistencies, and anomalies and coordinate corrections with the appropriate district departments and schools.
  7. Complete required certification processes and maintain appropriate documentation supporting district data submissions.
  8. Serve as a liaison between the District and DESE regarding Core Data/MOSIS questions, reporting requirements, corrections, and data-quality issues.
  9. Attend appropriate DESE meetings, webinars, conferences, and training sessions related to Core Data, MOSIS, accountability, student information, and state reporting.

Data Quality, Validation, and Auditing

  1. Develop and maintain processes for regularly auditing district data to identify errors, missing information, inconsistencies, duplicate records, and other data-quality concerns.
  2. Conduct periodic data-quality reviews throughout the school year rather than relying solely upon validation immediately before state reporting deadlines.
  3. Compare information across district systems and departments to identify discrepancies and ensure consistent reporting.
  4. Work collaboratively with Human Resources, Finance, Special Education, Technology, Student Services, Curriculum and Instruction, Transportation, Food Services, and school personnel to resolve data discrepancies.
  5. Develop procedures for documenting data corrections and maintaining appropriate records of significant changes.
  6. Identify trends or recurring data-entry problems and recommend procedural, system, or training improvements.
  7. Assist administrators in understanding how data accuracy and reporting practices may affect district accountability, funding, compliance, enrollment, attendance, and other district operations.
  8. Alert appropriate administrators when data findings could negatively affect district compliance, accountability measures, funding, or reporting accuracy.

Student Information System Support

  1. Work collaboratively with Technology and other appropriate personnel to maintain the accuracy and integrity of information contained within the District's student information system.
  2. Assist in establishing and maintaining district standards for student demographic, enrollment, attendance, scheduling, course, program, and other information required for state reporting.
  3. Coordinate with school registrars, secretaries, counselors, administrators, and other staff to ensure accurate and consistent data-entry practices.
  4. Assist with the establishment and maintenance of school-year and summer-school data structures necessary for state reporting.
  5. Coordinate processes related to MOSIS student identification numbers and resolve student identification issues.
  6. Assist with state assessment pre-code files and other required student-data extracts.
  7. Assist district departments and schools in developing reports and extracting information needed for operational, compliance, and decision-making purposes.

Training and Technical Assistance

  1. Develop and provide annual and ongoing training for administrators, secretaries, registrars, counselors, and other personnel responsible for entering or maintaining information used in Core Data/MOSIS submissions.
  2. Develop written procedures, manuals, calendars, checklists, reference materials, and other resources to promote consistent district-wide data practices.
  3. Provide individualized technical assistance to district and building personnel regarding Core Data, MOSIS, student information, and reporting procedures.
  4. Communicate changes in state reporting requirements and district procedures in a clear and timely manner.
  5. Provide additional training when audits or data reviews identify recurring errors or areas of concern.
  6. Cross-train designated district personnel on critical Core Data/MOSIS functions to support continuity of operations.

State and Federal Reporting

  1. Assist with or coordinate additional state and federal data-reporting requirements assigned to the position.
  2. Coordinate the collection and validation of information required for the Civil Rights Data Collection (CRDC), as assigned.
  3. Assist with state assessment reporting, enrollment reporting, attendance reporting, summer-school reporting, and other required submissions.
  4. Collaborate with appropriate departments to ensure consistency between Core Data/MOSIS submissions and other state and federal reports.
  5. Maintain documentation necessary to support district responses to state or federal data audits.

Data Governance and Continuous Improvement

  1. Assist district leadership in establishing and maintaining district-wide data definitions, procedures, standards, and responsibilities.
  2. Recommend improvements to data-collection and reporting processes to increase accuracy, efficiency, consistency, and accountability.
  3. Collaborate with Technology and district leadership when implementing or modifying systems that generate information used for state reporting.
  4. Assist in evaluating the impact of software changes, system integrations, and new district procedures on Core Data/MOSIS reporting.
  5. Maintain confidentiality and security of student, employee, and district information in accordance with FERPA, district policy, and applicable state and federal requirements.
  6. Promote a culture in which accurate data is viewed as a shared district responsibility and an essential component of effective decision-making.

Collaboration and Communication

  1. Establish effective working relationships with administrators, school personnel, district departments, DESE representatives, software vendors, and other external partners.
  2. Communicate reporting requirements, deadlines, identified errors, and corrective actions clearly and professionally.
  3. Facilitate meetings of district personnel responsible for Core Data/MOSIS information when necessary.
  4. Provide district leadership with periodic updates regarding reporting status, data-quality concerns, upcoming deadlines, and areas requiring administrative attention.
  5. Respond promptly and professionally to requests for data and technical assistance.
  6. Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

The successful candidate should demonstrate the ability to:

  • Interpret and apply detailed state reporting requirements.
  • Analyze data for accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
  • Troubleshoot complex data problems and identify their underlying causes.
  • Establish systems and procedures that reduce reporting errors.
  • Communicate technical information to employees with varying levels of technical expertise.
  • Develop productive working relationships across multiple district departments.
  • Manage confidential information appropriately.
  • Work accurately under strict deadlines.
  • Prioritize multiple competing responsibilities.
  • Exercise sound judgment and independent problem-solving.
  • Provide exceptional internal customer service.
  • Adapt to changing state requirements, technologies, and district needs.
  • Translate data requirements into understandable procedures for school and district personnel.

Work Environment

The position is primarily performed in a professional office and school environment. The employee may be required to travel between district facilities and attend meetings or training outside the District. The position may require additional time during critical state reporting periods to ensure required submissions are completed accurately and on time.

Performance Indicators

Successful performance in this position includes:

  • Core Data/MOSIS submissions completed accurately and by required deadlines.
  • Reduction in state reporting errors and warnings.
  • Timely identification and correction of data-quality concerns.
  • Consistent district-wide data-entry and reporting procedures.
  • Effective training and support for building and department personnel.
  • Accurate documentation of reporting processes and procedures.
  • Positive working relationships with district departments, schools, and DESE.
  • Effective communication of deadlines and compliance requirements.
  • Continuous improvement in the accuracy, reliability, and usefulness of district data.

Terms of Employment

12-month position; salary and work calendar established by the Board of Education.

Evaluation

Performance will be evaluated annually in accordance with Independence School District policies and procedures.

title: Billing Specialist III
description:
Cedar Rapids, Iowa, United States of America

Extraordinary Care. Extraordinary Careers.

With one of the nation’s largest, most innovative long-term care pharmacy services providers, there is no limit to the growth of your career.

Right Dose Pharmacy, a member of the Guardian family of pharmacies, has an exciting opportunity for you to join our rapidly growing team in Cedar Rapids, Iowa.

Why Right Dose Pharmacy? We’re reimagining medication management and transforming care.

Who We Are and What We’re About:

Our core focus is delivering customized medication management solutions to support healthcare organizations serving seniors and individuals with complex care needs. With our comprehensive suite of tech-enabled pharmacy services and a dedicated team of professionals committed to enriching the lives of those we serve, we are redefining how pharmacy care is delivered.

We offer an opportunity to learn and grow your career in a fast-paced, diverse, and inclusive environment. If you are looking for a challenging, team-oriented environment in which you can put your expertise to work, then this is the place for you.

Responsible for processing customer bills and insurance claims in an accurate and timely manner. This includes assisting with all daily and month-end billing functions, procedures and reporting. Provides excellent customer service to patients, caregivers, medical providers and insurance carriers. The Billing Specialist III serves as a subject matter expert and departmental resource.

ATTRIBUTES REQUIRED:

  • Work Ethic/Integrity – must possess intrinsic drive to excel coupled with values in line with company philosophy.
  • Relational – ability to build relationships with business unit management and become “trusted advisor.”
  • Strategy and Planning – ability to think ahead, plan and manage time efficiently.
  • Problem Solving – ability to analyze causes and solve problems at functional level.
  • Team Oriented – ability to work effectively and collaboratively with all team members.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS (include the following):

  • Research and establish patient eligibility coverage with insurance providers including private individuals and/or government entities. Reverify benefit coverage criteria as needed for claims follow up. Accurately enters and/or updates patient/insurance information into billing system.
  • Maintain and continually audit patient files and corresponding documentation necessary to defend third party audits and ensure payer and company compliance. Accurately enter patient information into the pharmacy system.
  • Provide assistance and timely response to all billing customer inquiries via phone or electronic communications. Using advanced knowledge, independently, troubleshoot, research and resolve patient billing issues regarding insurance eligibility, coverage, and related benefits. Uses advanced knowledge to independently resolve customer service issues that require judgement and critical thinking.
  • Provide guidance and support to resident or responsible party by running Medicare plan comparisons during open enrollment and special enrollment periods. Proactively review patient profiles, drug regimens and insurance coverage to evaluate options to save resident money.
  • Responsible for completion of daily census, admit, discharge, and room changes for the facilities assigned.
  • Process patient payments, returns, and credits. Transmit individual credit card payments as needed.
  • May pursue payment from delinquent accounts and make payment arrangements.
  • Research, identify and organize requested audit documentation in timely manner.
  • Perform prescription claims adjudication including communication with insurance companies regarding rejected claims, eligibility, prior authorizations or other issues as needed. Make corrections as needed and rebill claims as necessary.
  • Through prior experience and cross training, demonstrate advanced knowledge and understanding in pharmacy facility billing requirements (Medicare, Medicaid, Prescription Drug Plans (PDPs) and Third-Party Insurances) and working/functional knowledge of other pharmacy departmental functions
  • Serve as subject matter expert and departmental resource in Pharmacy information systems and workflow. This includes using pharmacy systems to process prior authorizations, resolve rejections, produce various reports as necessary, and complete billing functions in a timely manner and with a high degree of accuracy.
  • Consistently exceed pharmacy's established accuracy and productivity levels.
  • Follow all applicable government regulations including HIPAA.
  • Work as a collaborative team member to meet the service goals of the pharmacy.
  • Other essential functions and duties may be assigned as needed.

EDUCATION AND/OR CERTIFICATIONS:

  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • Pharmacy Technician license/certification/registration per state requirements; National Certification preferred (PTCB) may be required (pharmacy specific).

SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years related experience including a minimum of 1 year at Billing Specialist II level.
  • Advanced computer skills; pharmacy information system experience required
  • Ability to work independently and deliver to deadlines.
  • Great attention to detail and accuracy
  • Ability to excel in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment working on multiple tasks simultaneously, while adhering to strict deadlines
  • Quality minded; motivated to seek out errors and inquire about inaccuracies.

WORK ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the job.

  • The noise level in the work environment is usually low to moderate.
  • Due to the collaborative nature of the business and the need to service customers, the employee must be able to interact effectively with others in an office environment, manage conflict, and handle stressful situations and deadlines.
  • Requires desk work in office environment.
  • Ability to work flexible hours.

What We Offer:

Guardian provides employees with a comprehensive Total Rewards package, supporting our core value of, “Treat others as you would like to be treated.”

Compensation & Financial

  • Competitive pay
  • 401(k) with company match

Family, Health & Insurance Benefits (Full-Time employees working 30+ hours/week only)

  • Medical, Dental and Vision
  • Health Savings Accounts and Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Company-paid Basic Life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment
  • Company-paid Long-Term Disability and optional Short-Term Disability
  • Voluntary Employee and Dependent Life, Accident and Critical Illness
  • Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts

Wellbeing

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Guardian Angels (Employee assistance fund)

Time Off

  • Paid holidays and sick days
  • Generous vacation benefits based on years of service

The Guardian Difference

Our clients require pharmacy services that aren’t “cookie cutter.” That’s why every Guardian pharmacy is locally operated and empowered with the autonomy to tailor their business to meet their clients’ needs.

Our corporate support offices, based in Atlanta, Ga., provide services such as human resources, business intelligence, legal, and marketing to promote the success of each Guardian location.

Regardless of your role at Guardian, your voice and talents matter. Because healthcare is an ever-changing industry, we encourage innovative thinking, intellectual curiosity, and diverse viewpoints to ensure we stay competitive in today’s dynamic business environment.

At Guardian, we are dedicated to fostering and advancing a diverse and inclusive workforce.

Join us to discover what your best work truly looks like.

description:

Position Title: IT Support Specialist & Hardware Coordinator

Germantown Academy is an independent, coeducational, college preparatory day school located on a beautiful 126-acre campus in the Fort Washington suburbs near Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The school serves more than 1,200 students in grades PK-12. The position troubleshoots, researches, documents, tracks, monitors, and resolves technical problems in a timely and accurate manner. In addition, the Hardware Coordinator manages the lifecycle of GA technology hardware, including asset tracking, inventory, repair and replacement coordination, device deployment, and the ordering of technology-related supplies and consumables.

title: Transportation Representative, IB Sked
description:
Over the past 20 years, Amazon has reinvented on behalf of customers and has become the largest internet retailer and marketplace in the world. NOC (Network Operation Center) is the central command and control center for ‘Transportation Execution’ across the Amazon's transportation network. It ensures hassle free, timely pick-up and delivery of freight from vendors to Amazon fulfillment centers (FC) and from Amazon FCs to carrier hubs. In case of any exceptions, NOC steps in to resolve the issue and keeps all the stakeholders informed on the proceedings. Along with this tactical problem solving, NOC is also charged with understanding trends in network exceptions and then automating processes or proposing process changes to streamline operations. This second aspect involves network monitoring and significant analysis of network data. Overall, NOC plays a critical role in ensuring the smooth functioning of Amazon transportation and thereby has a direct impact on Amazon’s ability to serve its customers on time. Overall, NOC plays a critical role in ensuring the smooth functioning of Amazon transportation and thereby has a direct impact on Amazon’s ability to serve its customers on time.

Within NOC’s umbrella, resides a specific arm which manages Inbound scheduling, MFI (Missing from inbound), 3P pickups, Vendor returns and invoice scanning operations across India (IN), AMET (South Africa, UAE, KSA, EGY and Turkey), Australia (AU), Japan (JP), Singapore (SG), Brazil (BR) and Mexico (MX).

Purview of a Transportation Specialist
A Transportation Specialist inbound at NOC facilitates flow of information between different stakeholders (Vendors/Sellers/Inbound Supply chain/category managers/Fulfillment centers) and resolves any potential issues that impacts vendor/seller experience and business continuity. Transportation Specialist at NOC works on Inbound operations which deals with appointment scheduling at Fulfillment centers requested by Vendors/sellers/carriers, ensuring that the truck reaches the FC for shipment delivery from vendors/sellers as per schedule. Transportation specialist on Inbound addresses any potential issues occurring during the lifecycle of freight placement and freight unloading at FCs.
A Transportation Specialist provides timely resolution to the issue hand in hand by researching and querying internal tools and by taking real-time decisions. An ideal candidate should be able to understand the requirements/be able to analyze data and notice trends and be able to drive vendor/seller Experience without compromising on time. The candidate should have a basic understanding of Logistics and should be able to communicate clearly in the written and oral form. Transportation Specialist should be able to ideate process improvements and should have the zeal to drive them to conclusion.


Key job responsibilities
A Transportation Representative at NOC facilitates flow of information between different stakeholders (Warehouses/Category teams/Carriers) and resolves any potential issues that impact customer experience and business continuity. Transportation Representative at NOC works across Inbound operations.
Inbound Operations deals with Vendor/Carrier/FC relationship, to plan the freight for delivery in warehouses as per given appointment time. Transportation Representative on Inbound addresses any potential issues occurring during the lifecycle of forecasting to actual delivery of the appointment.

Key job responsibilities
A Transportation Representative provides timely resolution to the issue in hand by researching and querying internal tools and by taking real-time decisions. An ideal candidate should be able to understand the requirements/be able to analyze data and notice trends and be able to drive Customer Experience without compromising on time. The candidate should have the basic understanding of Logistics and should be able to communicate clearly in the written and verbal form.

About the team
NOC Inbound Team manages and owns the end to end execution of vendor’s/seller’s shipment inbounding process. This includes Appointment scheduling & prioritization, Appt sidelining and rescue, Appt modification etc and other related process/tasks across IN and ECCF countries.

title: Grounds and Maintenance Staff (Seasonal)
description:
GENERAL SUMMARY

Lincoln Park Zoo inspires communities to create environments where wildlife will thrive in our urbanizing world. The zoo is a leader in local and global conservation, animal care and welfare, learning, and science. A historic Chicago landmark founded in 1868, the not-for-profit Lincoln Park Zoo, is a privately-managed, member-supported organization and is free and open 365 days a year. Visit us at lpzoo.org.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

This person contributes to the success of the Lincoln Park Zoological Society by performing routine duties and functions in order to meet the cleanliness, beauty and aesthetic requirements of the park to help provide an exceptional guest experience. They will have a strong focus on safety which will be utilized while they operate a variety of equipment such as leaf blowers, power washers, and other equipment as required. This person will be expected to complete tasks as assigned by Management while also being responsible for the following tasks:

  • Perform general custodial cleaning duties as directed by supervisor, including sweeping, mopping, vacuuming, scrubbing, dusting, waste collection, rug cleaning, paper picking, laundering, etc. Assigned work areas may include all sections of the park: restrooms, restaurants, lunchrooms, offices, laboratories and hospital, animal buildings, conference rooms and meeting areas, security, etc.
  • Properly operate and maintain assigned equipment including mops and buckets, brooms and other hand tools, vacuum cleaners, scrubbers, rug cleaning equipment, laundry equipment, and other equipment as required, reporting needed repairs to direct lead or supervisor.
  • Observes appearances and conditions of premises; reports needed repairs, safety hazards, or conditions requiring outside vendor services
  • Gathers and disposes of waste materials by hand or with use of powered equipment
  • Performs general and heavy cleaning duties with the appropriate approved chemicals. Properly cleans and / or disposes of bio-hazardous waste. Wears the appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) as needed
  • Follows specific open/closing procedures for buildings, ensuring that buildings are properly secured before and after shift.
  • Scrubs, strips, sanitizes, waxes, and buffs floors using powered machines equipped with rotating brushes
  • Polishes furniture, metal work, and chrome using appropriate cleaning and polishing compounds
  • Maintains an inventory of cleaning and toiletry supplies, communicating needs to lead and/or supervisor
  • Washes walls, ceilings, woodwork, windows, mirrors, and fixtures using both step and folding ladders
  • Cleans grounds and parking lots of litter, weeds, glass, or other debris
  • Loads and unloads supplies, and moves heavy furniture and equipment using dollies, handcarts, or power equipment
  • Uses equipment to shampoos carpets, floor mats and other flooring materials
  • Replaces toilet paper and paper towels and soap
  • Perform basic maintenance on toilet paper dispensers, paper towel dispensers, and soap dispensers
  • Perform specific specialty cleaning projects throughout zoo

title: Network Administrator, VoIP
description:
PROBATIONARY EMPLOYEES ARE NOT ELIGIBLE TO APPLY FOR VACANCIES OR PROMOTIONS DURING THEIR PROBATIONARY PERIOD

All education provided on your application must be supported by attaching a scanned copy of your high school diploma, transcription or college/university transcript.

Work Year Calendar and Hours

  • 12-month position (260 days / year), 8 hours per day
  • Daily work hours: TBD


For more information about employee benefits please go to:

Salary

  • Technology Salary Grade T21: $47.46 per hour; starting


Under the Fair Labor and Standards Act this position is non-exempt from overtime. Actual salary placement will be in accordance with the salary procedures of the Frederick County Public School System. Please see linked salary scale for the full range.

Role

The Network Administrator provides design expertise and technical direction for the IP telephony (LAN/MAN/WAN) systems infrastructure including requirements, planning and implementation of communications services for buildings and systems. This position also performs network related duties with a primary focus on VOIP and network administration.

Essential Functions

Reporting directly to the Supervisor of Network Infrastructure and Security, the Network Administrator (VoIP) performs the following duties:

  • Manage the day-to-day operations of network infrastructure including VOIP, unified communications and telecommunications infrastructure including servers. This includes scheduling upgrades and maintenance that minimally impact core business and instructional functions. Performs off hour upgrades, installing patches, service packs, maintenance releases, troubleshooting, etc.
  • Installs, configures, maintains and troubleshoots all network resources including telecommunications and network infrastructure, switches, IP protocols and connectivity, network sub-systems, and network communication links.
  • Implements and maintains network security as mandated by state, county, and internal requirements. Performs routine network audits and vulnerability assessments, verifies network security compliance as directed by management.
  • Performs multi-tiered incident, change management, problem resolution, and end-user support.
  • Monitors faults, performance, and capacity issues; prepares remediation reports and documentation.
  • Proactively researches, analyzes, identifies and resolves trends of utilization or errors and implement appropriate performance tuning and troubleshooting techniques.
  • Continuously identifies opportunities for process and quality improvement and implements applicable technologies and/or process changes.
  • Implement and configure telephony and network highly available infrastructure including design and test of fail-over services, fault tolerance, disaster recovery, load balancing, etc.
  • Implement and configure systems management and proactive monitoring tools; troubleshoots and resolves identified telecommunication and network issues.
  • Implement and oversee telecommunications backup systems. Protect all systems and end user data: schedule and maintain onsite and offsite backups, review backup logs, develop and maintain backup procedures, restore backups and configurations, document recovery plans and implement new backup technologies.
  • Document all network administration processes and installation procedures.
  • Interfaces with internal and external customers and vendors to determine communications infrastructure needs.
  • Updates job knowledge by participating in educational opportunities; reading professional publications; maintaining personal networks; participating in professional organizations.


Other Functions

  • Remain technically current and competent by learning new technologies and obtaining certifications as requested by management.
  • Manage and oversee telecommunications bills and service agreements, manage purchasing of telecommunications and related equipment, open and work with TAC cases to resolve issues, creates, implements, and manages dial plans.
  • Performs other duties as required.


Performs other duties as assigned by the Supervisor of Network Infrastructure and Security.


Required Qualifications

  • Associate's Degree in information technology, computer science, engineering or related field, or equivalent combination of education, certifications, or VOIP/IP technical experience.
  • Four (4) years' full time experience providing network administration within a large scale converged Ethernet infrastructure including experience with VOIP administration and implementation, QOS configurations, VOIP protocols, IP call signaling and control, H323, SIP, etc.
  • CompTIA Network+ certification; Avaya, Cisco or related IP telephony certifications.
  • Minimum two (2) years' installing, troubleshooting, implementing, maintaining and building configurations on switches and/or routers.
  • Experience with and ability to independently configure and troubleshoot Avaya CM, Avaya MM, Avaya Media Gateways, UCC and other Avaya related telecommunications infrastructure or Cisco CUCM, Unity, UCS, etc.
  • Demonstrated experience and broad knowledge of routing protocols, switch protocols, TCP/IP, telecommunication protocols (IP), QOS, VLANs, ACL's, DHCP, DNS, TFTP, FTP, SNMP, SMTP, POE, etc.
  • Demonstrated experience with network monitoring tools, preferably Solarwinds and WUG.
  • Demonstrated experience performing and analyzing network packet captures using packet analyzers such as Wireshark.
  • Demonstrated experience with and knowledge of Windows or Linus servers.
  • Ability to work off-hours as needed/required.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with minimal supervision.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently and effectively complete work assignments and projects in a timely fashion.
  • Capable of performing the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodations.
  • Regular and predictable attendance.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience configuring, administrating, and troubleshooting unified communications technologies such as Microsoft Lync.
  • Experience or good understanding of Microsoft Exchange mail servers and Active Directory.
  • Knowledge of storage environment and how it interrelates with telecommunications infrastructure.
  • Experience with implementing and configuring wireless VOIP.
  • Experience with VMWare or other virtualization technologies.
  • Experience implementing and administering VOIP and telecommunications high availability systems.
  • Work experience in K-12 educational setting.
  • Familiarity with the FCPS policies, goals and programs.

Under the direction of an assigned supervisor, acts as liaison to assigned business area and provides and recommends solutions to improve processes and delivery of services to students, faculty, and staff through expansion of existing systems or the use of third party systems and applications; responsible for assisting and leading the updates and changes in the student success web pages; analyze and implement integration/interfacing of systems with the College's ERP system; serve as the administrator of designated third-party applications.

DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS

This classification is a unique and highly specialized role within the district which provides functional and process support for the business units of the district in using information technology systems and tools effectively and efficiently. This classification is assigned to support one or more business units based on the business expertise of the individual assigned and acts as a liaison between the business unit and the technical staff in the Information Technology department. This classification is tasked with understanding system and tool capabilities and their application to the business needs of the supported units.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

The following duties and responsibilities describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be restricted or construed as an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities required of individuals so classified, and not all duties listed are necessarily performed by each employee in this classification.

2. Works independently and collaborates with other technical staff and functional staff to implement solutions seamlessly.

4. Performs a variety of advanced analytical, internal consulting and project leadership/oversight duties to enable multiple stakeholders to achieve business, administrative, and academic objectives.

8. Serves as the content manager of the assigned area webpages.

9. Trains users on systems processes specific to the assigned business area's software programs and other technical areas, including training guides, written procedures, documentation, manuals, and materials for user and staff support.

10.Consults with administrators and managers on application development, enhancement, and maintenance issues; explains technology and process options and assists in analysis and decision making.

11.Recommends solutions and works with functional users to develop and to implement solutions that align with the needs and requirements.

12.Performs application-level troubleshooting for students and employees.

13.Performs support to functional users during upgrades and patching, and during migration from/to systems.

14.Assists in planning and scheduling of upgrades, testing, and roll out of the systems that minimizes impact to daily operations.

title: IT System Administrator
description:

Tokio Marine North America Services (TMNAS) provides professional support services to Tokio Marine Group companies in the United States, including Tokio Marine America, First Insurance Company of Hawaii, and Philadelphia Insurance Companies.   • Experience with scripting, automation, infrastructure-as-code concepts, monitoring tools, PowerShell, and Python preferred

  • Experience documenting technical standards, operational procedures, business requirements, functional specifications, and support handoff materials

Knowledge

  • Knowledge and understanding of business processes, technology dependencies, security expectations, service availability needs, and operational risk in the context of the company’s business
  • Knowledge of current infrastructure trends, including cloud adoption, hybrid management, automation, monitoring, endpoint/server security, identity and access management, and resiliency planning

Skills

  • Strong project and change management skills, including planning, organizing, monitoring, coordinating resources, and executing work within approved maintenance windows and deadlines
  • Strong interpersonal relationship-building skills; able to work constructively and collaboratively with infrastructure, security, application, service desk, vendor, and business teams
  • Strong analytical ability with the capability to identify root causes, assess risk, evaluate options, and recommend practical, supportable solutions
  • Ability to use automation, scripting, monitoring, and standard operating procedures to improve consistency, reliability, and operational efficiency

Your mission

We are looking for a Business Unit Director to lead the strategy and business development of Dermo-Cosmetics Business Unit in Spain, driving profitable growth and making a meaningful impact across the organization

  • Define the country strategy for the BU within the assigned area, in collaboration with the subsidiary manager, and play a direct role in the implementation of key initiatives, especially regarding priority topics

  • Improve efficiency/productivity by developing activity in your country (structure, marketing/digital investments, human resources) through rational expenditure management within your area according to the Group’s strategic guidelines and in the context of profitable growth.

  • Define and implement the resulting actions alongside the subsidiary manager: staff management, reorganization, recruitment or dismissal, budget cuts, etc. in accordance with the strategy defined by management.
  • Promote a digital culture to improve "patient or consumer centricity" and ensure that we are a preferred and trusted partner.
  • Draw up a comprehensive medicalization policy to set us apart from the competition
  • Lead and supervise the team. Develop skills and manage performance, both individually and collectively
  • Optimize working methods and organization by proposing monitoring means and procedures in accordance with Group standards and local legislation, and by ensuring employee commitment (leadership, mobility, skills development, etc.).
  • Defend and implement the conditions for promoting and maximizing the value of our ethical, compliance and sustainable development approaches (Green Mission).

Who you are ?

We are looking for a strategic and business-oriented leader with:

  • Master’s degree in Business, Pharmacy, Science or a related field; additional marketing/management training is a plus.
  • 10+ years of relevant experience in dermo-cosmetics, skincare, beauty or healthcare, ideally across Business Unit/Brand Management, Marketing or Sales.
  • Strong knowledge of the pharmacy and para-pharmacy ecosystem and experience working with pharmacists, dermatologists, HCPs and key retail/e-commerce partners.
  • Strong leadership & strategic commercial experience and deep understanding of the spanish competitive landscape
  • Strong business acumen and P&L expertise, with a clear understanding of sales, margin, investments and ROI.
  • Proven experience in brand building and activation, combining scientific credibility, HCP/pharmacist recommendation and excellent execution both offline and online.
  • Strong leadership capabilities, with experience leading large cross-functional teams in a matrix environment.
  • A highly results-driven, analytical and strategic mindset, combined with strong operational discipline.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to connect effectively with local and global teams and external partners.

We are convinced that diversity is a source of fulfillment, social balance and complementarity for our employees, which is why our offers are open to all, without restriction.

title: Change & Culture Specialist
description:

Job Description

The Change & Culture Lead is a senior specialist role within the Old Mutual Wealth Human Capital team.

The role partners with executives, leaders, Human Capital Business Partners and project teams to lead the people and culture dimensions of strategic change across the business.

The successful candidate will translate business priorities into integrated change and culture strategies that build readiness, strengthen leadership alignment, drives adoption and embed sustainable ways of working.

The role will also lead culture activation initiatives, build change capability across the organisation and use data and employee insights to assess progress and continuously improve interventions.

This opportunity is suited to an experienced change and culture professional who is comfortable navigating ambiguity, influencing senior stakeholders and managing multiple priorities in a complex, highly regulated and rapidly changing environment.

The role is based in Pinelands, Cape Town

Responsibilities

Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead the development and execution of integrated change and culture strategies aligned to business and Human Capital priorities.

  • Partner with executives, sponsors, Human Capital Business Partners and project teams to integrate the people side of change into strategic initiatives.

  • Conduct stakeholder, change impact and readiness assessments to identify affected groups, adoption requirements, risks and potential resistance.

  • Translate culture priorities into clear, observable leadership and employee behaviours that can be activated and sustained in the flow of work.

  • Develop and deliver stakeholder engagement, sponsorship, communication, learning and reinforcement plans.

  • Coach and equip executives, leaders and change champions to communicate change effectively, role-model the required behaviours and support their teams through transition.

  • Facilitate leadership alignment sessions, workshops, focus groups and employee engagements that build understanding, commitment and accountability.

  • Identify, manage and mitigate people-related risks and barriers that could affect adoption, culture or business continuity.

  • Establish fit-for-purpose change methodologies, tools, templates and governance practices that support disciplined and consistent execution.

  • Build practical change capability across line leadership and the Human Capital community through learning content, toolkits, coaching and knowledge transfer.

  • Define and monitor measures of change readiness, adoption, employee sentiment, behavioural shift and culture impact.

  • Use feedback and data to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions, recommend corrective action and report progress to key stakeholders.

  • Manage multiple initiatives simultaneously, adapting plans quickly as business priorities and operating conditions evolve.

  • Stay informed about emerging practices in organisational change, culture, employee experience and transformation, and apply relevant insights to the Wealth context.

Qualifications and Experience required

  • A relevant bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Organisational Psychology, Organisational Development, Business, or a related field.

  • A recognised change management qualification or certification is advantageous.

  • At least 7 years of relevant experience in organisational change, culture transformation or organisational development, including experience leading complex or enterprise-wide change initiatives.

  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing integrated change strategies across multiple stakeholder groups.

  • Proven experience advising, coaching and influencing executives and senior leaders.

  • Experience designing and facilitating leadership, culture and employee engagement interventions.

  • Strong understanding of culture change, organisational behaviour, employee engagement and diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging principles.

  • Experience using qualitative and quantitative data to assess readiness, sentiment, adoption and intervention effectiveness.

  • Experience in financial services or another complex, highly regulated environment is advantageous.

  • Experience working effectively in a fast-paced environment with shifting priorities, competing demands and high levels of ambiguity.

title: Information Technology Services Student Records System Specialist
description:
QUALIFICATIONS:

  1. Associate's degree in information technology, business information systems, education technology, data management, or a related field; bachelor's degree preferred.
  2. Experience administering or supporting Focus School Software or a comparable K–12 student information system is preferred.
  3. Three years of relevant experience supporting a student information system, enterprise application, database, or comparable environment; equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered.
  4. Working knowledge of relational databases and SQL, including the ability to query, validate, analyze, and safely update data.
  5. Experience with data imports, exports, scheduled jobs, APIs, SFTP transfers, and third-party system integrations is preferred.
  6. Demonstrated ability to analyze data, troubleshoot software issues, document procedures, train users, and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical staff.
  7. Such alternatives to the above qualifications as the Board may find appropriate and acceptable.

REPORTS TO: Information Technology Services Director

JOB GOAL:

The Student Records System Specialist manages and supports the District student records system to ensure accurate, secure, timely, and compliant student information. This individual coordinates system configuration, data quality, user support, reporting, training, and process improvement so schools and district departments can rely on consistent records throughout the student lifecycle.

PERFORMANCE RESPONSIBILITIES:

  1. Maintains up-to-date knowledge and documentation regarding the District student records system, related modules, interfaces, workflows, data standards, procedures, training materials, data dictionaries, logs, and audit records.
  2. Database and reporting-Develops, maintains, tests, and documents SQL queries, district reports, extracts, validation reports, and authorized data-correction processes.
  3. Focus configuration-Configures and maintains Focus modules, system preferences, schools, calendars, marking periods, grading scales, enrollment settings, permissions, profiles, custom fields, scheduled jobs, and district-defined workflows.
  4. Integrations-Administers and monitors integrations between Focus and systems used for identity management, learning management, assessment, transportation, food service, library services, communications, state reporting, and other District operations.
  5. Data-quality monitoring-Establishes repeatable validation processes to identify missing, duplicate, inconsistent, or invalid records and coordinates corrections with the appropriate data owners.
  6. Change control and testing-Tests system updates, configuration changes, reports, integrations, and data corrections in an appropriate test environment before production implementation; maintains change documentation and rollback procedures when applicable.
  7. Security administration-Maintains role-based access, user profiles, school assignments, and permissions using the principle of least privilege; periodically reviews access and promptly addresses inappropriate or outdated permissions.
  8. State and federal reporting-Supports the preparation, validation, correction, and submission of required state and federal student-data reports in collaboration with the departments responsible for reported data.
  9. Vendor coordination-Serves as the primary technical liaison with Focus School Software and other vendors; submits and tracks support requests, evaluates vendor recommendations, and coordinates issue resolution.
  10. Operational monitoring-Monitors scheduled reports, automated updates, integrations, imports, exports, and other recurring processes; investigates failures and verifies successful completion.
  11. Documentation-Maintains configuration records, data dictionaries, integration specifications, SQL documentation, annual processing checklists, troubleshooting guides, and administrative procedures.
  12. Business continuity-Develops procedures that allow critical SIS operations to continue during staff absences, outages, system changes, or other interruptions.
  13. Availability expectations-Provides limited after-hours support for critical upgrades, annual rollover, system outages, and time-sensitive reporting deadlines.
  14. Provides telephone, digital, and in-person assistance to school and district personnel; investigates service requests, identifies root causes, recommends solutions, and coordinates resolution with internal staff and vendors.
  15. Monitors the accuracy, completeness, consistency, and timeliness of student data and works with schools and departments to correct errors and strengthen data-entry practices.
  16. Supports student records processes including enrollment, registration, demographic updates, attendance, scheduling, grades, transcripts, withdrawals, promotions, and graduation records, as assigned.
  17. Maintains system security and confidentiality by applying appropriate access controls, protecting personally identifiable information, and supporting compliance with Board policy and applicable student privacy requirements.
  18. Coordinates imports, exports, integrations, data exchanges, and interfaces between the student records system and other District applications.
  19. Plans and performs system updates, testing, annual rollover activities, school-year setup, and other scheduled maintenance in collaboration with Information Technology Services and District departments.
