title: Fire Sprinkler Designer (Clifton, NJ)
description:
Fire Sprinkler Designer

Full-Time, On-Site


Our client is an established fire protection organization expanding its design capabilities to support a strong and growing project pipeline. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Fire Sprinkler Designer who wants to take ownership of meaningful projects, work alongside knowledgeable industry professionals, and continue advancing technically. The position offers substantial exposure to residential and multifamily construction, including mid-rise and high-rise developments, along with opportunities for increased technical responsibility and continued professional development.


This Role Offers:

  • Competitive compensation based on sprinkler design experience, technical expertise, and certification.
  • Exposure to residential, multifamily, mid-rise, and high-rise fire protection projects.
  • An established design environment where experienced professionals can make an immediate impact.
  • Support for continued professional development, including advancement toward NICET certification.


Focus:

  • Create detailed water-based fire sprinkler system designs that meet applicable codes, project specifications, and construction requirements.
  • Develop sprinkler layouts, design drawings, hydraulic calculations, and supporting project documentation.
  • Review architectural and construction documents to determine system requirements and identify potential design or coordination challenges.
  • Coordinate sprinkler layouts with building systems and other construction disciplines to support efficient installation.
  • Participate in BIM and 3D coordination activities when required by the project.
  • Update designs to account for field conditions, construction changes, coordination feedback, and comments from reviewing authorities.
  • Work closely with project managers, field personnel, engineers, contractors, and other project stakeholders throughout the design process.
  • Evaluate constructability and develop practical solutions that help field teams execute installations efficiently.
  • Manage multiple design assignments while maintaining accuracy, quality, and project schedules.
  • Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing to developing members of the design team when appropriate.


Skill Set:

  • Direct professional fire sprinkler system design experience, with the ability to independently perform sprinkler layout and design work without extensive entry-level training.
  • Strong understanding of water-based fire protection systems, sprinkler design practices, applicable NFPA standards, and construction documentation.
  • Ability to read and interpret architectural drawings, specifications, and related construction documents.
  • Residential or multifamily sprinkler design experience is strongly preferred, particularly involving mid-rise or high-rise construction.
  • NICET certification in Water-Based Systems Layout is preferred, with Level II representing a particularly strong match. Experienced designers without NICET certification may also be considered.
  • Experience with AutoSPRINK is highly desirable, although candidates with substantial experience using other established sprinkler design platforms may be considered.
  • Revit, BIM, and 3D coordination experience are additional advantages.
  • Strong communication and problem-solving skills with the ability to collaborate across design, project management, and field teams.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities while producing accurate and constructible designs.
  • Ability to work full-time on-site and currently reside in New Jersey or an immediately commutable location.

title: SUPERVISOR MANUFACTURING (6000)
description:
Job description:

SUMMARY: Supervises all warehouse staff assigned to shift, including assigning daily job tasks. Responsible for having deliveries unloaded in order of priority and properly placed in the warehouse. Responsible for keeping production supplied with components and moving finished goods from the production areas to internal and external customers. Ensures Safety and Health requirements are met for the Department. Helps to maintain 5S and housekeeping standards. Helps to maintain and ensure compliance of all related SOP’s. Performs a variety of functions related to receiving personnel and equipment maintenance.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITES:

  • Manages all activities of assigned employees, including packing customer orders and completing all necessary shipping documentation, etc.
  • Warehouse Supervisor determines work procedures, prepares work schedules and expedites workflow; reviews and standardizes procedures to improve efficiency of subordinates
  • Directs assigned employees to tasks, ensuring they understand what is required for each shift and assigned duties
  • Provide coaching, training, and tools for employees to perform their jobs successfully. Provides feedback, when necessary, for improvement. Assists employees in resolving problems
  • Coordinates with other supervisors of preceding and succeeding shifts to ensure accurate understanding and communication of issues including full cycle carryover functions
  • Direct the operations of the assigned work team to achieve prescribed objectives
  • Follow all policies and procedures
  • Oversee the production goals established by the company and monitors to ensure employees are meeting established productivity goals, safely and accurately
  • Maintain all daily housekeeping and safety standards
  • Collaborate with workers and managers to solve work-related problems
  • Communicate via email or telephone if necessary all preventable problems to production, copying the warehouse collective email address
  • Resolve inventory issues found in empty bins
  • Counsels employees in work-related activities, personal growth, or career development
  • Recommend or initiate personnel actions, such as promotions, transfers, or disciplinary measures
  • Assess training needs of staff and arrange for or provide appropriate instruction
  • Work with Shift supervisor to keep damage area current and clean
  • Assist Line Leads in motivation to understand the necessity of meeting our customer demands and stepping forward to meet those demands
  • Routinely communicate with your Supervisor in order to gain directives, discuss decisions and action plans, and share information
  • Required to work a flexible work schedule when needed
  • Perform all other duties as assigned

SUPERVISORY REPONSIBILITIES: YES

EDUCATION:

High School Diploma/GED/or Equivalent required

Bachelor’s Degree preferred

EXPERIENCE:

Minimum of three (3) years of supervisory experience required

Five (5) years of forklift experience in a narrow aisle warehouse preferred

COMPETENCIES:

  • Thorough knowledge of warehouse methods and techniques employed in a distribution center
  • Demonstrated supervisory and administrative skills
  • Demonstrated leadership and management traits including the ability to motivate people while engendering their respect and support
  • Proficient with MS Office products.
  • SAP knowledge preferred
  • Knowledge of appropriate forklift regulations and safety rules is mandatory
  • Excellent interpersonal skills to interface across the entire company
  • Train and continually develop the skills of the personnel in your area
  • Empower personnel to improve and do their best; ensuring pride in their team and ownership of their line
  • Encourage a team spirit where all associates have pride in their line, and therefore continually attempt to break records and set new production standards
  • Follow Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs), Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) training, along with company pre-requisite programs, Standard Operating Procedures (SOP’s), and Standard Sanitation Operating Procedures (SSOP’s)
  • Problem Solving - Ability to find a solution for or to deal proactively with work-related problems
  • Multi-tasking - Ability to work under pressure, meet deadlines and handle multiple projects simultaneously and work in a fast-paced environment
  • Initiative - Ability to make decisions or take actions to solve a problem or reach a goal
  • Accuracy - Superior accuracy and attention to detail
  • Detail Oriented - Ability to pay attention to the last minute details of a project or task
  • Relationships - Establishes and maintains professional relationships with vendors, customers and employees at all levels based on credibility, integrity and trust
  • Accountability - Ability to accept responsibility and account for his/her actions
  • Honesty / Integrity - Ability to be truthful and be seen as credible in the workplace
  • Organized - Possessing the trait of being organized or following a systematic method of performing a task
  • Time Management - Ability to utilize the available time to organize and complete work within given deadlines
  • Reliability - The trait of being dependable and trustworthy
  • Verbal/Written Communication Skills - Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English
  • Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and/or maintenance instructions and procedure manuals

Machines, Tools, Equipment and Work Aids: Various forklift trucks, computers, general office equipment, and related programs. Ability to learn the use of SAP as it relates to the inventory job function. Proficiency operating an RF unit.

License(s)/Certification(s): Forklift operator certification or ability to obtain certification.

Travel: None

Work Environment:

This role occasionally uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines. Worker will be exposed to ambient noise level in an office and warehouse environment. Temperatures can vary from cool to warm depending upon the season. The employee must comply with the assigned location PPE requirements including but not limited to safety glasses, hearing protection, appropriate gloves, clothing and shields for required tasks and closed toed or safety shoes as required by facility safety policies. Worker exposed to physical conditions such as proximity to moving mechanical parts. Worker occasionally exposed to atmospheric conditions such as fumes.

Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Sitting, walking, climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, reaching, pushing, pulling, grasping, lifting, talking, and hearing. Occasionally lifting pallets up to 60 lbs. by hand, stacking finished good cases on a pallet up to 30 lbs. / case by hand, replacing stretch film into the automatic wrapper up to 30 lbs. by hand, and moving pallets of products weighing up to 2000 lbs. with a forklift. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision and depth perception.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee is regularly required to stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms. The employee frequently is required to use hands to manipulate objects, tools or controls and talk or hear. The employee is regularly required to walk; stoop; crouch; bend and reach above shoulders. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 60 pounds unassisted and up to 200 pounds with assistance, waist high, up to 10 feet away.

title: Advokat/Advokatfullmektig
description:
Vil du bruke jussen til å løse komplekse og samfunnsviktige saker?

Hos oss får du jobbe i skjæringspunktet mellom juss, gransking og rådgivning. Du blir en del av et tverrfaglig miljø og får bidra i komplekse oppdrag for både private og offentlige virksomheter.

BDO er stort nok til å gi deg spennende prosjekter og utviklingsmuligheter, og samtidig lite nok til at du blir sett, hørt og får påvirke. Som advokatfullmektig eller advokat i Forensics & Integrity får du ansvar, tillit og muligheten til å arbeide tett på reelle og krevende problemstillinger.

Teamet du blir en del av

Du blir en del av Forensics & Integrity i Risk, BDO Consulting. Risk består av rundt 45 rådgivere med ulik faglig bakgrunn, mens Forensics & Integrity teller rundt 10 spesialister.

Sammen bistår vi kunder med håndtering av varsler, granskinger, compliance, internkontroll og andre krevende risiko- og integritetsrelaterte problemstillinger. Vi jobber tett med kunder i både privat og offentlig sektor og kombinerer kompetanse innen juss, revisjon, økonomi, etterforskning, sikkerhet og teknologi.

Hos oss møter du et sterkt fagmiljø med høy kompetanse og stor takhøyde. Arbeidsmiljøet er preget av samarbeid, raushet og en genuin interesse for å lære av hverandre. Du får ansvar tidlig, samtidig som du har dyktige kolleger rundt deg som støtter deg og bidrar til utviklingen din.

Dette kommer du til å jobbe med

Arbeidsoppgavene vil variere ut fra erfaring, interesse og prosjektbehov. I rollen vil du blant annet:

  • Bistå i granskinger, varslingssaker og andre undersøkelser, inkludert faktainnhenting, dokumentgjennomgang, analyser, intervjuer og rapportskriving.
  • Bidra i prosjekter innen blant annet compliance, internkontroll, risikostyring, personvern, arbeidsrett og virksomhetsstyring.
  • Utarbeide juridiske og tverrfaglige analyser, beslutningsgrunnlag, notater og rapporter.
  • Delta i kundemøter, presentasjoner og andre deler av kundeleveransen.
  • Samarbeide tett med kolleger fra ulike fagområder og bidra til videreutvikling av teamets kompetanse og tjenestetilbud.
  • Bidra i tilbudsarbeid og utvikling av nye tjenester og metoder.

Hvorfor BDO?

Hos oss får du muligheten til å gjøre en forskjell - både for kundene våre og for din egen utvikling.

Komplekse og meningsfulle saker: Du får jobbe med reelle og krevende problemstillinger der juss, fakta og forretningsforståelse møtes.

Et tverrfaglig fagmiljø: Du samarbeider med spesialister innen blant annet juss, økonomi, revisjon, etterforskning, sikkerhet og teknologi – og lærer av ulike perspektiver og fagområder.

Ansvar og tillit tidlig: Du får mulighet til å bidra aktivt i kundeleveranser og ta ansvar i takt med erfaring og utvikling.

Gode utviklingsmuligheter: Vi gir deg muligheter, ikke bare oppgaver. Gjennom varierte oppdrag, kurs, sertifiseringer, tett oppfølging og en tydelig karrierevei legger vi til rette for faglig og personlig utvikling.

Hvem ser vi etter?

Vi ser etter deg som har:

  • Mastergrad i rettsvitenskap eller cand.jur.
  • Inntil tre års relevant arbeidserfaring. Nyutdannede oppfordres også til å søke.
  • Svært god skriftlig og muntlig fremstillingsevne på norsk.
  • Gode analytiske evner og interesse for å forstå komplekse problemstillinger.
  • Evne til å arbeide strukturert og selvstendig, med høy kvalitet i leveransene.
  • Motivasjon for å anvende juridisk kompetanse i praktiske problemstillinger og kundeleveranser.

Det er en fordel om du har erfaring med eller interesse for ett eller flere av områdene arbeidsrett, personvern, gransking, varslingshåndtering, compliance, risikostyring eller internkontroll.

Erfaring fra rådgivning, offentlig sektor, revisjonsvirksomhet, utrednings- og analysearbeid, intervjuer, faktainnhenting, dataanalyse, prosjektarbeid eller kundedialog er også relevant.

Som person er du nysgjerrig og analytisk, og motiveres av å forstå komplekse problemstillinger. Du har høy integritet og god rolleforståelse, særlig i arbeid med sensitive saker. Samtidig kommuniserer du tydelig, samarbeider godt med andre og tar ansvar for å drive arbeidet strukturert fremover.

Vi tror at forskjeller i bakgrunn, utdanning og perspektiver gjør oss bedre. Er du usikker på om du kvalifiserer til stillingen? Vi oppfordrer deg likevel til å søke.

Vil du være med og styrke Forensics & Integrity?

Da vil vi gjerne høre fra deg. Last opp CV-en din raskt og enkelt i søknadsportalen. Vi vurderer søknader fortløpende og oppfordrer til å søke snarest.

title: Office/Database Administrator - International & EL Office
description:
Office/Database Administrator

International & EL Office

Full-time, 12 months/year

Bilingual preferred

Are you looking to work in a school division where students are engaged in authentic, challenging, and relevant learning experiences, becoming lifelong contributors and leaders in our dynamic and diverse society? Then look no further!

In Albemarle County Public Schools, we work together as a team to end the predictive value of race, class, gender, and special capacities for our children’s success through high-quality teaching and learning for all. We seek to build relationships with families and communities to ensure that every student succeeds. We will know every student!

We are the first public school division in Virginia, and among the first in the country, to develop and implement an Anti-Racism policy with the expressed purpose of building school communities that share the responsibility to recognize and end racism, eliminate inequitable practices that result in achievement gaps, and support the unique gifts, talents, and interests of every child. In ACPS, “all” really means all.

ACPS employees enjoy competitive pay and benefits, including health & dental coverage, retirement, flexible spending accounts, paid time off, wellness program, discounts on gym memberships, and more! Be sure to check out our website to learn more about our Division and our Schools.

*This is a grant-funded position.

General Definition of Work:

Performs technical work to coordinate student information system activities. Provides primary support and training for users of the student information system. Other work consists of varied administrative support duties involving a wide range of processes and methods. Requires a broad knowledge of County and/or school operations and frequent contacts with top-level officials. Work is performed under general supervision with considerable latitude for independent judgment.

Essential Functions:
  • Oversees the school's or program's student information system application including data entry, data validation, and reporting;
  • Trains school building/program users on the student information system application and network operations;
  • Coordinates existing administrative procedures and handbooks with student information system operations;
  • Performs quality checking on data entry by other school or program staff;
  • Designs and executes complex queries of the student database for reporting and analysis;
  • Meets division and school deadlines for processing and reporting student data;
  • Participates in student information system users' group(s) as appropriate;
  • Participates in development and delivery of division-wide training on the student information system;
  • Works with Information Services to maintain necessary files, directories, and updates to student information system software;
  • Works with Information Services and school or program staff to determine hardware needed to support users' requests and advises on hardware purchases to comply with Information Services standards;
  • Responsible for completion of complex administrative and technical assignments;
  • Regularly responsible for complex payroll related tasks;
  • May screen applicants and conduct interviews, and included in hiring/promotion/termination decisions;
  • Communicates with department employees on personnel-related programs;
  • Works independently on complex projects including preparation of budgets and reports, administration of grants, and accounting systems;
  • Routinely prepares and administers department budget;.
  • Monitors multiple department accounts and completes all bookkeeping tasks, and handles purchase orders/requisitions, receiving reports;
  • Prepares correspondence for department and responds to general inquiries;
  • Answers and screens calls, and gathers information to provide appropriate response;
  • Gives direction to administrative staff who provide reception coverage for school;
  • Responds to difficult customer-related issues and resolves them accordingly;
  • Establishes and maintains files, frequently of a confidential and/or sensitive nature;
  • Creates bulk mailings using databases and mail merge features;
  • Plays significant role in office management and oversight for unit/department; Frequently provides back-up to department/unit head in his/her absence;
  • May serve on special and/or regular teams and committees, serves on the school Crisis Team;
  • Frequently provides day-to-day direction for or has responsibility for supervision of administrative services within the department/unit;
  • Dispenses meds, provides basic first aid, and monitors students with medical special needs;
  • Performs various other functions as required.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Knowledge of database management, word processing, spreadsheets, and data communications; ability to organize and plan work for self and others; ability to develop training materials and skills in conducting training; and ability to communicate effectively, orally and in writing. Considerable knowledge of departmental functions, school administration, organization, and policies. Ability to occasionally perform complex mathematical and statistical calculations. Ability to maintain complex clerical records and prepare reports from records. Comprehensive knowledge of business English and spelling. Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with students, parents, staff, government officials, and the general public. Ability to meet parents, community, top-level officials, and others with tact and diplomacy. Ability to maintain financial records and prepare reports and statements. Intermediate to advanced proficiency in office-related and department-specific software. Ability to effectively use office equipment, including computer, copier, postage meter, Fax, printer, multiple-line phone, paper folder, laminator, projector, and scanner.

Education and Experience:

Education or experience equivalent to graduation from high school with postsecondary coursework or training and at least one year experience supporting a networked database application and at least four years extensive, increasingly responsible experience in clerical work. Documented and certified post high school classes or training providing technical knowledge may be considered as additional experience.

Physical Conditions and Nature of Work Contacts:

Work is typically performed in an office setting primarily sitting at office equipment, with occasional walking throughout the school building. Lifting and carrying of objects weighing up to 30 pounds is required. Frequent operation of microcomputers, printers and a variety of office machines is required. Regular, daily contact is made with school administrators, counselor, teachers, students, parents, and the general public.

Evaluation:

Performance will be evaluated on the ability and effectiveness in carrying out the above responsibilities.

title: Tier 2 SOC Analyst with AI Tools Experience - REMOTE

  • Be the main point of contact to the MDR Provider’s Detection team

Serving as a key strategic partner and connector, the Coordinator continuously assesses district-wide needs, evaluates emerging tools, and ensures all digital learning platforms align with strict accessibility and privacy standards.   • Support the research, development, and implementation of district policies governing digital learning, acceptable use, data privacy, and instructional technology.
  • Oversee elementary digital literacy initiatives while partnering with secondary coordinators to align digital learning and computer competencies across PK–12.

  • Support faculty in maximizing the use of district Learning Management Systems (LMS), and complementary academic software.

title: Platform Engineer med DX-fokus till Sveriges Radio
description:
Sveriges Radios uppdrag är att sända radio i allmänhetens tjänst. Varje vecka tar drygt sju miljoner lyssnare del av innehållet via linjär radio och on demand, i FM och på digitala plattformar. Innehållet ska vara brett, mångsidigt och av hög kvalitet, och alla som bor i Sverige ska kunna hitta något av intresse hos oss. Att jobba på Sveriges Radio innebär därför att du, oavsett roll, är en värdefull del i ett viktigt uppdrag.

Sveriges Radio är en utpräglad tech-organisation. När du lyssnar på oss är det 100 års konstant teknikutveckling från en arena i teknologins framkant du hör. Bakom varje program och sändning, i varenda kanal och plattform, finns ett kraftfullt fundament av innovativ teknologi som verkar tyst i bakgrunden, dygnet runt, året om, med oerhörda krav på precision och stabilitet. Kraven på oss framåt är om möjligt ännu högre. Vi är idag över 300 IT-experter som ser till att ge röst åt fler röster och starkare berättelser för en större förståelse. De utmaningar vi har framför oss har inget utrymme för misslyckanden. Så vill man vara med och göra skillnad, på riktigt, ja då ska man jobba med tech på Sveriges Radio.

Tjänsten och ansvarsområden

Som platform engineer är du med och formar vår tekniska plattform och de verktyg som andra utvecklare använder varje dag. Vårt team består av tre utvecklare och en produktägare som sitter utspridda på radiohus runtom i landet.

Teamets syfte är att förbättra vardagen för utvecklare på Sveriges Radio, till exempel genom att:

  • utveckla och vidareutveckla Sveriges Radios interna Kubernetesplattform och utvecklarportal.
  • förbättra CI/CD-flöden och Git-baserade arbetssätt från utveckling till produktionssättning.
  • arbeta med infrastruktur som kod.
  • bidra till tydliga och användbara golden paths för exempelvis deployment, rollback och nya applikationsmiljöer.
  • bygga en utvecklarportal som knyter samman utvecklarnära system och verktyg.
  • arbeta nära andra utvecklare och fånga upp behov och pain points.
  • dela kunskap genom dokumentation, praktiska exempel, demos och direkt samarbete med andra team.
  • skriva egna applikationer och använda tredjepartslösningar för att lösa problem.

Vi jobbar bland annat med dessa verktyg: ArgoCD, Kargo, Hashicorp Vault, Backstage, GitHub, Harbor, Grafana-stacken, Terraform, External Secrets Operator.

Vi söker dig som har intresse för och gärna erfarenhet av ovan nämnda områden. Utöver det hoppas vi att:

  • du gillar att lösa uppgifter som ett team.
  • du angriper problem som en utvecklare, automatiserar och löser dem med kod.
  • du värdesätter developer experience och autonomi för utvecklarteam.
  • du är nyfiken på att utforska nya tekniker.
  • du gillar att sprida kunskap, både inom teamet och till användare.

Varför du ska söka

Hos oss får du arbeta genom hela kedjan – från utveckling och infrastruktur till cloud, CI/CD, säkerhet och utvecklarupplevelse. Rollen ger stort utrymme för ett utforskande arbetssätt där du har möjlighet att påverka teknikval och riktning. Vi värdesätter kontinuerligt lärande och avsätter tid för att utvecklas, både som individ och tillsammans med teamet.

Du kommer att vara en viktig del av många utvecklares vardag och bidra till att skapa en plattform som fungerar som en produkt. Det innebär att förstå användarnas verkliga behov, prioritera det som skapar störst värde och följa upp att lösningarna faktiskt gör arbetet enklare.

Genom ditt arbete skapar du förutsättningar för andra team att utveckla och leverera public service till hela Sverige.

Samtidigt blir du en del av ett team med kunniga och engagerade kollegor som arbetar nära varandra och delar med sig av sina erfarenheter, vilket ger goda möjligheter att utvecklas tillsammans.

Frågor och kontaktuppgifter

Det här är en tillsvidareanställning med 6 månaders inledande provanställning. Tjänsten är på heltid, med placering i något av våra radiohus. Frågor om tjänsten besvaras av Olof Lindmark och skickas till olof.lindmark@sr.se. Vill du komma i kontakt med facket så hittar du alla fackliga kontakter här. Vi arbetar fyra dagar från kontoret med möjlighet till distansarbete en gång i veckan.

Skicka in din ansökan senast den 20/9/2026, och intervjuer sker löpande. Sveriges Radio krigsplacerar personal med anställning som överstiger 6 månader.

title: Technology Specialist
description:
Park County School District 6
Technology Specialist
Job Description

Purpose Statement

The job of Technology Specialist is done for the purpose/s of providing student and staff support to resolve software and hardware problems encountered, maintaining computer equipment and supplies, providing professional development to staff, and assisting with administration and support of the District's business applications, which may reside on multiple platforms.

This job reports to Assistant Superintendent

Essential Functions

  • Assists users with computers, mobile devices, printers, electronic, and audiovisual malfunctions for the purpose of providing immediate problem resolution and/or escalating for resolution.
  • Considers the needs of students of all ages for the purpose of supplying age-appropriate devices and software to enhance learning in every grade - in collaboration with district personnel.
  • Installs and sets up computer hardware and software applications involved with 500 - 2,000 devices annually (e.g. new computers, mobile devices, peripheral cards, configuring operating systems, printers, etc.) for the purpose of providing upgrades and program expansion to maintain standards.
  • Instructs personnel for the purpose of ensuring their ability to use new and/or existing operating systems and application software.
  • Maintains a detailed inventory of District resources (e.g. phones, printers, computer/mobile devices, access points, scanners, hardware, software, etc.) for the purpose of keeping resources available for any immediate need and for equipment rotation planning.
  • Maintains a variety of files, databases and records (e.g. parts inventory, service records, etc.) for the purpose of providing audit trails, control mechanisms and documenting department activities.
  • Provides technical support to staff for the purpose of ensuring efficiency in the use of various software products.
  • Researches technology issues and works with other team members to achieve the proper resolution in a timely manner.
  • Responds to a wide variety of requests, concerns and/or complaints for the purpose of resolving problems, providing information and/or referring to appropriate personnel.
  • Assists with the direction and supervision of summer technology assistants for the purpose of managing the workload in an efficient manner.
  • Troubleshoots existing/new/proposed application software and hardware for the purpose of identifying and resolving issues, providing user training, or referring to other resources for resolution.
  • Works with vendors (e.g. outside repair sources, etc.) for the purpose of repairing, updating or replacing technology equipment in a timely manner.
  • Performs other duties as assigned by Supervisor.

Knowledge, Skills and Mental Ability

  • Ability to prioritize and perform duties without direct supervision
  • Ability to meet deadlines and work under pressure
  • Ability to install, configure and maintain technology equipment and devices
  • Ability to analyze, troubleshoot and repair computer and software problems
  • Demonstrates skill and experience with a variety of computer hardware, operating systems and software
  • Physical dexterity and visual acuity to work with small parts
  • Written/oral interpersonal communication skills
  • Organizational skills including paper documentation, electronic documentation, daily logs, scheduling, etc.
  • Team player and team builder
  • Demonstrate ability to work with and maintain positive relationships with others
  • Demonstrate ability to create District technology training documents


Job Requirements: Minimum Qualifications
Skills, Knowledge and Abilities

SKILLS are required to perform multiple, technical tasks with a need to routinely upgrade skills in order to meet changing job conditions. Specific skill-based competencies required to satisfactorily perform the functions of the job include: operating standard office equipment using pertinent software applications; planning and managing projects; preparing and maintaining accurate records; adhering to safety practices and procedures; analyzing data; applying job-related codes, regulations and laws; assembling and/or repairing office and classroom equipment; classifying data and/or information; diagnosing equipment malfunctions; estimating required resources; handling hazardous materials; operating standard office equipment and office technology.

KNOWLEDGE is required to perform advanced math; read technical information, compose a variety of documents, and/or facilitate group discussions; and analyze situations to define issues and draw conclusions. Specific knowledge-based competencies required to satisfactorily perform the functions of the job include electronics/audiovisual maintenance and repair; MS Office application software; Google applications, computer operating systems; hardware/network and troubleshooting techniques; web applications; and concepts of grammar and punctuation.; age-appropriate behavior; concepts of grammar, spelling and punctuation; current and emerging technology; job-related codes/laws/rules/regulations/policies; knowledge of community resources; office equipment and technology; record keeping and record retention practices.

ABILITY is required to schedule a significant number of activities, meetings, and/or events; routinely gather, collate, and/or classify data; and consider a number of factors when using equipment. Flexibility is required to independently work with others in a wide variety of circumstances; analyze data utilizing a variety of complex processes; and utilize equipment under a variety of conditions for multiple purposes. Ability is also required to work with a diversity of individuals and/or groups; work with data of varied types and/or purposes; and utilize a wide variety of types of job-related equipment. Independent problem solving is required to analyze issues and create action plans. Problem solving with data frequently requires independent interpretation of guidelines; and problem solving with equipment is moderate to significant. Specific ability based competencies required to satisfactorily perform the functions of the job include: gathering information to diagnose problem; providing clear instructions; adapting to changing work priorities; communicating with diverse groups; setting priorities; and working as part of a team; accuracy and attention to detail; analyzing issues and determining appropriate course of action; being available on-call; communicating with persons of diverse backgrounds; displaying tact and courtesy; maintaining confidentiality; meeting deadlines and schedules; multitasking; organizing tasks; working with detailed information/data; working with frequent interruptions.

Responsibility
Responsibilities include: working independently under broad organizational policies to achieve organizational objectives; leading, guiding, and/or coordinating others; operating within a defined budget. Utilization of resources from other work units is often required to perform the job's functions. There is a continual opportunity to impact the organization's services.

Work Environment
The usual and customary methods of performing the job's functions require the following physical demands: significant lifting, carrying, pushing, and/or pulling, frequent climbing and balancing, significant stooping, kneeling, crouching, and/or crawling and significant fine finger dexterity. Generally the job requires 10% sitting, 30% walking, and 60% standing. The job is performed under minimal temperature variations and under conditions with exposure to risk of injury and/or illness.

Experience: Education: Equivalency:
Job related experience with increasing levels of responsibility is desired. Community college and/or vocational school degree with study in job-related area.

Continuing Educ. / Training:

Blood borne Pathogens Training & Testing
Diabetes Training & Testing
Homeless Training & Testing

Clearances
Criminal Justice Fingerprint/Background Clearance

title: Research Software Engineer, Calibration, MQS Center for Quantum Computing
description:
The Models, Quantum, and Silicon (MQS) Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) is a multi-disciplinary team of scientists, engineers, and technicians, on a mission to develop a fault-tolerant quantum computer.

We are looking to hire a Research Software Engineer to join our growing Software team. You will work closely with our experimental physics teams to enable their work characterizing, calibrating, and operating novel quantum devices. The ideal candidate should be able to translate high-level science requirements into software implementations (e.g. Python APIs/frameworks, data analysis pipelines, calibration nodes) that are performant, scalable, and intuitive. This requires someone who (1) has a strong desire to work within a team of scientists and engineers, and (2) demonstrates ownership in initiating and driving projects to completion. This role has a particular emphasis on working directly with experimental physicists to develop scientific software workflows that enable scaling to larger quantum devices.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at Amazon, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Export Control Requirement
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be either a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be able to obtain a US export license. If you are unsure if you meet these requirements, please apply and Amazon will review your application for eligibility.

Key job responsibilities
- Architect extensible & intuitive frameworks for running quantum computing experiments and analyzing data.
- Leverage the latest techniques in quantum calibration to enable scaling to larger devices.
- Optimize the performance of experiment & analysis tools to enable faster experiment throughput.
- Develop dashboards that allow experimentalists to inspect and control the state of quantum device calibration.
- Deploy and maintain cloud infrastructure that supports increasingly-complex science workflows.
- Empower scientists to actively contribute to the codebase through mentorship and documentation.

We are looking for candidates with strong engineering principles, a bias for action, superior problem-solving, and excellent communication skills. Working effectively within a team environment is essential. As a Research Software Engineer embedded in a broader research science organization, you will have the opportunity to work on new ideas and stay abreast of the field of experimental quantum computation.

A day in the life
The majority of your time will be spent on projects that extend the functional capabilities or performance of our internal research software stack. This requires working backwards from the needs of our science staff in the context of our larger experimental roadmap. You will translate science and software requirements into design proposals balancing implementation complexity against time-to-delivery. Once a design proposal has been reviewed and accepted, you’ll drive implementation and coordinate with internal stakeholders to ensure a smooth roll out. Because many high-level experimental goals have cross-cutting requirements, you’ll often work closely with other engineers or scientists or on the team.

About the team
You will be joining the Software group within the MQS Center of Quantum Computing. Our team is comprised of scientists and software engineers who are building scalable software that enables quantum computing technologies.

Be part of a team that pushes boundaries, developing custom silicon solutions that power the future of Google's direct-to-consumer products. Your expertise will shape the next generation of hardware experiences, delivering unparalleled performance, efficiency, and integration.

As a Senior Hardware Engineer in the Board and System Design team, you will work on ML/AI hardware systems projects to craft the solutions for current and future data center deployments. You will work with product teams to ensure that their goals are met with your systems. You will work with Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC), Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), Software, and Verification teams to ensure proper verification of features in your systems. You will work with the manufacturing teams to ensure that your designs are manufactured and ready for volume production. As a hardware engineer, you will design and build the systems that are the heart of the world's largest and most powerful computing infrastructure. You will see those systems from concept all the way through to high-volume manufacturing. Your work has the potential to shape the machinery that goes into our cutting-edge data centers, affecting millions of Google users.Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

title: Lube Tech
description:
Position Purpose

The Lube Technician position is a non-exempt hourly rate (plus bonus potential) position in which the associate will greet and enter guest information into the lube system, diagnose vehicle needs for oil change and additional services based on manufacturer recommendations, mileage and known service history, make service recommendations to the guest and complete them with the highest level of customer service. Perform oil change and other services ordered by guests using trained procedures and safety call outs, drive vehicles off the conveyor when needed, hand dry vehicle exterior surfaces from the wash tunnel including glass and wheels, clean and vacuum interior surfaces and complete additional wash services indicated on the wash ticket with high attention to detail with quality assuring guest satisfaction. Assist in finishing/detail as needed. Bonus payout can be reduced or forfeited for damages incurred, poor performance or attendance, failure to attend mandatory meetings and being on disciplinary notice or quitting without providing a 2 week written notice.

Reports To

Lube Manager, Lube Assistant Manager and Corporate (JLI/CMC) Operations

Major Tasks & Responsibilities

Duties include but are not limited to:

  • Provide excellent quality and customer service at all times
  • Follow all MCCW/CMC Operations and Lube, Oil Change and
  • Additional Service Processes per Lube Job Procedure Training
  • Follow Safety Standards per the operations and safety manuals at all times
  • Perform all roles and tasks associated with the Lube Operation
  • Follow all used oil and filter disposal per Operations/Safety Manual
  • Follow all Safety Call outs IA W Lube Tech Training Manual
  • Dry vehicle exteriors and clean interiors using Mr. Clean procedures and standards IA W Finisher Training as needed in the lube shop
  • Enter and drive vehicles off the conveyor when needed and move vehicles into position as needed if CMC driver certified
  • Greet guests with a smile using their name when possible when entering the lube area
  • Verify guest satisfaction using their name, lay out a blue towel and say "Thank You, Please Come Again" as guest is presented their vehicle before leaving the property
  • Ensure high quality results on every guest vehicle
  • Maintain a clean and safe work area at all times
  • Keep lube and finishing supplies stocked during the day
  • Occasionally assist in other carwash areas/departments to relieve congested areas due to business flow fluctuations
  • Help maintain overall site appearance/equipment (clean lot, windows, bathrooms, lobby, tunnel walls/floors/ arches/ equipment, reclaim trough - "pit"; minor painting, lawn/flower/landscape care, equipment maintenance/repair, minor damage repair/replace damaged parts)
  • Holding a sign on the carwash property near the street to attract attention of passing vehicles on the road way that advertise hours, services, special offers/programs, other business communication, etc.
  • Inform management of any issues that arise (safety, mechanical, damages, cleanliness, guest/customer service, etc.)
  • Any other CMC job task or duties assigned by Management Upper Bay
  • Greet guest and enter their information into the computer system
  • Evaluate/recommend services based on manufacturers recommendations, mileage and history
  • Ensure all fluids are filled per vehicle specifications
  • Maintain a clean and safe work area at all times in the Lower Bay
  • Communicate lower vehicle needs to upper bay tech
  • Complete all lower bay inspections and services
  • Keep tools and supplies clean and orderly
  • Unpack, re-stock and organize the lube inventory

Scheduling, Weather, Lunch Breaks

  • Work week is Wednesday through Tuesday
  • Work Schedules are posted and copies are available no later than the Sunday before the work week is to start
  • It is the associate's responsibility to obtain a copy of the current week and upcoming week work schedule
  • Requests for specific days off must be submitted in writing to your manager a minimum of one (I) week in advance
  • Our Oil Change business can be a weather driven business and all work is done outdoors in all types of weather therefore no hours can be guaranteed
  • All associates are expected to work their scheduled hours except in cases of severe weather conditions

We do our best to communicate prior to your shift if we are changing the operating hours of the day, splitting shifts, or not requiring you to work at all. Inclement weather is to be expected throughout the spring, summer, fall and winter months of the oil change business. Associates are required to follow the company's procedure and policy when any type of inclement weather (such as rain/snow days) affects the location's opening time schedule:

  1. The management from your location will be responsible for contacting associates that are scheduled to work that day. The management will either indicate if the location is delaying the opening operation time or if the location will be closed for business that day.
  2. If you do not receive a call from your manager before the start of your shift, you are required to report to work or you must contact your manager directly to determine the business's opening time. The responsibility is then placed on the associate to contact management.
  3. If an associate does not make contact with management or decides they are not reporting to work based on the weather, the associate will be subject to disciplinary action up to and including termination. Not reporting to work a scheduled shift on an "inclement weather" day will be treated as a "no call, no show" for your shift.

Lunch Breaks: we do our best to allow associates the opportunity to eat lunch and have a break. Our guests dictate our workload so there is no guaranteed time that associates will be allotted for a scheduled lunch/break. Lunches, when given, are to be a minimum of 30 minutes off the clock. Associates are not required to be available or wait on the property when not clocked in on the company time clock when there is a delay in the opening time, inclement weather days, associate lunch/breaks or other business operating issues.

title: Operational Risk Analytics and Insights Specialist
description:
About Northern Trust


As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions.


Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide.


With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service.



About The Role:

We are seeking a Senior Risk Analytics Specialist (P4 / VP) to support the Second Line of Defense (2LOD) in the evolution of non-financial risk analytics capabilities to better identify early warning signals, connect cross-cutting risk themes, and deliver real-time insights to leadership. This role is critical to that evolution, driving the development of dynamic, near real-time analytics and translating complex risk signals into concise, decision-ready narratives for senior management.

This is not a process-oriented role. It requires a deep understanding of how the business operates, strong stakeholder engagement, and the ability to translate complex data into compelling executive narratives. The individual will play a critical role in shaping how risk is identified, understood, and managed across the organization.

Last but not least, we are a team that lives Northern Trust’s values of cherishing and nourishing our diverse and inclusive culture, and we welcome you to help us further define and grow our community.

Responsibilities

Lead Development of Risk Analytics Reporting

  • Design and deliver risk scorecard reports, providing consolidated views of operational risk and resiliency
  • Define standardized metrics across risk, controls, resiliency, and performance
  • Ensure outputs deliver clear, decision-ready insights

2. Deliver Actionable Risk Intelligence

  • Convert risk data (events, metrics, assessments, issues) into prioritized, actionable insights
  • Identify cross-cutting and systemic risk themes impacting critical business services
  • Support leadership by clearly articulating risk implications, trade-offs, and recommended actions

3. Enable Near Real-Time Risk Analytics

  • Develop dynamic dashboards and real-time analytical views aligned to leadership needs
  • Drive automation of data sourcing and refresh cycles to reduce reliance on static reporting
  • Support rapid response to emerging risks through on-demand analytics and insight generation
  • Enable earlier identification and escalation of risk signals

4. Leverage Data and AI for Advanced Insights

  • Identify and implement opportunities to use advanced analytics and AI to enhance risk insight generation
  • Apply techniques such as pattern detection, clustering, and thematic analysis across risk data sets
  • Generate forward-looking insights to anticipate emerging risks
  • Improve the speed, consistency, and quality of risk intelligence

5. Provide Executive-Level Storytelling and Engagement

  • Translate complex analytics into clear, concise narratives for senior leadership
  • Participate directly in senior forums to provide real-time risk insight and challenge
  • Anticipate leadership needs and tailor messaging accordingly
  • Ensure consistency and clarity in risk communication across deliverables

6. Partner Closely with Local Stakeholders

  • Serve as a trusted analytics advisor to senior stakeholders
  • Engage directly with local leadership and risk partners to understand business context
  • Contribute to discussions “in the room” where decisions are made
  • Build strong relationships to enhance influence and effectiveness

Skills/Experience

  • Extensive experience in risk management within a financial institution
  • Strong background in risk analytics, data analysis, or quantitative disciplines
  • Demonstrated ability to connect analytics to business and risk outcomes
  • Experience working with senior stakeholders and influencing decision-making
  • Deep understanding of operational risk and financial services environment
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
  • Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, executive-level insights
  • Excellent communication and storytelling skills
  • Proven ability to build new capabilities and innovate

Work Authorization


Applicants must have the right to work in Ireland at the time of application and for the duration of employment.


Please note that Northern Trust is unable to provide employment permit sponsorship for this role. This includes Critical Skills Employment Permits, General Employment Permits, Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permits, Stamp 1G permissions, and other employment permits under Irish immigration frameworks.


Working with Us


As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve.


Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities.


Reasonable Accommodation


Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing adjustments to individuals with health conditions and disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com, or alternatively you can discuss your individual requirements with the recruiter you are working with.

BCCD serves the communities of Barstow, Lenwood, Newberry Springs, Daggett, Yermo, Hinkley, Ludlow and Baker. The institution also maintains a satellite learning center at the U.S. Army National Training Center in Ft. Irwin, California, which serves military personnel and their families.

Barstow Community College is committed to providing an equitable, accessible, and affordable education to its diverse student body, including local, military, distance education, and historically marginalized student populations. Through a variety of high-quality and comprehensive degree, certificate, and job skills training programs, we provide holistic student support with clear and diverse educational pathways that provide students with life-long learning and networking opportunities, critical thinking skills, and success in a globalized world.

Barstow Community College serves as a hub of innovation and educational excellence, fostering a culture of growth, partnership, and inclusion as the premier college of the California High Desert.

SUMMARY

Provides assistive technology, alternate media services and auxiliary aides for students with disabilities. Performs testing, support, and accommodation activities for the ACCESS (DSPS) program under the guidance of an area administrator. Provide support to the area administrator in the hiring, selection, and training of student accommodation support staff (interpreters, note takers, readers) in order to remove barriers and ensure accommodations for students.?Provides faculty and staff with education and guidance regarding the use of various resources to accommodate students with disabilities to increase awareness of disability issues

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

- Provide a variety of specialized technical student services, testing, support, and accommodation services for participants in the ACCESS program; offer general assistance, support, and encouragement for students participating in the program. Process and confirm receipt of intake forms of students referred to the program as required by Title V and forwards to the ACCESS Counselor for appropriate accommodation.?

- Administersand monitors various tests and quizzes . Schedules students for testing in distraction reduced rooms both in ACCESS and at the TLSC.

- Arranges for and schedules program services and/or accommodations resulting from accommodation recommendations.

- Conducts presentations to students about the program and its goals and resources.

- Assists with program registration, orientations and outreach/community activities; ensures that participants have accurate information on forms; answer questions, and forward concerns with the ACCESS program to area administrator.

- Periodically requests IT for installs of new and updated software used in the high technology center. May troubleshoot basic problems with software, referring complex problems to the Management Information Systems department. Maintains inventory records for all equipment and supplies allocated to the program. Processes orders for supplies and equipment as needed.

- Provides adaptive technology in the classroom as needed. Plans, schedules, and trains students in the use of adaptive technologies, for example Smart-Pen and C-Pen., Assists students by administering tests and quizzes in Testing Room and other areas on campus as appropriate.

- Provides training fpr the face-to-face communication technical device the Ubi-Duo device in various locations on campus. Train staff and faculty on how to communicate with deaf and hard of hearing students using the Ubi-Duo.

- Coordinate and assign deaf students ASL sign language interpreters through RISE Interpreting services according to class schedule or other school events. Assist deaf students completing interpreter requests. Works with Director on renewing annual contract. Communicates with Faculty when ASL interpreters will be working in the classroom.

- Serve as web administrator for bookshare online library: qualify students for bookshare with specific disabilities such as dyslexia, blindness, cerebral palsy, and other reading barriers. Assign students user name and passwords - assign digital books to students 'from online library. Train students on the reading software features.

- Educate and train students, staff and instructors as needed on how to utilize appropriate software features such as Kurzweil3000, Caption Sync, etc.; manage a book share online library and assign digital books.

- Arrange, schedule, drive and provide shuttle services for students with mobilities disabilities to and from scheduled classes and other school events. Ensure that staff is available to assist with transport of students at designated times. Report mechanical issues to Maintenance for service.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

The position requires working knowledge of programs, resources, regulations, and laws encompassing disabled students. Requires knowledge of alternative teaching and learning methods and media for disabled students. Requires a working knowledge of assistive technology and electronic information equipment, software, and programs, including a basic knowledge of the operation, troubleshooting, and maintenance of respective equipment. Requires experience working with accessibility software. Requires experience producing information in alternate formats including but not limited to Braille, Digital Books, E-Text conversion, Closed Captioning, and Enlarged Text. Requires a basic knowledge of the use of closed caption video presentations. Requires basic knowledge of on-line program and course delivery, effective web page design, layout, and maintenance. Requires sufficient oral and written language and human relations skill to convey technical concepts to faculty and students, exercise patience, resolve confrontation, and conduct in-service training. Requires professional writing skills. Requires a working knowledge of California Community Colleges Learning and Disabilities Assessment rules, regulations, processes and procedures. Americans with Disabilities Act; Title V Regulations, Olmstead Act (2002) and Rehabilitation Act (1973). requirements, as well as the services that may be available to students from other agencies. Requires sufficient human relations skill to convey technical concepts to students, exercise patience, and make collect disability verification from secondary schools and outside agencies.

ABILITIES

Requires the ability to demonstrate sensitivity to a diverse population of individuals with disabilities. Requires the ability to carry out all aspects of the position. Must be able to maintain the learning or simulation lab and equipment in a safe and organized manner. Requires the ability to instruct students in the use of learning assistance equipment and programs. Requires the ability to perform routine record keeping and report writing duties. Must be able to organize and prioritize work and manage time effectively. Requires the maintenance of confidentiality with student records. Must be able to communicate in both formal and informal setting with students, instructors, and other interested parties. Requires the ability to learn and apply laws, rules and regulations pertaining to student access to education and information. Requires the ability to conduct in-service presentations to small groups. Requires the ability to develop layouts for printed material that complies with ADA requirements. Requires the ability to audit and prepare compliance instructions to all forms of communications for students. Requires the ability to establish and maintain productive work relationships with faculty and staff, students, and regulatory agencies. Requires the ability to use and troubleshoot computer-aided adaptive technologies, specialized audiovisual equipment and modern office-productivity computer software. Requires the ability to perform Braille translation and sign language within a reasonable time. May require the ability to perform work assignments at all College locations.

PHYSICAL ABILITIES

Requires sufficient ambulatory ability to move to various work locations. Requires manual hand-eye-arm coordination to use a personal computer keyboard and instructional media equipment. Requires special hand-arm coordination to perform sign language. Requires the ability to lift objects of medium weight (less than 40 pounds) on an occasional basis. Requires sufficient hearing and auditory ability to carry on conversations in one-on-one and small group settings and deliver in-service type training. Requires near visual acuity to read printed materials.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Work is performed indoors where some safety considerations may exist working with students having at-risk behaviors

REQUIREMENTS

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Requires the equivalent to a Bachelor's degree in secondary or special education and two years of experience working with disabled students in a one-on-one or classroom environment where computer-aided technology is used to facilitate learning. Alternatively, an Associate's degree and six years of experience may satisfy job requirements. Additional experience with alternative learning and student access may substitute for some higher education.

APPLICATION PROCEDURE

Interested applicants must submit the following to be considered:

- Completed District Application for Classified Employment (Online Application)

- Resume

- Unofficial Transcripts with Conferred Degree

- List of at least 3 references to include at least 2 supervisors (contact information only)

Application materials will be evaluated by a screening committee. Applications will be evaluated, taking into account the breadth and depth of relevant education, experience, skills, knowledge and abilities. A select group of candidates will be invited for an oral interview with the selection committee. Meeting the minimum qualifications does not assure the candidate an interview.

Please note: The district does not provide sponsorship for authorization to work in the United States. Work authorization should be established at the time of application submission.

LICENSES AND CERTIFICATES

May require a valid driver's license.

Hours

This position primarily location at Main Campus 2700 Barstow Road, Barstow Ca 92311.

Normal Hours: Mon - Thru: 8:00 am to 6:00 pm; Fri: 8:00 am - 12:00 pm .

Summer Hours: Mon- Thurs 7:00am- 6:00pm Friday's off

Barstow Community College District is committed to hiring a staff that is sensitive to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural and ethnic backgrounds of community college students. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, creed, color, national origin, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, religion, disability, political affiliation, age, or veteran status.

title: People & Culture Coordinator
description:

Who you are

title: Systems Analyst/Programmer
description:

To view the detailed position description for Systems Analyst/Programmer, click here.

title: Specialist - Information Technology
description:
The Specialist - Information Technology delivers advanced technical support, field engineering, and systems maintenance, focusing primarily on school districts within the Region 3 service area. This position requires frequent travel utilizing fleet vehicles to local school campuses to deploy, troubleshoot, and optimize computer systems and localized network infrastructures. Additionally, the Specialist provides secondary technical support for the internal operations of the Education Service Center.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent blend of education and hands-on experience).
  • 3–5 years of progressive experience in IT technical support, field services, or network administration.
  • Relevant certifications preferred: CompTIA Network+/Security+, CCNA, Palo Alto PCNSA, Aruba ACMA, or Microsoft/Google certifications.
  • Frequent travel within the Region 3 area is required. Must possess a valid driver's license and an acceptable driving record to operate Education Service Center fleet vehicles.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Advanced troubleshooting of computer systems (Windows, Google and Mac platforms), mobile devices, and peripherals in a school environment.
  • Practical proficiency with network switches, port configurations, VLAN routing, and basic DHCP/DNS administration.
  • Experience deploying, configuring, and optimizing wireless access points (Aruba, Ubiquiti, or Meraki) across school campus environments.
  • Basic administrative familiarity with firewall configurations, secure remote access, and Zero Trust frameworks.
  • Strong troubleshooting and root-cause analysis abilities with attention to detail.
  • Skilled in documenting configurations, diagrams, and standard operating procedures.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across IT and school district admin teams.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Primary Focus – On-Site School Support: Travel to regional school districts to provide Tier 2/3 hands-on troubleshooting, diagnostics, and resolution for complex hardware, software, and localized network issues.
  • Secondary Focus – Internal ESC Support: Assist with the technical maintenance, help desk escalation, and infrastructure support of the internal Education Service Center operations as needed.
  • Configure, deploy, and maintain campus network switches, manage localized VLAN traffic, and resolve device-level connectivity issues.
  • Install, configure, and monitor school-wide wireless networks to ensure seamless, high-density connectivity for classroom devices.
  • Assist with the setup of WAN links, localized server hardware, and peripheral systems like VoIP or classroom smart tech.
  • Document network configurations, diagrams, and standard operating procedures.
  • Comply with federal and state laws, State Board of Education Rules, and ESC board policy and procedures.

All positions at ESC 3 are defined as security-sensitive. Security-sensitive positions are those which require employees to be
entrusted with the certain types of data, whether electronic or in paper form. Those data elements, as defined by the ESC 3 Data
Classification and Handling Policy may include, but not limited to:

  • Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
  • Personally, Identifiable Information (PII)
  • Protected Health Information (PHI)
  • Family Educational Records (FERPA Data)
  • Federal Tax Information (FTI)

  • HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability Accountability Act)


It is the employees on-going responsibility to safeguard this type of data and to report any instance of lost or stolen data.

title: Director, Technical Program Management, Equipment Supply Chain
description:
Behind everything our users see online is the architecture built by the AI2 team to keep it running. Within AI2, the Equipment Supply Chain (ESC) Planning organization transforms phase-level demand signals into high-accuracy equipment supply plans. We leverage Integrated Business Planning and financial stewardship to proactively mitigate capital expenditure and supply constraints, reliably meeting our customers' evolving capacity needs and supporting Google's accelerated global growth.

As Director of ESC Planning, you will be a visionary leader and be responsible for directing a portfolio of strategic, complex programs that accelerate the business impact of Google's global infrastructure. You will lead the organization through a pivot, moving from establishing basic visibility to dynamic transformation and outcome-driven execution. You will manage a high-performing team across Demand Planning, Supply Planning (e.g., Mechanical and Electrical), Capital Expenditure/Operational Expenditure Management, and Integrated Business Planning. This role exhibits positive influence and technical leadership, prioritizing a user-centered development process to increase product utility and user satisfaction.

Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $281000 - $391000 (USD) + 30% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.
  • Transition to a full Integrated Business Planning model. Decouple supply from demand to drive Build-to-Stock (BTS), Build-to-Order (BTO), and Configure-to-Order (CTO) strategies. Enable "Available to Promise" (ATP) capabilities through aggregate supply positioning and allocation.
  • Implement advanced methodologies to increase forecast precision and reduce cycle times.
  • Optimize capital expenditure and operational expenditure flow by implementing hybrid funding models and site-agnostic procurement to remove funding releases from the critical path.
  • Establish safety stock and cycle stock buffer models. Scale Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimization (MEIO) across all tiers to protect SLAs while increasing Inventory Turns and reducing carrying costs.
  • Partner with ELS, ESC Operations and Delivery, Finance, and Engineering, and publish a Single Source of Truth (SSOT) for global supply plan.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business Administration, or equivalent practical experience
  • 15 years of experience in supply chain, technical infrastructure, or mission-critical environments.

Preferred qualifications:

  • MBA or Master’s degree in a technical or business field.
  • Experience managing multi-billion dollar asset portfolios and multi-tier global supply chains (e.g., Tier 1 integrators and Tier 2 suppliers).
  • Experience with Advanced Planning Systems (e.g., Kinaxis, SAP) and advocating for AI/ML best practices to unlock process efficiency and scale.

title: Security Infrastructure Engineer
description:
DATE: Feb 10, 2026

POSITION: Security Infrastructure Engineer

LOCATION: Technology - District Technology Office

REPORTS TO: Executive Director of Technology

SALARY: Pay Grade 82

TERM OF EMPLOYMENT: 12 months

Effective: 5/1/2026



Position Summary

The Information Security Specialist is responsible for safeguarding the district’s technology infrastructure, data, and systems by developing, implementing, and maintaining security policies, tools, and best practices. This position monitors for threats, responds to incidents, ensures compliance with state and federal regulations, and supports secure technology operations across all K–12 schools within the district. The role requires strong technical expertise, excellent communication skills, and a deep understanding of cybersecurity challenges in public education.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Cybersecurity Operations

  • Monitor district networks, servers, cloud platforms, and endpoints for security alerts, anomalies, and indicators of compromise.
  • Analyze logs, conduct threat assessments, and manage alerts from SIEM, firewall, endpoint protection, and email security systems.
  • Lead or assist with investigations, containment, remediation, and recovery of security incidents.
  • Maintain and tune security tools such as firewalls, DNS filtering, endpoint protection, vulnerability scanners, and identity security tools.

Identity & Access Management

  • Manage secure user access practices across Active Directory, Azure/Entra ID, Google Workspace for Education, and district applications.
  • Enforce MFA, password policies, and least-privilege access.
  • Conduct regular access reviews and support account lifecycle processes.

Compliance & Risk Management

  • Ensure district compliance with NC DPI requirements, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, CIS Controls, FERPA, CIPA, and other applicable regulations.
  • Conduct annual risk assessments and participate in external audits.
  • Maintain documentation for policies, procedures, recovery plans, and incident response.

Security Awareness & Training

  • Develop and deliver cybersecurity awareness training for staff, including phishing simulations and safe computing practices.
  • Provide guidance to school administrators, technology facilitators, and support staff on secure use of district technology resources.

Systems & Network Security

  • Assist in hardening servers, switches, wireless systems, cloud resources, and network infrastructure.
  • Support secure configuration and patch management across district devices.
  • Review and validate vendor security controls for third-party applications and integrations.

Disaster Recovery & Business Continuity

  • Maintain and test data backup systems, restoration procedures, and disaster recovery plans.
  • Participate in district continuity planning for critical technology services.

All other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

  • Associate or Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or related field (or equivalent experience).
